firmwares.firmwareDescription: {"format":"markdown","content":"# Pitaox PaperMono Mesh - [English](#english) - [中文](#中文) --- ## English ### 1. Before you begin Pitaox PaperMono Mesh is designed for the full PaperMono model with LoRa hardware. Charge the device, insert a microSD/TF card if you plan to read books, then power it on. The e-paper panel is intentionally different from a phone display. A brief flash or a slightly slower update can be normal, especially after several rapid UI changes. ### 2. Home screen and navigation The Launcher is the home screen. Its bottom navigation bar provides four main destinations: | Label | Function | | --- | --- | | `READ` | Open the current book in the Reader. | | `LIB` | Browse books and folders on the TF card. | | `MESH` | Open LoRa Mesh, messages, nodes, and radio settings. | | `SET` | Open device settings. | To return from Library, Reader, Settings, or Mesh, swipe upward from the bottom edge of the screen. This bottom-edge gesture is the normal Back action. ### 3. Reading books 1. Copy EPUB files to a FAT-compatible microSD/TF card. 2. Safely eject the card from the computer and insert it into PaperMono. 3. Tap `LIB` on the Launcher. 4. Tap a folder to enter it, or tap an EPUB file to open it. #### Reader gestures | Action | Result | | --- | --- | | Tap the left side of a page | Previous page. | | Tap the right side of a page | Next page. | | Tap the center | Open reading settings. | | Swipe downward from the top edge | Open the front-light panel. | | Tap the bookmark control | Add or remove a bookmark for the current page. | | Swipe upward from the bottom edge | Return to Library. | The reading settings panel provides text size, line spacing, chapters, and bookmarks. The first time a TF card is used, PaperMono may install its bundled Chinese fonts; leave the card inserted until startup finishes. ### 4. Device settings Open `SET` from the Launcher. #### Brightness Drag the brightness slider, or use `-` and `+` for 10% steps. The percentage shown on the right is the saved value. #### Sound Tap the `SOUND` row or its switch to turn the global sound preference on or off. This affects local audible notifications; Mesh notification behavior is separately selected in Mesh settings. #### Firmware version The `FIRMWARE` row shows the installed Build ID in `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS` form. It is useful when reporting an issue or confirming that a newly built image was flashed. ### 5. Mesh basics Open `MESH` from the Launcher. The Mesh page has its own bottom navigation: | Label | Function | | --- | --- | | `OVR` | Overview of the local node, radio, and device statistics. | | `INBOX` | Conversation list and message composer. | | `NODES` | Known nodes and direct-message entry point. | | `SET` | Radio, alert, indicator, and stored-data settings. | #### Select a radio region Before using LoRa, open `OVR` and tap the status area to select the applicable regional configuration. Use only a radio region and transmit settings that are legal for your location. #### Connect the Meshtastic mobile app 1. Enable Bluetooth on the phone. 2. Open the Meshtastic app and select the PaperMono device. 3. Complete the pairing flow. If PaperMono shows a pairing code, enter or confirm that code in the app. 4. Keep the app open until the initial configuration and node data have synchronized. The device keeps the Mesh service active according to its Mesh background setting. Bluetooth, phone synchronization, and radio activity can take a moment after startup or reconnection. ### 6. Messages and conversations 1. Tap `INBOX`. 2. Tap a conversation to open it. 3. Tap `TAP TO WRITE A MESSAGE` to open the on-screen composer. 4. Enter text and send it. Use the `INBOX` button in the bottom Mesh navigation to return from an open conversation to the conversation list. An unread badge may appear below the `INBOX` label. Delivery state is shown for locally sent messages; `SENT` only means the local radio accepted the transmission, while delivery confirmation can later change the state to `DELIVERED` or `FAILED`. ### 7. Nodes and direct messages Tap `NODES` to view discovered nodes. The heading includes total, online, and offline counts. Tap a remote node row to open a direct-message composer for that node. Node discovery and message delivery depend on the radio region, modem preset, channel configuration, antenna, distance, and other Mesh nodes. A node listed on screen is not a guarantee of immediate end-to-end delivery. ### 8. Mesh settings Open `MESH` > `SET`. Tapping a row changes or opens its setting. | Setting | Use | | --- | --- | | `MESH BACKGROUND` | Keep Mesh runtime servicing while you use other PaperMono apps. | | `MODEM PRESET` | Cycle the LoRa modem preset. Use a preset compatible with the intended mesh. | | `HOP LIMIT` | Cycle the maximum routing hop limit. | | `TX POWER` | Cycle transmit-power settings. Follow local radio rules. | | `MESSAGE ALERTS` | Cycle message alerts through off, sound, light, and both. | | `LIGHT STYLE` | Choose the supported unread-message light reminder style. | | `DATA & HISTORY` | Review and clear stored messages and/or node cache. | `DATA & HISTORY` is destructive. Clearing the node cache also removes stored node names and direct-message public-key information, so direct-message key synchronization must happen again. ### 9. Power off Double-press the side power button to start the controlled shutdown sequence. Wait until the shutdown screen has completed before disconnecting power or storing the device. A short single press may only acknowledge through the power-management hardware and is not the normal software shutdown action. ### 10. E-paper care - Keep the panel away from direct sunlight, high temperatures, and strong UV. - Do not deliberately perform continuous rapid UI actions for long periods. - The firmware merges rapid updates in the same area and performs a cleanup refresh after a limited number of fast updates, but these are safeguards rather than a substitute for careful use. - If a persistent ghost image remains after normal use, allow the interface to perform its next full refresh; avoid repeatedly forcing rapid changes. ### 11. Troubleshooting | Symptom | What to try | | --- | --- | | A new book is not visible | Confirm the TF card is inserted, the file is EPUB, and reopen `LIB`. | | Mesh has no activity | Confirm the correct regional setting, matching channel/modem settings, antenna connection, and another reachable node. | | Phone does not connect | Toggle the phone's Bluetooth, reconnect from the Meshtastic app, and complete any displayed pairing-code flow. | | Direct messages fail after clearing data | Let node information synchronize again; node-cache clearing removes stored DM key material. | | Screen has visible ghosting | Stop rapid interaction and allow a full refresh; keep the panel away from heat and direct sun. | For a firmware issue report, include the Build ID from `SET` > `FIRMWARE`, the exact device model, and relevant serial logs. --- ## 中文 ### 1. 使用前准备 Pitaox PaperMono Mesh 面向带 LoRa 硬件的完整版 PaperMono。使用前请为设备充电；如需阅读书籍，请插入 microSD/TF 卡，然后开机。 墨水屏的工作方式与手机屏幕不同。短暂闪烁或在连续操作后更新稍慢属于正常现象。 ### 2. 主界面与导航 启动器（Launcher）是主界面，底部导航栏提供四个主要入口： | 标签 | 功能 | | --- | --- | | `READ` | 在阅读器中打开当前书籍。 | | `LIB` | 浏览 TF 卡上的书籍和文件夹。 | | `MESH` | 打开 LoRa Mesh、消息、节点和无线电设置。 | | `SET` | 打开设备设置。 | 在图书馆、阅读器、设置或 Mesh 页面中，如需返回，请从屏幕底部边缘向上滑动。这是标准的返回手势。 ### 3. 阅读书籍 1. 将 EPUB 文件复制到 FAT 兼容的 microSD/TF 卡中。 2. 在电脑上安全弹出 TF 卡，再将其插入 PaperMono。 3. 在启动器中点击 `LIB`。 4. 点击文件夹进入，或点击 EPUB 文件开始阅读。 #### 阅读器手势 | 操作 | 结果 | | --- | --- | | 点击页面左侧 | 上一页。 | | 点击页面右侧 | 下一页。 | | 点击页面中间 | 打开阅读设置。 | | 从屏幕顶部边缘向下滑动 | 打开前光面板。 | | 点击书签控件 | 添加或移除当前页书签。 | | 从屏幕底部边缘向上滑动 | 返回图书馆。 | 阅读设置面板可调整字号、行距，并打开目录和书签列表。首次使用 TF 卡时，PaperMono 可能会安装内置中文字体；请在启动完成前保持 TF 卡插入。 ### 4. 设备设置 在启动器中点击 `SET`。 #### 亮度 拖动亮度滑块，或点击 `-`、`+` 按钮以 10% 为单位调整。右侧显示的百分比为已保存的亮度值。 #### 声音 点击 `SOUND` 行或右侧开关，即可开启或关闭全局声音偏好。它影响本机的声音提醒；Mesh 消息提醒方式需在 Mesh 设置中单独选择。 #### 固件版本 `FIRMWARE` 行显示当前安装固件的 `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS` Build ID。反馈问题或确认新固件是否已烧录时，请提供这一编号。 ### 5. Mesh 基本使用 在启动器中点击 `MESH`。Mesh 页面拥有独立的底部导航： | 标签 | 功能 | | --- | --- | | `OVR` | 本机节点、无线电和设备指标概览。 | | `INBOX` | 会话列表和消息编辑器。 | | `NODES` | 已知节点及私信入口。 | | `SET` | 无线电、提醒、指示灯和本地数据设置。 | #### 选择无线电区域 使用 LoRa 前，请进入 `OVR` 并点击状态区域，选择适用的区域配置。只能使用所在地允许的无线电区域和发射参数。 #### 连接 Meshtastic 手机 App 1. 打开手机蓝牙。 2. 在 Meshtastic App 中选择 PaperMono 设备。 3. 按 App 的步骤完成配对。如 PaperMono 显示配对码，请在 App 中输入或确认该代码。 4. 保持 App 打开，直到首次配置和节点数据同步完成。 设备会依据 Mesh 后台运行设置持续服务 Mesh。开机或重连后，蓝牙、手机同步和无线电活动可能需要短暂时间恢复。 ### 6. 消息与会话 1. 点击 `INBOX`。 2. 点击一个会话进入对话页。 3. 点击 `TAP TO WRITE A MESSAGE` 打开屏幕键盘。 4. 输入文本后发送。 在会话页面中，点击底部 Mesh 导航中的 `INBOX` 即可返回会话列表。`INBOX` 标签下方可能显示未读徽标。本机发送消息会显示投递状态：`SENT` 仅代表本机无线电已接受发送；后续确认可能将状态更新为 `DELIVERED` 或 `FAILED`。 ### 7. 节点与私信 点击 `NODES` 查看已发现节点。标题区域会显示总数、在线和离线统计。点击远程节点行可打开该节点的私信编辑器。 节点发现和消息投递取决于区域设置、调制解调器预设、信道配置、天线、距离及中间 Mesh 节点。屏幕上已显示某节点，并不代表一定可以立即完成端到端投递。 ### 8. Mesh 设置 进入 `MESH` > `SET`。点击对应项目可切换或打开设置。 | 设置 | 用途 | | --- | --- | | `MESH BACKGROUND` | 使用其他 PaperMono 应用时，是否继续服务 Mesh 运行时。 | | `MODEM PRESET` | 切换 LoRa 调制解调器预设；需与目标 Mesh 兼容。 | | `HOP LIMIT` | 切换最大路由跳数。 | | `TX POWER` | 切换发射功率设置；请遵守当地无线电规定。 | | `MESSAGE ALERTS` | 在关闭、声音、灯光、声音+灯光之间切换消息提醒。 | | `LIGHT STYLE` | 选择设备支持的未读消息灯光提醒样式。 | | `DATA & HISTORY` | 查看并清理保存的消息和/或节点缓存。 | `DATA & HISTORY` 中的清理操作不可撤销。清除节点缓存会同时移除保存的节点名称和私信公钥信息，之后需要重新同步私信密钥。 ### 9. 关机 双击侧边电源键会启动受控关机流程。请等待关机画面完成后，再断开电源或收纳设备。短按一次可能只会被电源管理硬件响应，并不是正常的软件关机操作。 ### 10. 墨水屏使用注意事项 - 避免阳光直射、高温和强紫外线。 - 不要长时间持续进行高频界面操作。 - 固件会合并同一区域的快速刷新，并在达到一定次数后执行清理刷新；这些是保护措施，不能替代谨慎使用。 - 正常使用后若出现持续残影，请等待界面进行下一次全屏刷新；避免反复强制快速变化。 ### 11. 常见问题 | 现象 | 可尝试的处理方式 | | --- | --- | | 新书未显示 | 确认 TF 卡已插入、文件为 EPUB，然后重新打开 `LIB`。 | | Mesh 没有活动 | 确认区域设置正确、信道/调制设置匹配、天线连接正常，并且附近有可达节点。 | | 手机无法连接 | 关闭再打开手机蓝牙，在 Meshtastic App 中重新连接，并完成设备显示的配对码流程。 | | 清理数据后私信失败 | 等待节点信息重新同步；清理节点缓存会移除已保存的私信密钥材料。 | | 屏幕有明显残影 | 停止快速操作并等待全屏刷新，同时避免高温和阳光直射。 | 如需反馈固件问题，请提供 `SET` > `FIRMWARE` 中的 Build ID、具体设备型号以及相关串口日志。"}

{"format":"markdown","content":"## changes

Fixed the crash that occurred when opening large EPUB files due to std::string reallocation. The reader now estimates the required text capacity before loading chapters and checks available contiguous PSRAM. If memory is insufficient, it shows an error instead of rebooting. EPUB loading and memory usage were also optimized to reduce peak consumption.

Additionally, corrected the overly conservative Chinese text pagination width. The 12/14/16 pt font measurements now match the actual glyph widths, reducing premature line breaks by approximately 2–3 Chinese characters on the right side and improving Chinese text, mixed Chinese-English content, and punctuation layout.

---
修复阅读器打开较大 EPUB 文件时因 std::string 扩容导致系统崩溃的问题。现在会在加载章节前预估正文容量，结合 PSRAM 可用连续空间进行安全检查，内存不足时显示错误提示，不再触发系统重启。同时优化 EPUB 正文的章节加载和内存使用方式，降低加载过程中的峰值占用。

另外，修正阅读器中文正文分页宽度过于保守的问题，使 12/14/16 pt 字体的分页测量与实际字形宽度一致，减少右侧提前约 2–3 个汉字换行的现象，改善中文正文、中英文混排及标点排版效果。"}

{"format":"html","content":"

The Invalid image block, can't boot issue was not caused by corruption of the application firmware image itself. It resulted from a difference between the development validation environment and the public flashing environment.

During development, firmware is flashed with idf.py flash or the VS Code ESP-IDF extension. These tools automatically write the bootloader, partition table, and application image using the correct offsets, so this issue does not occur during development validation.

For public distribution, however, Pitaox-PaperMono-Mesh.bin is an application-only image and must be flashed at 0x10000. Some generic flashing tools write a selected file at the default offset 0x0, causing the ESP32-S3 ROM to interpret the application image as a bootloader and report Invalid image block, can't boot.

The firmware release process has now been improved. Future firmware releases include Pitaox-PaperMono-Mesh-full.bin, a complete image containing the bootloader, partition table, and application firmware. It is designed for generic flash tools using the default 0x0 offset. 

-----------

Added

  • Settings now opens an offline bilingual USER GUIDE. Its final WHAT'S NEW chapter is generated at build time from this current changelog and carries the same timestamp Build ID as the firmware.
  • Launcher Settings now provides confirmed RESTART and SHUTDOWN controls. Both save the Mesh snapshot before the transition; shutdown reuses the display-retention deep-sleep path.
  • The Launcher now includes ANS, an offline Answer Book. It embeds the supplied 1,100-answer dataset and a purpose-built 22 pt CJK subset font, so drawing an answer does not require a TF card or network connection. Each reveal uses a brief asynchronous fixed-pitch E5-G5-C6 arpeggio when global SOUND is enabled.
  • An on-screen Pinyin input mode. Switch between CN and ABC from the keyboard mode key, type a Pinyin syllable, page through candidates with < and >, and tap a candidate or press Space to commit the first one.
  • A compact embedded Pinyin candidate table adapted from zh_pinyin_decoder, including its license notice and attribution.
  • Upstream-compatible Meshtastic monochrome emoji rendering in Mesh text. Supported emoji render as 1-bit icons and accept common variation-selector and skin-tone modifiers where the upstream matcher does.

Changed

  • Keyboard UTF-8 editing now deletes a complete code point, so one delete removes one Chinese character rather than corrupting or requiring multiple deletes. Mixed Latin/CJK input uses matching measurement and drawing paths, and the input cursor remains visible after redraws.
  • Pinyin candidates now follow the table's preferred order, placing common candidates on the first page instead of reversing the list.
  • Emoji vertical placement is adjusted to align with the surrounding CJK text baseline.
  • Project licensing changed to GPL-3.0-or-later to match the incorporated GPLv3 Meshtastic emoji renderer/assets. README and User Guide licensing and emoji documentation were updated accordingly.

Reader and EPUB improvements

  • EPUB loading no longer performs a separate metadata pass before loading the book text. It avoids repeated central-directory/package parsing, reduces temporary chapter-title processing, and collapses excessive blank lines in one linear pass.
  • EPUB load logs now report entry/chapter count, text size, read activity, and elapsed time for device-side performance diagnosis.
  • Pagination no longer pre-scans every glyph in a complete book. It proceeds incrementally with a bounded background time budget, reducing TF-card I/O, startup delay, and watchdog pressure on large EPUB files.
  • Reader navigation delays position persistence briefly after page turns, avoiding repeated TF-card writes during rapid paging while still saving on close or after the user pauses.
  • CJK pagination now uses a conservative size-specific grid with right-bearing allowance. This prevents Chinese punctuation at a line end from extending beyond the visible text area.
  • First-time bundled CJK-font installation shows an explicit reader loading state rather than appearing as a stalled book open.

Launcher refinements

  • The former READ navigation item is now ANS for the Answer Book. The existing CONTINUE card remains the direct Reader entry point.
  • The CONTINUE book title uses the bundled CJK font renderer and safely truncates by pixel width at UTF-8 character boundaries, so Chinese titles display correctly without broken trailing bytes.
  • The battery progress bar derives its left edge from the rendered percentage width and preserves a readable gap after 100%.


经排查，之前出现的 Invalid image block, can't boot 并非固件应用镜像本身损坏，而是开发验证环境与对外烧录环境存在差异。

开发阶段使用 ESP-IDF 的 idf.py flash 或 VS Code ESP-IDF 插件烧录。该方式会自动按构建配置写入 bootloader、分区表和应用镜像，并使用正确偏移，因此开发验证中不会出现此问题。

但对外发布时，若仅使用 Pitaox-PaperMono-Mesh.bin，它实际上是应用镜像，正确烧录偏移应为 0x10000。部分通用烧录工具默认从 0x0 写入，导致 ESP32-S3 ROM 将应用镜像误当作 bootloader 解析，最终报出 Invalid image block, can't boot。

现已改进固件发布方式：后续固件将提供 Pitaox-PaperMono-Mesh-full.bin 完整镜像，已合并 bootloader、分区表和应用固件，适配通用烧录工具的 0x0 默认烧录方式。

-----------

新增

  • Settings 新增离线双语 USER GUIDE。末尾的“本版本更新”会在构建时根据当前更新日志生成，并使用与固件一致的时间戳 Build ID。
  • Launcher Settings 新增需确认的 RESTART 与 SHUTDOWN 控件。两者都会先保存 Mesh 快照；关机复用保屏深度休眠路径。
  • 启动器新增 ANS 离线答案之书：内嵌提供的 1,100 条答案数据及专用 22 pt CJK 子集字体，抽取答案不依赖 TF 卡或网络连接；全局 SOUND 开启时，每次揭晓会播放简短的异步 E5-G5-C6 固定音高琶音。
  • 屏幕键盘新增拼音输入模式：通过键盘模式键在 CN 与 ABC 间切换；输入拼音后可用 <、> 翻页候选词，点击候选词或按空格提交首个候选词。
  • 新增基于 zh_pinyin_decoder 适配的紧凑拼音候选表，并保留其许可证和署名。
  • Mesh 文本新增与上游 Meshtastic 行为兼容的单色 emoji 渲染。已支持的 emoji 将以 1-bit 图标显示；匹配逻辑兼容上游所支持的常见变体选择符和肤色修饰符。

调整

  • 键盘的 UTF-8 删除改为一次删除完整字符。删除一个中文字符不再破坏文本，也不再需要多次按删除键。中英文混合输入使用一致的测量与绘制路径，刷新后输入光标仍会显示。
  • 拼音候选词改为表中的优先顺序，常用候选词会优先出现在第一页，不再出现候选列表反序。
  • 调整 emoji 的垂直位置，使其与周围中文文本的基线更协调。
  • 项目许可证改为 GPL-3.0-or-later，以与引入的 GPLv3 Meshtastic emoji 渲染器/资源保持一致；README 和用户手册也同步更新了许可证与 emoji 说明。

阅读器与 EPUB 改进

  • EPUB 加载不再在加载正文前单独进行一次元数据遍历，避免重复解析中央目录与包文件；章节标题处理减少临时副本，并以线性方式合并连续空行。
  • EPUB 加载日志新增条目数、章节数、文本大小、读取活动和耗时，便于在真机上分析性能。
  • 分页不再预扫描整本书的所有字形，而是采用增量分页与受时间预算限制的后台处理，降低大 EPUB 的 TF 卡 I/O、打开延迟和看门狗压力。
  • 快速翻页时延迟保存阅读位置，减少连续 TF 卡写入；关闭阅读器或用户停止翻页后仍会保存位置。
  • 中文分页按字号采用更保守的网格宽度，并为右侧字形承载预留空间，避免行尾中文标点溢出可视区域。
  • 首次安装内置中文字体时，阅读器会显示明确的加载状态，不再看起来像打开书籍时卡住。

Launcher 优化

  • 原 READ 导航项改为答案之书的 ANS；原有 CONTINUE 卡片保留为直接进入阅读器的入口。
  • CONTINUE 下方的书名改为使用内置 CJK 字体渲染，并按像素宽度、UTF-8 字符边界安全截断，中文书名可正确显示，也不会出现截断到半个字节的情况。
  • 电池进度条左侧会根据百分比文字的实际宽度计算；100% 后保留清晰间距。
"}

{"format":"markdown","content":"# Tetris for M5Stack Faces Gamepad3

## 简介

为 M5Stack CoreS3 系列设备设计的轻量级俄罗斯方块游戏，基于 ESP-IDF 和 GameLib 开发，需要搭配 Faces Bottom3 与 Faces Gamepad3 使用。

### 游戏特点

- 经典 10 × 20 方块矩阵
- 7 种标准方块
- 方块旋转与墙边修正
- 幽灵方块预览
- Hold 暂存功能
- 连续消行和等级系统
- 最高分记录
- 暂停、继续和重新开始
- 适配 Faces Bottom3 与 Faces Gamepad3

### 操作方式

- 左键 / 右键：移动方块
- 下键：速下降
- 上键：直接落到底部
- A 键：顺时针旋转
- B 键：逆时针旋转
- START：暂存当前方块
- SELECT：暂停游戏
- 暂停时按上键 / 下键：选择继续或重新开始
- 暂停界面按 B：确认选择
- 暂停时按 SELECT：继续游戏
- 游戏结束时按 B：重新开始

### 硬件要求

- M5Stack CoreS3 或 CoreS3-Lite
- Faces Bottom3
- Faces Gamepad3

---

## Description

A lightweight Tetris game designed for the M5Stack CoreS3 series. Built with ESP-IDF and GameLib, it requires the Faces Bottom3 and Faces Gamepad3 accessories.

### Features

- Classic 10 × 20 playfield
- Seven standard tetrominoes
- Piece rotation with wall-kick support
- Ghost piece preview
- Hold piece functionality
- Line clearing and level progression
- High score tracking
- Pause, resume, and restart options
- Designed for Faces Bottom3 and Faces Gamepad3

### Controls

- Left / Right: Move the current piece
- Down: Soft drop
- Up: Hard drop
- A: Rotate clockwise
- B: Rotate counterclockwise
- START: Hold the current piece
- SELECT: Pause the game
- Up / Down while paused: Select Resume or Restart
- B in the pause menu: Confirm the selection
- SELECT while paused: Resume the game
- B on the Game Over screen: Restart the game

### Hardware Requirements

- M5Stack CoreS3 or CoreS3-Lite
- Faces Bottom3
- Faces Gamepad3"}

{"format":"markdown","content":"A little internet radio for your M5Stack StickS3. Tune into live stations, choose your favorites from ten curated options, and shake the radio to change its monochrome color.

Six stations are selected to start: Tiki Time, Illinois Street Lounge, KEXP, NTS 1, KCRW Eclectic 24 and Radio Paradise. Add Bossa Beyond, Secret Agent, Suburbs of Goa or Heavyweight Reggae from the setup page.

## First-time setup
1. Join the PocketRadio Wi-Fi network shown on the radio using its displayed password.
2. Open http://192.168.4.1/ on your phone if the setup page does not appear automatically.
3. Choose your 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi, enter its password, and tap Connect & play.

The radio remembers your network. No phone app, account or code editing is required.

## Controls
- A tap: next station. A hold: stop/resume.
- B tap: volume up. B hold: volume down.
- Shake: change color.
- Hold A+B for 1.5 seconds: Wi-Fi and station setup.
- Double-click the separate side power/reset button: power off. Single-click: power on/reset. Long press: upload mode.

To change your dial, select stations and tap Save stations, then Return to radio. Keep at least one selected.

## Notes
StickS3 only. Built-in speaker; Bluetooth speaker audio is not supported. Requires ordinary 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi with internet access. Hotel sign-in pages and enterprise Wi-Fi are unsupported. Battery percentage is approximate; volume is limited for battery stability. Station availability depends on broadcasters. Network stalls can briefly delay controls. Custom stream URLs and track titles are not supported.

The audio adapter is based on M5Stack's web-radio example. Streams connect directly to broadcasters; support the stations you enjoy."}

firmwares.firmwareDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"# MonoMesh

**Standalone Meshtastic client for the M5Stack Paper Mono** — chat, node list and
offline maps directly on the e-paper device, with no phone, no Bluetooth and no
Wi-Fi required.

[![CI](https://github.com/andrecolz/MonoMesh/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/andrecolz/MonoMesh/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

Current release: **v1.0b (beta)**

## What it can do

- **Mesh messaging** — broadcast channels and end-to-end encrypted direct
  messages (X25519 + AES-256-CCM, Meshtastic 2.5+ PKI), ACK/NAK, retries and
  managed-flooding relay, with unread badges and message history on screen.
- **Node list** — name, model, MAC, PKI lock, RSSI/SNR and hop count; telemetry
  (device, environment, air quality), traceroute, waypoints received and
  NeighborInfo transmitted.
- **Offline maps** — a single `.mmap` container per region (recommended) or a
  PNG tile tree on MicroSD; pan, zoom, node pins, waypoints and "go to my
  position".
- **Touch keyboard** — compose messages with uppercase/symbols and a scrolling
  text field; quick menu and physical buttons for page navigation.
- **On-screen settings** — region, modem preset, frequency, TX power, hop
  limit, channel name and PSK, node identity and role, broadcast intervals,
  TX duty-cycle budget, rebroadcast mode, buzzer mode, timezone/RTC, clock
  orientation and storage info.
- **Power modes** — power off, standby with the radio always listening, giant
  clock, clock + RX; battery protection and configurable power-button action.
- **Works without MicroSD** — settings, keys and recent messages persist in
  NVS; the card adds full chat history, node database and maps.

## Offline maps

The tools generate tiles from a local `.osm.pbf` file (for example from
[Geofabrik](https://download.geofabrik.de/)), completely offline and without API
keys:

```bash
# one-time
python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt

# one .mmap container for the area around a point (recommended)
python3 tools/mmap_converter.py --tui

Copy the resulting `.mmap` file into `/maps` on the MicroSD.

## License and attribution

GNU General Public License v3.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

MonoMesh is an independent implementation interoperable with the
[Meshtastic](https://meshtastic.org/) wire protocol; "Meshtastic" is a trademark
of Meshtastic LLC and this project is neither affiliated with nor endorsed by
Meshtastic LLC. Map data derives from **© OpenStreetMap contributors** (ODbL) and
the tiles must be attributed accordingly. Third-party components (map style,
clock font) are listed in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)."}

{"format":"markdown","content":"**Important note - don't unpair your stock Stackchan image, otherwise you won't be able to pair this. If you do accidentally unpair, flash it again from [StackChan-UserDemo](https://burner.m5stack.com/7B4CRJ), pair via StackChan World, then flash this custom firmware directly.**

I made a fork of the official StackChan firmware that others may be interested in, either to build upon or to use.

It's not groundbreaking. Rather, it addresses a few quality-of-life things that annoyed me in the week I've had this little guy.

I have no interest in dance or avatar settings, so these tweaks are for StackChan used as an AI assistant.

Caveat: I am a software engineer by day, but sometimes it's nice to just yell at AI and get it to do your bidding. I haven't spent time learning the innards of the StackChan firmware or hardware - these tweaks were entirely created by Opus 5 and, apart from quick sense-checking, haven't been fully vetted."}

{"format":"markdown","content":"Rill Mallet is an instrument in the Rill family for M5Stack StickS3. Seven multisampled instruments (balafon, glockenspiel, kalimba, marimba, piano, vibraphone and xylophone) play evolving melodies with eight visuals: Ring, Snap, Bloom, Ripple, Asanoha, Uroko, Kikko and Moons. Sound and visuals run entirely on the device, without an internet connection or account.

[Play in your browser at Rill Sound](https://rillsound.com/mallet).

### Controls
- Tap the front button for a new piece and visual.
- Hold the front button for about 0.65 seconds to fade sound out or in.
- Tap the side button to cycle volume and show information.
- Hold the side button to slow the ensemble by 4 BPM; below 52 BPM it wraps to 100.
- Shake for a different visual without changing the music.

### Ensemble
Current firmware joins nearby Rill Voice, Synth, Mallet, World and Drums devices over ESP-NOW without setup, sharing tempo and bar lines. New music enters on a shared downbeat. Voice, Synth and Mallet can propose the shared key.

### Installation
StickS3 only, using its built-in speaker. Installing the factory image replaces the current firmware and settings.

[Source, build instructions and credits](https://github.com/bruceblay/rill-mallet). GPL-3.0-or-later; samples and dependencies retain their own licenses."}

firmwares.firmwareDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"Fox Hunt for M5StickS3

Active hide-and-seek game for two M5StickS3 devices. One player hides as the Fox, and the other searches as the Hunter.

The game uses radio (ESP-NOW) to track distance like a "hot-or-cold" radar and an infrared beam (IR) on top of the device for direct line-of-sight tag shots.

Hardware

    2x M5StickS3 devices.
    No extra components required: all game mechanics use the built-in screen, buttons, speaker, radio antenna, and top-facing IR transmitter/receiver.

Important: The infrared sensor is located on the top edge of the M5StickS3. Do not cover the top of the case with fingers, stickers, or clothes, or shots will not register.
Game Rules
Role Selection

When turned on, the screen prompts for role selection:

    Side Button: Choose Fox.
    Blue Front Button: Choose Hunter.
    Both Buttons (pressed together): Return to role selection menu.

Hunter

    Starts with 5 shots.
    The screen shows a signal bar in the center. When the bar is low (green), the Fox is far away. When the bar fills up with yellow and red segments, the Fox is nearby.
    Press the Blue Front Button to fire.
    Save your ammo: Shooting from far away is useless. The IR beam will miss, the Fox will not react, and you will lose the game once all 5 shots are spent. Wait until the signal bar turns red to strike!
    You must aim the top of the device directly at the Fox.
    If you shoot while close to the Fox and miss with the IR beam, the Fox dodges, and you receive a 30-second penalty lockdown during which you cannot shoot.
    If you use all 5 shots without tagging the Fox, you lose.

Fox

    Hide and do not get tagged.
    The Fox automatically barks at random intervals (every 40 to 75 seconds) and can manually bark using the Side Button.
        If the IR beam hits your device, you are caught and the Hunter wins.
        If the IR beam does not hit, you successfully dodge: a 30-second countdown screen appears, giving you time to run and hide again while the Hunter is penalized.

How to Flash via Arduino IDE
1. Requirements

    Arduino IDE 2.x
    ESP32 Board Package (by Espressif) version 3.0.0 or newer
    M5Unified library (install via Library Manager: Tools -> Manage Libraries -> search "M5Unified")

No third-party IR libraries are required. The project uses built-in ESP-IDF drivers.
2. Board Configuration

Open Arduino IDE, connect the M5StickS3 via USB-C, and set the following under the Tools menu:

    Board: M5StickS3 (or "ESP32S3 Dev Module")

firmwares.firmwareDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"# BTCSigner Cardputer

Signer Bitcoin air-gapped e stateless para o M5Stack Cardputer. A seed é digitada no teclado, a
transação entra e sai pelo microSD, e nada secreto fica gravado no aparelho.

## Recursos

- Sem WiFi e sem Bluetooth: os rádios nunca são ligados.
- A seed (12 ou 24 palavras BIP39) é digitada a cada sessão e fica só na RAM. Passphrase opcional.
- A sessão expira após 3 minutos sem uso e apaga a chave da memória.
- Carteira single-sig BIP84 (`bc1q…`), mainnet e testnet.
- Exporta o zpub e os output descriptors para o microSD, para importar como watch-only no Sparrow,
  Bitcoin Core ou Electrum.
- Assina PSBTs mostrando cada saída com o endereço completo, o valor e a taxa. Para confirmar,
  segure Enter por 1,5 s.
- Rejeita qualquer PSBT que não consiga verificar por inteiro.
- Criptografia do trezor-crypto, a mesma biblioteca das carteiras Trezor.

## Como usar

1. Gere a seed fora do aparelho, num computador offline, e anote as palavras e o fingerprint.
2. Digite a seed no Cardputer e confira o fingerprint.
3. Em CARTEIRA > Exportar xpub, grave o `wallet_export.txt` no microSD e importe no software de
   carteira.
4. Crie a transação no computador e salve a PSBT em `/psbt/` no microSD.
5. Em ASSINAR, escolha o arquivo, revise e segure Enter. A PSBT assinada é gravada como
   `<nome>_signed.psbt`.
6. Leve o arquivo assinado de volta ao computador, finalize e transmita.

## Teclas

- `` ` `` (ESC): voltar ou cancelar
- `;` `.`: subir e descer
- `,` `/`: trocar de aba
- Enter: abrir ou confirmar

## Links

- Código-fonte e documentação: https://github.com/AlldDev/BTCSigner-Cardputer
- Licença: MIT

## Apoie o projeto

Doações em Bitcoin: `bc1qtu6nvfjdcujpweazeq8w0et0vs7swmef75nurw`"}

currentVersion.versionDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"BTCSigner Cardputer v1.2.2
Novidades

* Aviso de taxa baixa: se a taxa estimada ficar abaixo de 0,1 sat/vB (mínimo de relay padrão do Bitcoin Core), o RESUMO mostra a taxa em laranja com o aviso "abaixo do min.". É só um aviso e não bloqueia a assinatura, mas uma transação assim não seria propagada pela rede.
* Taxa mais precisa na tela: abaixo de 1 sat/vB, a taxa aparece com 2 casas decimais. Antes, 0,07 sat/vB era arredondado para "0.1" e escondia uma taxa abaixo do mínimo.
* Rótulos do RESUMO mais claros: "Taxa total" e "Taxa por vbyte".

Correções

* Leitura de PSBT mais rigorosa:
   * Arquivos com campos duplicados são recusados, inclusive campos desconhecidos ou proprietários.
   * Arquivos com dados sobrando depois do fim da PSBT são recusados (por exemplo, duas PSBTs coladas no mesmo arquivo).
   * PSBT em base64 salva por editores de texto agora é aceita: o BOM do Bloco de Notas e espaços ou quebras de linha no começo e no fim são ignorados. A PSBT assinada sai em base64 limpo.
* Proteção dos segredos em caso de falha:
   * Se o aparelho travar ou detectar uma falha, a seed e as chaves são apagadas da memória e ele reinicia na hora, sem mostrar nada na tela ou na saída USB.
   * O firmware não grava mais o "core dump" na memória flash. Esse registro podia guardar restos da seed depois de uma falha. Se algum dump de uma versão anterior estiver na flash, ele é apagado no boot.
   * A memória de trabalho é limpa continuamente durante o uso, então restos de cálculos com a chave não ficam na RAM.

Testes
Novos casos para a leitura de PSBT (dados sobrando, campos duplicados, base64 com espaços e BOM), para o aviso de taxa baixa no limite de 0,1 sat/vB e para a limpeza de emergência dos segredos. O comportamento em uma falha real (reinício sem registro) ainda precisa ser validado no aparelho.

Sem mudanças
Interface e fluxo de uso. Single-sig BIP84 (bc1q), PSBT v0 e SIGHASH_ALL. Taproot (BIP86) está planejado.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/AlldDev/BTCSigner-Cardputer/compare/v1.2.0...v1.2.2"}

versions.versionDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"# BTCSigner Cardputer v1.2.0

## Novidades

- **Menu em carrossel**: depois da seed, as áreas ASSINAR, CARTEIRA, TOOLS e SESSAO viram um carrossel infinito de ícones. Use as setas para deslizar entre as áreas, Enter para abrir a lista e ESC para voltar ao carrossel.
- **Tela SCRIPT (tipo de carteira)**: escolhida depois da rede e antes da seed, como no Electrum. Por enquanto só "SegWit nativo" (BIP84) está disponível. "Taproot (em breve)" aparece em cinza e não pode ser selecionado.
- **Endereço de recebimento por índice (CARTEIRA)**: escolha um índice de 0 a 999. O endereço é calculado pela chave privada e conferido de novo a partir do zpub exportado. Só aparece se tudo bater, senão mostra "(falha na verificacao)".
- **Revisão de PSBT mais completa**:
  - Saídas desta seed identificadas como "TROCO #i" ou "PROPRIO receb. #i".
  - RESUMO com entradas, saídas, taxa, sat/vB estimado e o total que sai da carteira (saídas externas + taxa).
  - Nova tela DETALHES quando a transação sinaliza RBF (BIP125) ou tem nLockTime.
  - Campos apenas informativos: nenhuma regra de validação mudou.
- **Carregamento mais claro**: splash de boot com logo e barra de progresso durante a inicialização do microSD, e mais detalhes nas telas de carregamento e transferência.

## Testes

Novos casos para a derivação por tipo de script, o índice de recebimento e o endereço verificado, comparados com vetores gerados à parte (mainnet e testnet, índices 0, 1 e 999). Os caminhos pela chave privada e pelo zpub são comparados em toda a faixa 0 a 999.

## Sem mudanças

Single-sig BIP84 (bc1q), PSBT v0 e SIGHASH_ALL. Taproot (BIP86) está planejado.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/AlldDev/BTCSigner-Cardputer/compare/v1.1.0...v1.2.0"}

{"format":"markdown","content":"# BTCSigner Cardputer v1.1.0

## Novidades

- **Backup opcional da seed em cartão RFID**: com a M5Stack Unit RFID2, a seed pode ser gravada cifrada num cartão MIFARE Classic 1K/4K (AES-256-CBC + HMAC-SHA256, chaves derivadas da senha por PBKDF2 com 200.000 iterações).
- **Restauração pelo cartão**: no início da sessão, encoste o cartão e digite a senha, sem digitar as 12/24 palavras.
- **Gravação segura**: o cartão guarda duas cópias independentes e é relido e conferido após gravar. Se a gravação for interrompida, o backup antigo ou o novo continua legível.
- **TOOLS > Testar backup**: confere um backup em papel ou no cartão contra a sessão aberta, sem exibir o mnemônico. Também permite apagar o backup do cartão.
- **RFID só quando necessário**: o rádio liga apenas durante backup, restauração ou teste. WiFi e Bluetooth continuam desativados.
- **Unit RFID2 é opcional**: sem o módulo, o firmware funciona como na v1.0.0.

## Correções

- Leitura do microSD: a aba ASSINAR tenta montar o cartão de novo periodicamente, então dá para inserir ou trocar o microSD sem reiniciar.
- Correções na gravação do backup e em arquivos auxiliares.

## Sem mudanças

Single-sig BIP84 (bc1q), PSBT v0 e SIGHASH_ALL.

{"format":"markdown","content":"A real-time audio spectrum analyzer for the M5StickS3, using its built-in microphone. No extra hardware needed.

**What you see**

- 48 bars on a logarithmic 50 Hz – 8 kHz scale, with peak caps that hold and then fall, at about 31 fps
- The frequency of the strongest harmonic, refined between FFT bins (within 0.5 Hz on test tones)
- The nearest musical note, how many cents off it is, and a ±50-cent tuner needle
- Dashes in silence: background noise never shows up as a frequency

**Controls**

- KEY1: pause / resume (a HOLD badge appears)
- KEY2: sensitivity, three steps
- Turn the device over: the picture flips 180°
- Side button: press to power on or reset, double-press to power off

**Good to know**

- For voice and string instruments the second or third harmonic is often the loudest, so the note can read an octave high.
- The microphone barely passes fundamentals below about 60–70 Hz, so such sounds read at their second or third harmonic.

Source code (MIT license): https://github.com/mbogatyr/M5SpectrumAnalyzer"}

{"format":"markdown","content":"## Talking Tom for M5StickS3

Say something, and a cartoon character repeats it in a funny voice, moving its mouth and paws.

**Three characters.** The blue button (KEY1, under the screen) switches between them:

- **Cat**: a cartoon voice, like Talking Tom
- **Hippo**: a deep, gritty bass
- **Mouse**: a squeaky voice

**How to play**

1. Switch the StickS3 on with the side button: the Cat is listening.
2. Say a phrase. The character cups its ear while you speak and repeats the phrase as soon as you stop.
3. Press the blue button for the next character. The new one drops in from above.
4. After two minutes without a phrase the character gets sleepy, waves goodbye and the StickS3 powers off. Press the blue button while it waves to keep it on.

The pitch is shifted while the tempo stays about the same, so the voices sound like cartoons rather than a sped-up tape.

{"format":"markdown","content":"🇬🇧 ENGLISH

MCCC (MeshCore CardComm) is a dedicated MeshCore client built specifically for the M5Stack Cardputer ADV and CAP LoRa-1262 module.

After trying out various MeshCore firmwares on the M5Stack Cardputer ADV, I encountered compatibility issues with my local repeaters running newer MeshCore versions, alongside some usability drawbacks for everyday use. As a developer and active amateur radio operator (EA3IIU), I decided to develop my own client: MCCC — MeshCore CardComm.

My main goal was clear from the start: to make the Cardputer function as a fully independent MeshCore device without needing a phone nearby, while still retaining the ability to pair via Bluetooth as a companion whenever needed. Above all, MCCC is a personal learning project focused on experimentation, solving real-world compatibility hurdles, and sharing progress with the MeshCore community.

Features:

Dual Mode: Operates 100% standalone or as a Bluetooth companion for smartphones.
Rich Messaging: Displays usernames, timestamps, unread badges, and supports path hash size configuration for maximum repeater compatibility.
Alerts & Audio: Visual message notifications and customizable alert tones for DMs and channels.
UI & Tools: On-screen battery level indicator, UI color themes, display brightness control, and real-time user/channel search.
Clock & GPS: Automatic RTC time sync via Bluetooth or physical GPS module.

☕ Support the project: [https://buymeacoffee.com/jsaludes](https://buymeacoffee.com/jsaludes?utm_source=gemini)

Como desarrollador y radioaficionado (EA3IIU), decidí desarrollar mi propio cliente: MCCC — MeshCore CardComm.

firmwares.firmwareDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"**MARS** is a port of the legendary demo by **Tim Clarke** (1993) to the M5StickS3.

Preserved in the Hornet demoscene archive, the original MARS.EXE was a tiny DOS
program of just 5.6 KB. It generated a fractal landscape with the Diamond-Square
algorithm and flew you over it in real time with voxel rendering: a
three-dimensional "red planet" on an IBM PC 386 with VGA (320×200, 256 colours).
Every run made a new planet.

This port does the same on the stick's 240×135 screen at about 35 frames per second:

- a new 256×256 Diamond-Square planet at every start, wrapping seamlessly, so the flight never ends;
- voxel rendering front to back, column by column, as in the original, with its palette,
  its salmon-red cloudy sky, the glowing horizon and far mountains sinking into dark maroon;
- an autopilot that follows the terrain, and steering by tilting the stick.

### Controls

Hold the stick in landscape, screen towards you.

| Input | Action |
|---|---|
| Lower the left or right end | Turn |
| Tip the top edge away / towards you | Dive / climb |

firmwares.firmwareDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"**MARS** is a port of the legendary demo by **Tim Clarke** (1993) to the Cardputer ADV.

Preserved in the Hornet demoscene archive, the original MARS.EXE was a tiny DOS
program of just 5.6 KB. It generated a fractal landscape with the Diamond-Square
algorithm and flew you over it in real time with voxel rendering: a
three-dimensional "red planet" on an IBM PC 386 with VGA (320×200, 256 colours).
Every run made a new planet.

This port does the same on the Cardputer's 240×135 screen at about 33 frames per second:

- a new 256×256 Diamond-Square planet at every start, wrapping seamlessly, so the flight never ends;
- voxel rendering front to back, column by column, as in the original, with its palette,
  its salmon-red cloudy sky, the glowing horizon and far mountains sinking into dark maroon;
- an autopilot that follows the terrain; steer it by tilting the Cardputer or with the arrow keys.

### Controls

Hold the Cardputer in front of you, screen towards you. Lower the left or right end
to turn; tip the top edge away or towards you to dive or climb.

| Input | Action |
|---|---|
| Arrow keys `,` `/` or `A` `D` | Turn left / right |
| Arrow keys `;` `.` or `W` `S` | Climb / dive |
| Enter or the G0 button | New planet; the current grip becomes neutral |
| Space | Speed: slow, cruise, fast |

The keys and the tilt work together. Let go, and the autopilot flies on by itself.
The screen goes dark after 3 minutes without a key press or a tilt; tilt the
Cardputer or press a key to wake it.

The same firmware also runs on the M5StickS3 (a separate MARS listing).

Source code: https://github.com/mbogatyr/M5Mars"}

{"format":"markdown","content":"🌍 LiveEarth Stopwatch 实时地球监控视界
LiveEarth Stopwatch 是一款专为 M5Stack Stopwatch（ESP32-S3 + 466×466 AMOLED 圆屏）量身打造的沉浸式桌面科技玩具与全球实况观测终端。

它将科幻风格的实时 3D 数字孪生地球与全球高可用的公开景观监控源深度融合——转动旋钮或轻触屏幕，地球仪将平滑缩放飞行至目标城市，瞬间呈现来自各大洲地标、火山、阿尔卑斯山脉与港口的真实气象与现场动态。

核心亮点
466×466 AMOLED 硬件级视觉盛宴：纯正全黑背景与低功耗极客 UI，支持 3D 地球昼夜光暗分界线与空间经纬网实时渲染。
全屏 16:9 高清现场流：支持小窗画中画与 406×228 全视界超清直出，搭载极速硬件流式解码与 512KB 高清大图支持。
离线优先与无感 OTA：内置离线机位数据库与 LittleFS 持久化存储，结合 GitHub Actions 自动化探针，每天静默更新全球机位健康度。
极客交互系统：配备滑动收纳抽屉、LIVE 在线智能过滤胶囊、以及全屏倒梯形触控软键盘（支持 Wi-Fi 密码动态配置与 NVS 掉电保存）。
⚖️ 数据来源与合法合规声明
合规性承诺：本工程所收录并呈现的所有实时画面，100% 来源于各国政府机构、官方气象部门、国家公园及科研观测站公开发布的公益性开放数据源（包括但不限于：中国香港天文台 HKO、日本国土交通省 MLIT、欧洲阿尔卑斯全景观测网 Foto-Webcam、美国国家公园管理局 NPS、美国地质调查局 USGS 火山观测所等）。

本项目不收录任何私人监控、安防摄像头或需要越权鉴权的非公开视频流，所有机位均为面向公众开放的自然风景、地标实况及气象地质监测机位，严格遵守公共网络数据访问规范与隐私保护法律法规，仅用于开源学术研究、嵌入式技术交流及公益展示。
🌍 LiveEarth Stopwatch — Cyberpunk Global Live Viewport
LiveEarth Stopwatch is an immersive desktop smart gadget and global live viewfinder tailored specifically for the M5Stack Stopwatch (powered by ESP32-S3 with a 466×466 AMOLED circular display).

By pairing an interactive 3D digital-twin globe with real-time public live cameras worldwide, LiveEarth lets you explore planet Earth in style. Rotate the dial or touch a marker, and the camera smoothly flies across the globe to stream real-world snapshots from iconic landmarks, alpine peaks, oceanic bays, and active volcanoes in real time.

Key Highlights
Vibrant 466×466 AMOLED Graphics: Deep blacks, neon cyber-accents, dynamic day-night solar terminators, and real-time latitude/longitude matrix rendering.
16:9 Inscribed Cinema Feed: Seamless transitions between mini-card previews and a 406×228 max-inscribed fullscreen mode, powered by ultra-low-latency streaming JPEG hardware decoding.
Offline-First & Silent OTA: Preloaded ROM dataset with LittleFS caching, backed by automated GitHub Actions CI probe pipelines that health-check global cameras daily.
Touch-Optimized Cyberpunk UI: Smooth slide-out directory drawer, LIVE filter toggle capsule, and an on-screen inverted-trapezoid virtual keyboard with NVS-persisted Wi-Fi credential management.
⚖️ Data Sources & Legal Compliance Notice
Compliance & Privacy Statement: All live feeds and camera snapshots utilized in this project are 100% sourced from officially open, publicly accessible government meteorological agencies, national park services, and environmental scientific research networks (including, but not limited to: the Hong Kong Observatory [HKO], Japan Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism [MLIT], Foto-Webcam.eu Alpine Network, US National Park Service [NPS], and USGS Volcano Observatories).

This project strictly prohibits and excludes any private webcams, residential surveillance feeds, or credential-restricted streams. All cameras featured are outdoor scenic, meteorological, or geophysical landscape monitors intended for public interest, weather awareness, and tourism. The project strictly adheres to public internet access standards and privacy protection laws, dedicated solely to open-source experimentation, embedded graphics showcase, and educational use."}

{"format":"markdown","content":"Rill Voice is an instrument in the Rill family for M5Stack StickS3. Six synthesized singers (alto, bass, choir, falsetto, tenor and vocoder) sing evolving wordless melodies and vocables. Six visuals sing along: Portrait, Trio, Rubin, Eyes, Carriage and Windows. Sound and visuals run entirely on the device, without an internet connection or account.

[Play in your browser at Rill Sound](https://rillsound.com/voice).

### Controls
- Tap the front button for a new piece and visual.
- Hold the front button for about 0.65 seconds to fade sound out or in.
- Tap the side button to cycle volume and show information.
- Hold the side button to slow the ensemble by 4 BPM; below 52 BPM it wraps to 100.
- Shake for a different visual without changing the music.

### Ensemble
Current firmware joins nearby Rill Voice, Synth, Mallet, World and Drums devices over ESP-NOW without setup, sharing tempo and bar lines. New music enters on a shared downbeat. Voice, Synth and Mallet can propose the shared key.

### Installation
StickS3 only, using its built-in speaker. Installing the factory image replaces the current firmware and settings.

[Source, build instructions and credits](https://github.com/bruceblay/rill-voice). GPL-3.0-or-later; samples and dependencies retain their own licenses."}

{"format":"markdown","content":"一台永远停在「无信号」频道的迷你显像管。琥珀磷光雪花缓缓呼吸，偶尔泛起一阵故障 —— 上千种组合里，规则从不重复。

**拍它一下**：一半的机会，从雪花深处锁定出一个真正的频道 —— 极光与雷暴、金字塔与吴哥窟、云龙与巨鲸、独眼巨人与飞碟母舰；另一半机会，两根亮扫描线滚过，表示「我听见了」。每个世界都有自己的声音：稀疏的盖革叮嗒、外星数字语、摩尔斯电码的 SOS —— 画面和声音讲同一个故事。

· 3864 种故障场景随机组合：雪花、文字招牌、行场扭曲
· 拍打解锁「世界频道」：38 个主体 × 背景 × 天体 × 台标
· 稀有事件：测试卡、彩条、TELETEXT、外星字母表、辐射风暴
· 白噪声随画面联动：假关机静音加一声闷响、搜台扫频
· 闲置 5 分钟自己变成时钟（大字 HH:MM），按任意键回到雪花
· 为失眠准备的：低亮度、低音量、可以一直盯着看

操作：B 键调亮度（6 档）· A 键静音 · 拍一下切台

A mini CRT stuck forever on a dead channel. Amber phosphor snow breathes slowly; now and then a glitch rolls through. Thousands of combinations, never the same twice.

**Slap it**: half the time a real channel locks in from deep in the static — auroras and thunder plains, pyramids and Angkor Wat, dragons and sky whales, cyclops and mother ships; the other half, two bright scan lines roll down to say "heard you". Every world speaks its own language: sparse geiger ticks, alien dial tones, a Morse SOS — picture and sound tell one story.

· 3,864 glitch combinations: snow, station cards, sync roll and tearing
· A slap unlocks 38 subjects across nature, human wonders, myth and sci-fi
· Rare finds: test card, colour bars, TELETEXT, alien alphabet, radiation storm
· White noise that follows the picture: a dead-air thump, a station-scan sweep
· Idle five minutes and it becomes a clock; any key brings the snow back
· Made for sleepless nights: dim, quiet, something to stare at

Controls: B = brightness (6 levels) · A = mute · a slap switches channel"}

{"format":"markdown","content":"P1-5 信道协商（抗多 WiFi 干扰）+ 取景提速。

① **接收端主导选净信道**：开机扫描 WiFi 环境，对候选信道 1/6/11 按干扰打分（Σ RSSI）选最干净的一条，beacon v2.1（`0x55 0x21 ch`）通知发送端搬过去跟随。WiFi 密集的家/办公室场景 FPS 谷底明显抬升（实测切换前常在 ~8fps）。
② **侧栏 HUD 新增常驻 `CHn` 绿色信道徽标**，切换后黄闪 3s——电池模式下也能现场确认协商结果。
③ **`[` `]` 手动切信道**（6→11→1 循环，钉住当前选择）；连续两次 stall（~20s）自动解除钉死回退 auto，防止卡在不在线的信道。
④ **10s 无帧自动重扫信道重新协商**（换路由器/换环境自适应）。
⑤ **取景提速**：`finishFilter` 改整数索引表整块拷贝（180×135，与 pushRotateZoom 逐像素一致），峰值维持 ~18fps。
⑥ **按键修复**：`[` `]` 补进键盘追踪表（此前键位无效）。

**向后兼容**：与旧版发送端混用可正常连接（beacon 前缀 `0x55` 不变）；建议两端同时升级到 Sender v0.1.1 获得完整协商体验。"}

{"format":"markdown","content":"P1-5 信道协商 + TX 队列卡死自愈。

① **beacon v2.1（`0x55 0x21 ch`）携带目标信道**：接收端主导选净信道（开机扫描 1/6/11 干扰最小的那条），发送端收到后跟随搬移。未发现阶段在 **ch6/1/11 巡逻**（每 2s 一跳），锁定后 beacon 静默 8s 自动解锁回巡逻。
② **TX 队列卡死自愈**（真机复现的"切信道后连不上"根因）：接收端离开信道后，单播帧在 MAC 层无限重传会灌满 espnow 发送队列（日志刷 `send(): Out of memory`），**重建 peer / 切信道都清不掉**。现在连续 10 帧一包都发不出即 `esp_now_deinit + begin` 整体重载清空队列，回巡逻态重新发现。
③ **向后兼容**：旧接收端（beacon 仅 `0x55`）仍可在巡逻经过 ch6 时正常锁定。

建议与 Receiver v0.8.9 配套使用以获得完整信道协商体验。"}

firmwares.firmwareDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"【Tab5 上首个满帧 GBA 模拟器】
GBA 在这块 720×1280 大屏上稳稳跑满 60 帧 —— 是真的刷满，不是"能跑"。一台 Tab5 顺带就是 11 台掌机：GB / GBC / NES / SNES / SMS / Game Gear / ColecoVision / PC Engine / Lynx / Game & Watch。
The first full-speed GBA emulator for M5Stack Tab5 — a solid 60 FPS on its 720×1280 display, plus 10 more classic consoles in the same device.

【好玩在哪】
· 屏幕就是手柄 —— 方向键和 A / B / X / Y 都在屏幕上，位置按真机布局摆过，不用另配手柄
· 按住连发 —— GB / GBC / NES 上按住 X / Y 就是连发，射击、跳跃不用一直点
· 中文界面 —— 开机按 1 中文、按 2 英文，两个都顺手
· ROM 直接放卡里 —— 连 .zip 压缩包都能直接放：卡上省一半空间，进游戏还快三成
· 存档留在卡上 —— 关机、换游戏、重启，回来接着玩

⚠️ 把 ROM 放进 SD 卡对应目录就能玩（GBA → /roms/gba，NES → /roms/nes，其余同理），不用刷机、不用电脑。

M5Stack Tab5 (ESP32-P4) · github.com/andjiang0083/retro-go-tab5"}

{"format":"markdown","content":"v0.4.5 (2026-10-06) 竖屏版 · 修两处 GBA 显示/存档问题（均来自用户真机反馈）
· 【修复·画面横条闪烁】快速移动画面时的横向条带闪烁（卷轴 / 换房间时最明显）已修。
  真因：GBA 主循环只有**一块**画面缓冲、且从不轮换，而显示任务在**另一个线程**里异步读取这块内存 ——
  核心渲染下一帧时，显示任务可能还在读上一帧，于是读到「上半屏旧帧 + 下半屏新帧」拼起来的画面。
  上游其它核心（NES / GBC / SNES / gwenesis）都是两块缓冲 + 提交后轮换，本版照此对齐。
  （v0.4.4 把帧率从 ~35 提到 ~60 之后，每秒提交次数多了 1.7 倍，把这个既有缺陷放大到肉眼明显。）
· 【修复·启动器选存档不生效】在游戏列表里选「继续游戏 → 某个存档位」进入游戏后，现在会**直接恢复该存档**；
  「保存并退出 → 下次开机自动续上」也随之恢复。真因：GBA 核心漏了消费启动器传来的「从存档位启动」标志
  （其它 8 个核心都有这 3 行）⇒ 存档位被丢弃，只能再从游戏内菜单手动读档。

firmwares.firmwareDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"A small screen on the table that keeps walking the Backrooms. Level 0, endless: yellowed wallpaper, flickering fluorescents, no exit. The walls slowly collect machine scribbles, handwriting, stains and scratches; sometimes you walk into a stretch that feels wrong, or a room you could swear you have already been in. Signal is collapsing — the picture tears, drops frames and loses itself in static, because you are a videotape that is playing back. No controls needed: set it on the table and watch.

桌上一块小屏，一直在走的后室。无尽 Level 0：泛黄墙纸、忽明忽暗的日光灯、没有出口。墙上会慢慢出现涂鸦、字迹、污渍和划痕；偶尔走进一段"不对劲"的区域，或一间你确信来过的房间。信号在崩坏——画面撕裂、跳帧、没入雪花，因为你是一盘正在回放的录像带。不用操作，放桌上看着就行。

| 规格 Spec | |
|---|---|
| 硬件 Hardware | M5StickS3 (ESP32-S3 · 240×135 ST7789 · AXP2101) |
| 渲染 Render | DDA 射线投射，真机 ~38 fps |
| 空间 World | 32 种 10×10 tile 流式生成，永不重复 |
| 氛围 Atmos | S 层贴花 / 异常段 / 既视感 + 11 种 HUD 事件 + 毫秒级 DV 计时 |
| 功耗 Power | 无 WiFi / 无 IMU / 无传感器（桌搭省电向） |

无需任何操作 —— 开机即走。"}

firmwares.firmwareDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"A pocket explorer of the Mandelbrot set for the M5StickS3. Tilt the stick to fly over the set, hold a key to dive in or pull back. The picture sharpens as soon as you stop, down to the finest filaments.

## Controls

Hold the stick in landscape: screen on the left, USB-C on the right.

- **Tilt**: the view rolls the way a marble would. Lower the right edge to move right, tip the top edge away to move up. The steeper the tilt, the faster.
- **Hold KEY1** (the blue key next to the screen): zoom in, 2x per second.
- **Hold KEY2** (the key on the top edge): zoom out.
- Releasing a zoom key makes the pose you hold the stick in level. Within 8 degrees of level nothing moves.
- An animated intro explains the controls at power-on; any key skips it.

## Features

- Smooth coloring with the classic blue, white and orange palette; the edges of the set are smoothed with four samples per pixel.
- Progressive rendering on both ESP32-S3 cores: a quick preview while the view moves, full resolution as soon as it stops.
- Zoom down to 16384x.
- The display turns off after 3 minutes without activity; any key wakes it.

Source code (MIT): https://github.com/mbogatyr/M5Fractal"}

{"format":"markdown","content":"Overhead - live 3D flight tracker for the M5Stack Tab5 (1.5.1)

The real aircraft around you, flown live in 3D by the Tab5 itself: no PC, no phone, no graphics chip and no subscription. A 3D engine written from scratch for the ESP32-P4 draws them at about 20 to 45 frames a second. Follow any flight and watch it land and take off at real airports - 3,214 from OpenStreetMap, with their terminals, taxiways, stands and control towers - under the real sun, at dusk or by night. CINEMA directs itself through the approach, touchdown (with a slow-motion replay), roll-out, take-off and climb; or pick CHASE, ORBIT, TOWER or FLY PAST. Recorded flights replay in 3D too.

New in 1.5.1: the real land in 3D - the hills of the UK and Ireland at their real height, in the colours of their fields, woods, moors and towns, marched in hand-written RISC-V assembly - one press of the GROUND button away, and a free tool to make the land of your own country. The sound of the engines, made live by the Tab5 with no recordings inside, for the A320 family, the Typhoon, the 777, the ATRs and 23 more turboprops. Take-offs as each kind of aircraft flies them. And a fix for a WiFi fault, in Espressif's ESP-Hosted, that could stop the feed until a restart, with a watchdog that mends a stuck link by itself.

Plus a table and a radar with a map of the world, airport close-ups showing the runways in use, alerts for emergencies, military and rare aircraft and your watchlist, spoken callsigns and clearances, a filter, recording, replay and export to MP4 video, and sharing over WiFi.

What you need: a Tab5 and 2.4 GHz WiFi. The aircraft come from the free adsb.lol and adsb.fi feeds, so no radio is needed. A FAT32 microSD card is optional: it holds recordings and two free packs from GitHub, for the card's overhead folder - airfields.bin (15 MB) for the real airports, and ground.bin (27 MB) for the land and hills of the UK and Ireland. Without them the 3D view's airports show runways only and its land is flat.

User manual (PDF, start here): https://github.com/craigdianesmith-glitch/tab5-adsb-flight-tracker-cpp/releases/download/v1.5.1/Overhead-v1.5.1-User-Manual.pdf
Airfield pack (airfields.bin, for the overhead folder of the SD card): https://github.com/craigdianesmith-glitch/tab5-adsb-flight-tracker-cpp/releases/download/v1.5.1/airfields.bin
Ground pack (ground.bin, for the same folder): https://github.com/craigdianesmith-glitch/tab5-adsb-flight-tracker-cpp/releases/download/v1.5.1/ground.bin
Source and release notes: https://github.com/craigdianesmith-glitch/tab5-adsb-flight-tracker-cpp/releases

Free. The source is on GitHub, under the MIT and PolyForm Noncommercial licences. Please report problems on GitHub.
Airport layouts (c) OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL. Land from ESA WorldCover (CC BY 4.0) and the Copernicus DEM, modified - their notices are in the user manual and ground-NOTICE.txt."}

firmwares.firmwareDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"**GPS & GNSS Monitor** is a firmware for the M5StickS3 that turns the device into a compact, portable GPS/GNSS monitoring system. By connecting a compatible GPS or GNSS module through UART, you can monitor positioning data, navigation parameters, satellite reception, and trip statistics directly on the device's display.

### Features

- 📍 **Position Monitoring** — View latitude and longitude in real time.
- 🚀 **Speed Monitoring** — Display current speed with selectable measurement units.
- ⛰️ **Altitude Monitoring** — View altitude with configurable units.
- 📏 **Distance Tracking** — Monitor the distance traveled during a trip.
- 🗺️ **Route Statistics** — View route information, including total distance, average moving speed, and starting coordinates.
- 🧭 **Course Monitoring** — Display the current direction of movement and related navigation data.
- 🛰️ **Satellite & Signal Information** — Monitor the number of satellites and HDOP (Horizontal Dilution of Precision) to assess positioning quality.
- 📅 **Date & Time** — Display GPS-derived date and time with customizable formats and timezone settings.
- ⏱️ **Session Information** — Track time in motion and other trip-related information.
- 🎨 **Display Customization** — Configure theme colors, brightness, screen orientation, and screen timeout.
- ⚙️ **GPS/GNSS Configuration** — Select UART RX and TX GPIOs, configure the communication baud rate, and adjust the module timeout.
- 🔧 **Flexible Settings** — Customize measurement units, coordinate formats, date and time formats, and screen update intervals.
- 💾 **Persistent Configuration** — Settings are saved in non-volatile storage (NVS) and retained after restarting the device.

### Navigation

- **Button B — Short press:** Move to the next screen.
- **Button B — Long press:** Move to the previous screen.
- **Button A:** Navigate between additional views on supported screens or change the selected setting.

### Recommended UART Connections

For the M5StickS3, the recommended GPIO configuration depends on the connection interface.

**Hat2-Bus**
- Configure G44 as RX and G43 as TX.
- Module TX → G44.
- Module RX → G43.

**HY2.0-4P**
- Configure G10 as RX and G9 as TX.
- Module TX → G10.
- Module RX → G9.

The firmware provides additional GPIO options that may not correspond to GPIOs physically available on the M5StickS3. These options are intended to make the firmware easier to adapt to other devices, including the M5 Cardputer and other devices in the M5Stick family. Always verify the available pins and UART capabilities of your specific hardware before connecting a module.

### Documentation & Source Code

The complete documentation, wiring instructions, configuration details, firmware information, and Arduino `.ino` source code are available in the project repository:

**GitHub:** https://github.com/viniciushnf/M5StickS3-GPS-GNSS-Monitor

The source code can be inspected, modified, and compiled using the Arduino IDE with the appropriate M5StickS3 board support and required libraries.

For questions, suggestions, or feedback, feel free to contact me on Instagram: [@viniciushnf](https://www.instagram.com/viniciushnf/)."}

{"format":"markdown","content":"# GPS & GNSS Monitor v1.2

This update introduces new configuration options, improved display controls, and enhanced trip statistics.

### New Features

{"format":"markdown","content":"v7.3 - 2026-09-20
Системный курсор (IMU pointer)
Новый модуль core/cursor.*: пиксельный курсор, управляется наклоном устройства (разгон/торможение, как обычный указатель).
Работает в Tools/Apps/WiFi/Games/Clock и их подменю (через list_menu.cpp), в Settings и в BIOS - хит-тест под все стили отображения (обычный список / Grid / List+Icons).
Активируется через Settings -> Cursor: IMU, либо автоматически в Desktop/OS режиме.
A = левый клик (выбрать/активировать), B = правый клик (назад) - там, где применимо.
Докрутка списка/переключение страницы у края экрана: если навести курсор к нижнему/верхнему краю видимой области - список сам скроллит или переключает страницу навстречу.
Desktop / OS режим
Новая настройка Settings -> Desktop: Firmware (обычное меню, как раньше) / OS (рабочий стол).
В OS-режиме главное меню рисуется как рабочий стол: сетка иконок приложений + таскбар снизу (имя устройства, время, WiFi, батарея), курсор активен всегда.
Клик по иконке (A) запускает приложение, как обычная активация пункта меню.
Air Mouse
Добавлен правый клик: A = левая кнопка, B = правая (было только A).
Стабильность
Исправлена гонка при закрытии сессий Internet SDR / Web Radio: закрытие ждало фиксированные 100мс перед уничтожением websocket-клиента, что могло совпасть с середины хендшейка фонового потока (потенциальный краш). Теперь ждём явного сигнала завершения потока.
Исправлен баг двойного тапа B в списках: если между первым тапом и срабатыванием окна успевали сменить выделение кнопкой A - активировался не тот пункт. Индекс теперь фиксируется в момент самого тапа.
Документация
README обновлён: раздел про формат .thm-тем (UEFI/BIOS) оформлен как таблица, добавлен FAQ про отличие от Bruce (философия проекта - не пентест-инструмент, а лёгкая PC-like ОС для маленького микроконтроллера).
Прошивка (ESP32-S3, 8 MB, dio, 80 MHz)
python -m esptool --chip esp32s3 -b 460800 write_flash 0x0 k85OS_7.3.bin"}

{"format":"markdown","content":"## 2026-10-30 (v0.7.0-alpha) - SIGNAL HUNTER
- **Hunt a BLE device by signal strength.** A "Track device" action on the BLE scanner opens a proximity view that locks onto the chosen device and turns its advertisement RSSI into a smoothed signal meter with a getting-closer / getting-farther arrow and a red/amber/green band, so you can walk down a beacon or tag. It is labelled signal, not distance (RSSI is not a tape measure). 
- **Locate a WiFi AP by beacon signal.** A "Locate AP" action on the WiFi scanner does the same for an access point: it locks the AP's channel, reads its beacon RSSI frame by frame and drives the same meter, arrow and band, and works on a hidden or idle AP.
- **Act on connected clients from Evil Twin.** The CLIENTS list is now interactive: ENTER on a client opens a menu to deauthenticate it once (bounce it back through the captive portal) or block it, which keeps it kicked off for the rest of the session.
- **BLE Identity Spoof is no longer a dead action.** Selecting "Spoof Identity" on a scanned device previously did nothing; it now opens the spoofer locked to that device to clone its name and MAC, and a cold launch from the BLE menu shows a `(select from scanner)` prompt that routes to the scanner to pick a target instead of advertising an empty persona. (Remains in the experimental tier pending on-device confirmation of the clone.)
- **Read-only logs scroll with a position thumb.** The probe, credential, client-traffic, saved-network, About and What's New views now use the shared list component: a proportional scrollbar thumb replaces the old carets and "N/M" readout, and scrolling clamps cleanly at both ends.
- **Crashes now record the heap state that preceded them.** A small flight recorder in always-on RTC memory logs the free heap, largest free block (fragmentation) and minimum free heap with a real timestamp, so an out-of-memory reboot leaves evidence of how starved the heap was instead of a bare reset.
- **Footer counters no longer truncate.** Large index/total counters (such as a four-digit file count) render in full instead of being cut to "1000/10"; the counter formatter is now shared and bounds-checked. First external community contribution.
- **Build integrity: third-party firmware-library ZIPs are pinned by SHA256.** The two external release ZIPs the build downloads are verified against recorded checksums in CI, so a re-uploaded asset at a fixed URL can't silently change the shipped bytes.



## 2026-10-30 (v0.7.1-alpha)

Stability point release.

- **BadBLE no longer loops after a reflash.** HID mode now advertises a fresh random identity each session by default, so a host's stale bond from a previous install can no longer collide and spin the device in an endless reconnect loop. "Fixed MAC" becomes opt-in persistence for operators who deliberately want a reconnectable identity, and a reconnect-storm guard stops advertising (with a "forget on host" hint) if that opt-in path ever spins. Verified on-device.
- **BadUSB SD scripts are discoverable.** The "No scripts found" screen now names the path and format (DuckyScript `.txt` in `/adversary/badusb/`), and the README documents the convention. The SD-loading feature already existed; operators just could not find it.
- **BadBLE "Type" row relabelled "Appearance".** It only ever set the BLE GAP appearance icon hint (hosts classify an HID device by its report map, which is always a keyboard), so the honest label avoids implying it changes the device class. A dead `setAppearance` no-op was removed. Real mouse/joystick device types are tracked for a later release."}

{"format":"markdown","content":"## 2026-10-25 (v0.6.0-alpha) FIELD USABILITY
- **The screen now sleeps on idle to save battery.** After a period of inactivity the display dims to a still-readable level, then turns off; any key wakes it. Both delays are configurable in Settings > Display (Dim After / Screen Off), and the dim stage is a readable intermediate so a glance does not require a keypress.
- **Clocks show your local time.** Set a UTC offset in Settings > Time Zone and the wardriving clock and on-screen times render local, while saved logs and exports stay in UTC so captures remain comparable across devices.
- **Actions that need an SD card grey out when none is in.** Rebuild Index no longer runs a scan that reports a false success with no card present; it reads as disabled until a card is inserted, matching the rest of the SD-gated menu.
- **Wardriving radio mode is chosen per run from the idle screen.** The WiFi / BLE / both selector sits on the pre-run screen, so each session picks its radios without a trip into Settings.
- **A what's-new screen shows once after an update.** The first boot on a new version opens a short summary of what changed; reopen it any time from Settings > What's New. The version is shown live from the build, so the notes never carry a stale number.
- **Handshake Auto Hunt describes itself accurately.** The config screen no longer claims Auto Hunt "uses values from the Settings menu": its timing is built in and the whitelist is its only Settings input, which the copy now states."}

{"format":"markdown","content":"## 2026-10-23 (v0.5.0-alpha) - The UX Update
- **One model behind every attack-config screen.** Deauth, Evil Twin, Karma, Probe Flood, Beacon Spam and Handshake now share the same config form: identical row chrome (label left, value right), the same selection and scrolling behaviour as the lists, one green start-button style, and one keyboard model for navigating, editing values and activating a row.
- **Handshake is now two screens: Auto Hunt and Manual.** The mode is chosen from the Wireless -> Handshake menu instead of toggled inside the screen, so each presents only the controls it needs.
- **Deauth and Handshake Manual take their target from the scanner.** The Target row shows `(select from scanner)` until set; selecting it opens the WiFi scanner and returns with the chosen AP. Manual capture shows the target SSID, channel and BSSID on the capturing screen.
- **Destructive confirms are consistent everywhere.** Every delete / clear / discard / forget prompt now routes through one shared confirm dialog.
- **Menus grouped by purpose, with a unified footer style.** The Wireless and BLE menus are banded into Recon / Attacks / Data sections, and footer hints and key glyphs follow one house style across the UI. 
- **New Tron electric-cyan theme preset.**
- **Wardriving is steadier in BOTH (WiFi+BLE) mode.** A fixed-size Bloom filter bounds deduplication memory and a passive BLE scan flattens the heap-usage slope, so long BOTH-mode sessions no longer trend toward out-of-memory; the live log reserves per-type slots and the network count survives Stop for the save screen.
- **Optional heap-fragmentation readout.** The heap badge can show the largest free block alongside free heap, the tell that classified the BOTH-mode OOM.
- **Sniffer capture controls moved into a config block** for a consistent setup flow before capture."}

{"format":"markdown","content":"## 2026-10-19 (v0.4.0-alpha)
- **Wardriving now observes BLE as well as WiFi.** A BLE observation source feeds both the live network log and the WiGLE CSV export, selectable with a radio-mode setting (WiFi / BLE / both); deduplication is type-aware so a WiFi AP and a BLE peripheral never collapse into one row. WiFi and BLE run at the same time via radio coexistence. 
- **Sniffer capture no longer corrupts the heap.** The WiFi-driver-task callback mutated containers the main loop also touched with no synchronization, so under load the dual-core chip smashed allocator metadata and rebooted (`CORRUPT HEAP`), usually caught on exit-to-menu. Each frame is now copied into a POD and handed to the main loop over a FreeRTOS queue, which does all stats/log/pcap work on one task. 
- **Packet log reads cleanly under heavy traffic.** Scrolling up off the newest row freezes the log so it stays readable at any packet rate (stats, flood detection and capture keep running), and the log renders in capture order after its ring buffer wraps.
- **Release firmware runs quiet.** A level-gated logging layer and a dedicated release build ship the image at WARN, so the serial console is no longer flooded at runtime.
- **One shared component behind every list and popup menu.** The scanner, sniffer, wardriving, captures, RFID, radio, BLE, settings and handshake-history lists, and all eight quick-action popups, now route through a single list/menu component, so navigation, scrolling and the selected-row highlight are consistent across the whole UI.
- **Evil Twin lists every connected client.** The clients view no longer drops entries."}

{"format":"markdown","content":"## 2026-10-11 (v0.3.0-alpha)
- **RFID Write / clone.** Restore a saved `.nfc` dump onto a MIFARE Classic 1K card — all 47 data blocks written back with the recovered keys (Key A → Key B → factory-FF fallback), with a per-block write-retry so a transient RF warm-up can't drop a block on the first pass. Every outcome is reported (blocks written, auth failures, write failures); nothing is silently skipped.
- **UID cloning on magic cards.** The opt-in UID write now lands block 0 on both card families: a Gen2/CUID direct write, and — falling through when that is refused — the Gen1a backdoor. The firmware reports which card type it detected; an ordinary card's locked UID is reported plainly, not masked. Verified end-to-end on a Gen1a card (UID written, read back, then restored).
- **Reliable Gen1a magic detection and sector reads.** Detection retries the timing-sensitive backdoor probe so a magic card is not missed on the first try; the audit read path authenticates once per sector (the fix for sectors reading back as `??`) and names every read/auth failure instead of failing silently.
- **Dashboard web AP is WPA2-protected.** The on-device dashboard access point now uses an auto-generated per-device key instead of being open. (#45)
- **Sniffer capture survives an attack handoff.** WiFi is re-initialised on sniffer start, so launching a capture after an attack no longer comes up dead. (#52)
- **Root-menu list items live-gate on Re-scan.** Menu entries for a module seated after boot (RFID, Wardriving, Captures, BadBLE) un-grey as soon as a Re-scan finds the hardware, no reboot."}

{"format":"markdown","content":"- **Captured credentials are no longer printed to the serial console.** The captive-portal login handler logged harvested usernames and passwords in cleartext via an unconditional `Serial.printf`; it now logs only a secret-free capture count, and the leftover debug pointer prints were removed. (slice-0035)
- **Screenshots save reliably from memory-heavy screens.** Fn+S now streams the BMP to SD row-by-row instead of allocating the whole ~97 KB file at once, so a capture from a full Scanner or Sniffer list no longer fails with an out-of-memory error on the no-PSRAM device. (slice-0034)
- **Screenshot capture (Fn+S).** Press Fn+S on any screen to save a BMP of the current display to `/adversary/screenshots/`. *(First appearance in this log; shipped earlier.)*
- **SD-gated menu entries are greyed out when no card is present**, so unavailable actions (captures, dashboard, wardriving export, API-key import, logs) read as disabled rather than failing only after you select them. *(First appearance in this log; shipped earlier.)*
- **Boots gracefully with no SD card.** The device no longer requires a card to start; SD-dependent actions degrade with a toast + retry instead of blocking boot. *(First appearance in this log; shipped earlier.)*"}

firmwares.firmwareDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"**Lego Duplo Train R/C** turns the M5StickS3 into a Bluetooth remote control for the LEGO DUPLO connected train, instead of the smartphone app. Tilt the stick to drive, press a key to start and stop, shake it to sound the horn. The screen is made for small children: big chevrons light up with the speed.

Tested with the **LEGO DUPLO Cargo Train, set 10875**.

### Controls

- **Tilt** the top of the stick away from you / towards you: forward / backward, 5 speed levels each way
- **KEY1** (the blue button on the front): start / stop, with the brake sound
- **KEY2** (the side button): next sound: steam, departure, water refill
- **KEY2 twice**: next light colour: off, red, blue, green, white
- **Hold KEY2 for 1.5 s**: make the current grip the zero tilt
- **Shake**: horn

### How to use

1. Switch the stick on. The splash screen shows the controls.
2. Switch the train on. The stick finds it and connects by itself: the dot in the corner turns green.
3. Hold the stick comfortably, press KEY1 and tilt.

Source code and documentation: https://github.com/mbogatyr/M5LegoDuploTrain

LEGO and DUPLO are trademarks of the LEGO Group, which does not sponsor, authorize or endorse this project."}

{"format":"markdown","content":"Open-source firmware turning the ultra-compact **M5Stack M5NanoC6** (ESP32-C6FH4) development board into a high-performance **Zigbee 3.0 Range Extender (Router)**.

Ideal for expanding Zigbee mesh coverage across your smart home, bridging dead zones, and improving link reliability for Zigbee coordinators like Home Assistant (ZHA) and Zigbee2MQTT.

### ✨ Features
- 🌐 **True Zigbee 3.0 Router (Range Extender):** Routes mesh traffic at the IEEE 802.15.4 layer and supports up to 20 direct child end devices.
- 💡 **Dual LED State Machine:**
  - **Searching/Pairing:** Flashing blue every 1s (500ms ON / 500ms OFF).
  - **Connected:** Solid blue for 2s, followed by solid green for 3s, then fully off.
  - **Discrete Normal Operation:** LEDs remain completely OFF during routing operation to eliminate annoying ambient light in bedrooms or living areas.
- 💓 **Active ZCL Heartbeat for Zigbee2MQTT:** Automatically transmits a periodic `genBasic` cluster read request every 60s to ensure `last_seen` and `linkquality` (LQI) stay continuously updated in Zigbee2MQTT and Home Assistant.
- 🔘 **Multi-Function Button (GPIO 9):**
  - **Quick Click (< 1s):** Instantly forces a ZCL heartbeat and ZDO query to coordinator `0x0000` with a rapid green confirmation pulse.
  - **Long Press (5s):** Clears Zigbee NVRAM/NVS credentials, leaves the current network, and reboots in pairing mode.
- 🔌 **Mains Powered Classification:** Declares `Power Source = Mains` to ensure coordinators maintain permanent keep-alive and routing paths.
- 🧩 **Zigbee2MQTT External Converter Included:** Ready-to-use converter (`m5nanoc6_extender.js`) for full vendor, model, and device identification in Z2M."}

{"format":"markdown","content":"Open-source firmware turning the ultra-compact **M5Stack M5NanoC6** (ESP32-C6FH4) development board into a high-performance **Thread Range Extender / Router (Full Thread Device - FTD)**.

Ideal for expanding IEEE 802.15.4 mesh coverage for **Matter over Thread** and native Thread networks across your smart home, eliminating dead zones and boosting connectivity for Thread Border Routers such as Home Assistant (OpenThread Border Router - OTBR), Apple Home (HomePod / Apple TV), and Google Home (Nest Hub).

### ✨ Features
- 🌐 **True Thread Router (FTD):** Full Thread Device routing mesh traffic at the IEEE 802.15.4 IPv6 layer, forwarding frames and supporting child end devices (Sleepy End Devices).
- 💾 **Persistent NVS Storage:** Thread active operational datasets are automatically saved to non-volatile storage (NVS), enabling instant, seamless reconnection after power cycles.
- 💡 **Dual LED State Machine:**
  - **Searching / Detached:** Flashing blue every 1s (500ms ON / 500ms OFF).
  - **Connected:** Solid blue for 2s, followed by solid green for 3s, then fully off.
  - **Discrete Normal Operation:** LEDs remain completely OFF during routing operation to eliminate ambient light in bedrooms or living spaces.
- 🔘 **Multi-Function Button (GPIO 9):**
  - **Quick Click (< 1s):** Triggers an immediate mesh diagnostic and telemetry report over Serial with a rapid green confirmation pulse (250ms).
  - **Long Press (5s):** Clears Thread dataset from NVS, performs an OpenThread factory reset, and reboots in pairing/unconfigured mode (solid red LED for 1s).
- 💻 **Interactive OpenThread CLI (USB CDC):** Built-in serial console on the native USB port at 115200 bps for easy configuration, inspection, and network management.
- 💓 **Periodic Mesh Heartbeat (60s):** Automatically logs network role, RLOC16, channel, and PAN ID every 60s to monitor mesh vitality."}
