{"format":"markdown","content":"**Live aircraft tracker for the M5Stack Cardputer.**

AirPuter shows nearby aircraft directly on the Cardputer display using live ADS-B data. It includes an interactive OpenStreetMap view, a lightweight outline map, a sortable flight list, aircraft details, and GPS support through the Cardputer LoRa/GPS CAP.

Project repository: https://github.com/lukasdurjan/AirPuter-For-Cardputer-ADV-CAP-LoRa-1262-

## Version 1.0.17 highlights

- Smoother live map: aircraft positions are dead-reckoned between ADS-B responses from groundspeed, track and data age. Prediction is capped at 60 seconds and resets to every newly received real position.
- More reliable photos: transient `HTTP -1` connection failures and incomplete JPEG transfers receive one clean automatic retry. A complete JPEG end marker is accepted even when a proxy reports a slightly incorrect content length.
- Faster and clearer GPS operation: NMEA parsing starts during the splash screen, quality and time-to-fix diagnostics are available in Serial Monitor, and the GPS indicator distinguishes searching, weak and quality fixes by colour.
- `C` toggles GPS Follow and Free View. Follow blocks panning; disabling it retains the last displayed GPS position instead of jumping to a fallback.
- A permanent centre crosshair, compact `Follow` / `Free View` label and coloured follow brackets make the current map state visible without a large status panel.
- Persistent custom Home position and ten Favorite Places. Tap `0`–`9` to open a favorite or hold a number to save the current map centre; successful saves beep once.

## Features

- Live nearby-aircraft tracking using the ADSB.lol API
- OpenStreetMap raster map with aircraft position and track
- Lightweight outline-map mode with country outlines and city labels
- Map pan and 5 / 10 / 25 / 50 / 100 / 200 NM zoom levels
- Continuous on-device aircraft position prediction between network refreshes
- Nearby-flight list sorted by distance from the observer
- Global SQUAWK7500 list available from the Tab screen cycle; select an aircraft and press `Enter` to keep the map centred on its live position
- Persistent display Auto Dim setting: 30, 60, 120 seconds or Off
- Persistent aircraft refresh interval setting: 10, 15, 20, 25 or 30 seconds (10 seconds by default)
- Detailed aircraft view: callsign, ICAO, registration, type, route, distance/bearing, altitude, groundspeed, track, vertical speed, squawk, coordinates, emergency state and data age when available
- Hold `Alt` on an active flight detail to temporarily show its aircraft photo; release it to return to the data
- Route lookup through ADSB.lol VRS standing data
- GPS input through the LoRa/GPS CAP (UART RX on GPIO 15, 115200 baud)
- Persistent user-defined Home fallback, with Poprad, Slovakia retained as the factory default
- Ten persistent Favorite Places assigned to number keys `0`–`9`
- Wi-Fi network scanner and on-device password entry
- Saved Wi-Fi credentials after a successful connection
- Map mode preference retained across restarts
- Network work runs separately so GPS and UI remain responsive

## Hardware

- M5Stack Cardputer / compatible StampS3-based Cardputer target
- Wi-Fi connection for live aircraft data and map tiles
- Optional LoRa/GPS CAP for live observer position

The current PlatformIO target is `m5stack-stamps3` and uses the `M5Cardputer` library.

## Controls

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Arrow keys | Pan map when GPS follow is off; move through lists/menus |
| `I` / `O` | Zoom in / out |
| `C` | Toggle GPS follow; disabling it keeps the last displayed GPS position |
| Short `0`–`9` | Open the corresponding saved Favorite Place |
| Hold `0`–`9` | Save the current map centre to the corresponding Favorite Place |
| `Opt` | Open settings / return from settings |
| `Tab` | Cycle map, flight list and global SQUAWK7500 list; details → map |
| `Enter` | Open a normal selected flight; in SQUAWK7500 start map tracking; activate a menu item |
| Hold `Alt` | Show the aircraft photo while viewing active flight details |
| `Esc` | Details → list; Wi-Fi screen → previous menu; on map restore GPS following |
| `R` | Rescan Wi-Fi networks while in Wi-Fi list |
| `Backspace` | Delete character during Wi-Fi password entry |

Aircraft photos and photographer credits are provided by the PlaneSpotters.net public photo API and require Wi-Fi.

Photo lookup and image download use a single clean retry for a transient connection-refused (`HTTP -1`) failure. If a transfer ends before a complete JPEG is received, AirPuter discards the partial buffer and downloads it again. Intermediate retry details are written only to Serial Monitor.

The flight list follows the current map viewport and refreshes with incoming aircraft data. Zooming and panning immediately filter cached aircraft; ADS-B requests wait for the configured refresh timer. Between responses, AirPuter advances moving aircraft locally using their reported groundspeed, track and position age, refreshing the map at up to 4 FPS. Every successful ADS-B response replaces predictions with real positions. Prediction stops after 60 seconds so stale aircraft cannot continue indefinitely. The query covers the viewport corners. Up to 50 visible aircraft are retained using stable sampling across the complete response; busy areas can contain more aircraft than displayed. Zooming out fills newly visible areas on the next successful refresh.

### API rate limits (HTTP 429)

HTTP 429 ("Too Many Requests") means ADSB.lol has temporarily limited requests. The response itself is a server-side rate limit, not an AirPuter crash or a map-rendering bug. ADSB.lol uses dynamic limits based on server load, so a refresh interval that works normally can occasionally be rate-limited. See the [ADSB.lol API documentation](https://github.com/adsblol/api/blob/main/README.md#rate-limits).

AirPuter automatically pauses both nearby-aircraft and SQUAWK7500 requests for 60 seconds after a 429. Further 429 responses extend the shared pause to 120, 240 and at most 300 seconds. A successful aircraft response resets the next backoff to 60 seconds. The selected Refresh Interval stays saved and unchanged.

During this pause, the last successfully received aircraft data remains available. Moving positions continue to be estimated for at most 60 seconds from the last real update, then stop until fresh data arrives. The nearby-aircraft status shows "Rate limited - automatic pause" after a nearby request receives 429. Zooming or panning does not bypass the pause or trigger an early ADS-B request. Updates resume automatically; a restart is unnecessary. Choosing a longer Refresh Interval can reduce request pressure. An actual device restart is a separate fault and should not be treated as normal rate-limit behavior.

## Map modes

### Important map-loading bugfix

Map tiles could download successfully but intermittently remain on **Map waiting for data**, especially while an ADS-B request was running. The cause was simultaneous TLS/network activity and PNG decoding competing for one large contiguous block of ESP32-S3 heap. A tile could return HTTP 200 and be saved correctly while the M5GFX PNG decoder still failed to allocate its working memory.

AirPuter now serializes memory-intensive HTTP/TLS operations and PNG decoding. Map rendering never blocks the UI: when networking is using the required memory, decoding is deferred automatically and retried after the operation finishes. A contiguous-heap guard also prevents starting a PNG decode that cannot complete. This applies when centring on GPS, panning, and changing zoom.

### Tiles

Downloads visible PNG tiles from OpenStreetMap while the tile map is displayed. AirPuter displays the required OpenStreetMap attribution on screen.

### Outline

A compact built-in black map with country outlines and city labels. It does not download raster map tiles and is useful when you want a cleaner, lighter display.

## GPS

AirPuter listens for NMEA GPS data at **115200 baud** on **GPIO 15**. UART reception and NMEA parsing start before the splash screen, allowing acquisition to proceed while the splash is visible. A recent valid GPS fix becomes the observer position and the map follows it by default.

The header GPS dot pulses red while searching, turns orange for a valid but weaker fix, and green for a quality fix. Serial Monitor reports received characters, satellite count, HDOP, data age, fix loss and time to first fix. No factory-reset command is sent to the GNSS receiver.

Without a valid GPS fix, AirPuter falls back to:

```text
49.0550 N, 20.3010 E
```

This is the default Poprad-area position. **Set home position** in the settings menu accepts coordinates in
`latitude,longitude` format and saves them on the device as the fallback position. If no custom home position
has been saved, the Poprad fallback remains unchanged.

**Favorite Places** provides ten persistent slots assigned to keys `0`–`9`. Tap a number to move the map to
that saved position, or hold it for 800 ms to store the current map centre. A short beep confirms a successful save. The **Favorite Places** settings screen lists all ten slots. Panning is disabled while GPS follow is active;
press `C` first to stop following while retaining the last displayed GPS position.

The centre of the map is always marked by a fixed white crosshair with a yellow centre. A small cyan `Follow` or grey `Free View` label shows the active navigation mode. Coloured corner brackets around the observer appear only while a valid GPS fix is actively followed.

## Building with PlatformIO

1. Install Visual Studio Code and PlatformIO.
2. Clone this repository.
3. Open the project folder in VS Code.
4. Build the `m5stack-cardputer` environment.
5. Connect the Cardputer and upload from PlatformIO.

Command-line build:

```bash
pio run -e m5stack-cardputer
```

Upload:

```bash
pio run -e m5stack-cardputer -t upload
```

Serial monitor:

```bash
pio device monitor -b 115200
```

## Wi-Fi configuration

AirPuter can scan for Wi-Fi networks and enter credentials directly on the Cardputer. Successfully connected credentials are stored for subsequent starts.

### Important Wi-Fi scan bugfix

The Wi-Fi scanner previously found no networks in most scans on some devices. An empty or placeholder `NONE` SSID was incorrectly treated as a configured network, causing a connection attempt to run before the scan. The scan could then start while the ESP32-S3 radio was still changing state and return an empty result.

The scanner now:

- treats empty and `NONE` credentials as **Wi-Fi not configured**;
- waits for the radio to stabilize before scanning;
- scans hidden networks and spends longer listening on each channel;
- retries automatically up to three times after a failed or empty scan;
- displays both the signal level (`+++`, `++`, `+`, `-`) and RSSI value for every network.

When Wi-Fi is not configured, the map displays **“No WiFi - press Opt, select network”**. Press `Opt`, choose **Wi-Fi networks**, select a network, and enter its password. Press `R` in the network list to request another scan manually.

`src/main.cpp` contains optional fallback credentials. **Do not commit personal Wi-Fi credentials to a public repository.** Leave them empty for public builds:

```cpp
const char* WIFI_SSID = "";
const char* WIFI_PASS = "";
```

## Data and map sources

Aircraft data and route information are obtained from **ADSB.lol**. Raster map tiles are provided by **OpenStreetMap**.

Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors. See `MAP_SOURCES.md` for map-source and attribution details.

## Release binary

Every `pio run -e m5stack-cardputer` build also generates **release/AirPuter.bin**. This folder is tracked by Git, so you can push the ready-to-install binary together with the source:

```bash
pio run -e m5stack-cardputer
git add release/AirPuter.bin
git commit -m "Update release firmware"
git push origin main
```

After every push to `main`, GitHub Actions builds the firmware, finds the highest existing `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` tag and increases its patch number. The current release floor intentionally advances from `v1.0.14` directly to `v1.0.17`; after that release, normal patch increments continue with `v1.0.18`. The workflow embeds that version in the firmware, commits the generated `release/AirPuter.bin` and version header back to `main`, creates the matching tag, and uploads the BIN as the newest GitHub Release. No manual tagging or binary commit is needed.

The repository must allow GitHub Actions to write repository contents. This is configured under **Settings → Actions → General → Workflow permissions → Read and write permissions**. A protected `main` branch must also allow the GitHub Actions bot to push the generated binary commit.

To choose a specific version instead (for example a new major or minor version), push a new version tag:

```bash
git tag v1.1.0
git push origin v1.1.0
```

Use a new version number for each release. GitHub Actions attaches the complete `AirPuter.bin` image to the release; installation instructions are at the top of this README.

## Support

AirPuter splash screen and project support:

**Ko-fi:** `https://ko-fi.com/lukaslukee`"}

# IRcito v1.5.0 — Utilities

IRcito v1.5 expands the v1.4 saved-remotes build with practical day-to-day utilities while keeping the proven IR pipeline unchanged.

## What's new

- Protocol-aware **hold/repeat** for saved buttons
  - Sony SIRC12 uses repeated canonical frames
  - NEC uses the standard NEC repeat frame
  - RAW signals only repeat when a valid repeat policy exists
- **Macros**
  - Up to 4 macros
  - Up to 8 saved-button steps per macro
  - Configurable delays between steps
  - Cancelable during execution
- **Rename**
  - Remotes
  - Buttons
  - Macros
- **USB Serial backup/import**
  - Export saved remotes, signals and macros
  - Versioned backup format
  - Safe merge/overwrite import
  - Truncated or invalid imports do not erase unrelated stored data
- Improved persistence and cross-version compatibility checks

## Installation

Download `IRcito-v1.5.bin` from the assets below.

The provided file is a valid **ESP32-S3 application image**.

It can be installed using EasyLauncher or any other compatible launcher/flashing tool capable of writing an application image to an appropriate app partition.

> **Important:** this is not a merged full-flash image. Do not blindly flash it at offset `0x0`.

### Binary

- File: `IRcito-v1.5.bin`
- Size: **666608 bytes**
- SHA-256:
  `6e0f4ff58be59fcff8e3a822eeeb45ed9a243f4415db0b96665adcc5cffb74ae`

## Compatibility with v1.4

v1.5 keeps the v1.4 saved-signal and remote storage format compatible.

Existing v1.4 Sony, NEC and RAW records can be loaded by v1.5 without migration.

The IR processing pipeline was intentionally kept unchanged:

- `src/ir_pipeline.h` is byte-for-byte identical to v1.4
- Partition configuration was not changed
- Existing saved remotes are not erased during upgrade
- Macro data is stored separately from existing signal records

`src/ir_pipeline.h` SHA-256:

`65a97ce85edb568bd26d30c7f1588d2e6fe680b02e11b6cb3991d0addae47770`

## Tested

Host-side tests passed for:

- IR pipeline
- transactional storage
- TV-B-Gone
- macros
- backup/import
- hold/repeat
- v1.4 → v1.5 NVS compatibility

PlatformIO build:

`pio run -e m5stack-sticks3` — **PASS**

Physical testing on M5StickS3: **PASS**

Validated functionality includes:

- Learn / replay
- persistent saved remotes
- Sony SIRC12
- NEC / NEC-like signals
- RAW fallback
- hold/repeat
- macros
- rename
- USB backup/import
- TV-B-Gone
- persistence across reboot
- v1.4 regression behavior

## Notes

IRcito v1.5 is still intentionally focused on functionality rather than a final polished UI.

Compatibility with every infrared device or protocol is not guaranteed.

See the repository README and `docs/BACKUP.md` for build, storage and backup details.
"}

firmwares.firmwareDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"# MAKER FIGHTER

**つくる手が、拳になる。**

M5Stack Tab5 で動く、1 対 1 の 3D 格闘ゲームです。90 年代のアーケードのようなフラットシェーディングのポリゴンで描かれたファイターたちは、格闘家ではなくメイカーやエンジニア。画面の仮想スティックと G・P・K の 3 つのボタンで、上段・中段・下段を打ち分けて戦います。

公式サイト: https://maker-fighter.com/

## 特長

- Tab5のソフトウェア 3D 描画で、30fps で動きます。
- 1P 対 CPU の勝ち抜き。
- 3 ラウンド制（2 本先取）、制限時間 45 秒、リングアウトあり。
- コマンドで出す専用技が 8 つずつ。


## 遊び方

1. 電源を入れるとタイトル画面（CPU どうしのデモ対戦）になります。画面をタップするとキャラクター選択へ進みます。
2. 下に並んだ顔をタップしてキャラを選び、同じ顔をもう一度タップすると決定です（15 秒たつと自動で決まります）。最初の相手はルーレットで決まります。
3. 勝てば次の相手へ。負けても、10 秒のうちに YES をタップすればコンティニューできます（回数の制限なし）。

音量は、タイトル画面の右上の ⚙ ボタン（設定画面）で変えられます（0〜10 段。本体に保存されます）。

USB ジョイスティックでも遊べます。Tab5 の USB-A に直接挿してください（アケコン用の USB エンコーダ、Xbox 360 互換のパッド、PS4 / PS5 の
パッドなど）。つないでいる間は画面のパッドが消えます。ボタンの割り当ては ⚙ の設定画面で変えられます。

## 操作

「前」「後」は、相手のいる方向が基準です（キャラはいつも相手のほうを向きます）。

| 入力 | 動作 |
|---|---|
| 前 / 後 | 歩く。前,前 / 後,後 でダッシュ / バックダッシュ |
| 下 | しゃがむ（上段が当たらない） |
| 上 | ジャンプ（短く入れると小ジャンプ、長押しで大ジャンプ） |
| 空中で P / K | ジャンプ攻撃（上昇中と下降中で技が変わる） |
| G | 立ちガード（上段・中段を防ぐ） |
| 下 + G | しゃがみガード（下段を防ぐ） |
| P | パンチ（上段。P,P,P で 3 連） |
| 前 + P | 肘（中段） |
| 下 + P | 下段パンチ |
| K | ハイキック（上段） |
| 後 + K | 中段キック |
| 下 + K | ローキック（下段） |
| 前下 + K | ヒザ（中段。当てると相手が浮く） |
| 前 + K | 大キック（上段。当たると相手が倒れる） |
| P + G | 投げ（近い間合いで。立ちガードしている相手にも決まる） |
| 倒れた相手に 下 + P / 上 + P | 踏みつけ / 飛び込みエルボー |
| 倒れているときに G か上 / 後 / K | その場で起きる / 後ろに転がる / 起き上がりの蹴り |

- 上段はしゃがむとかわせます。中段はしゃがみガードでは防げず、下段は立ちガードでは防げません。
- 相手が技を出している最中に当てるとカウンター（ダメージ 1.5 倍）。
- 専用技のコマンド（→↘P、↓→P、←溜め→P、K+P+G など）は、公式サイトの CHARACTER の MOVE LIST で、動きと一緒に見られます。

{"format":"markdown","content":"A note app for the Cardputer and Cardputer ADV. You type a note and press Enter, and an AI model running on the device suggests which list it belongs in. Press Enter again to file it, or pick another list.

currentVersion.versionDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"Pocket Notes is about 1.2 MB smaller and now also installs through Launcher.

### Changes since 1.0

- The AI picks a list in about 0.7 s per note, down from 1.8 s. A new engine runs it, and its answers match 1.0 to within about 2%.
- The firmware fits in the 6720 KB that Launcher leaves free on an 8 MB Cardputer. To install it with Launcher, remove your other Launcher apps, copy this file to the SD card and install it from the SD menu.
- The AI model is 0.5 MB smaller and gives the same answers for English text. It now reads a word with other characters, such as café or 25°C, as an unknown word.
- WiFi clock sync is gone. The app dates a new note only if the clock was already set when the app started. Otherwise it numbers the note.

Flashing 1.2 over 1.0 or 1.1 keeps your notes, on the SD card and in device memory, and what the AI learned from them. The same image runs on the Cardputer and the Cardputer ADV."}

firmwares.firmwareDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"# Cardputer WiFi 扫描器 / Cardputer WiFi Scanner

> 一个专为 **M5Stack Cardputer-ADV** 打造的 WiFi 扫描与管理工具，界面简洁，功能实用，支持中英文切换、信号强度可视化、密码保存、NTP 时间同步、电池电量显示等。
>
> A WiFi scanner and manager designed for **M5Stack Cardputer-ADV**. Clean UI, practical features, bilingual (Chinese/English) support, signal strength visualization, password saving, NTP time sync, and battery display.

![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/Platform-M5Stack%20Cardputer-blue) ![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/Version-1.0.0-green) ![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow)

---

## 🇨🇳 中文说明

### ✨ 功能特性

- 📡 **实时扫描**：一键扫描周围所有 WiFi 网络，按信号强度从强到弱排序
- 📶 **信号可视化**：5 格信号强度条 + RSSI 数值 + 信号等级描述（极强/强/中/弱/极弱）
- 🔐 **连接与保存**：支持选择 WiFi 并输入密码连接，密码自动保存至 NVS（掉电不丢失）
- 🌐 **中英文切换**：内置中英文双语界面，默认英文，可随时在设置中切换，语言设置持久化保存
- ⏰ **时间同步**：连接 WiFi 后自动通过 NTP 同步北京时间，顶部状态栏实时显示
- 🔋 **电量显示**：顶部状态栏显示电池百分比与充电状态图标
- 🎨 **开屏动画**：WiFi 图标弹性缩放 + 文字滑入淡入，非线性动画流畅自然
- 🔔 **开机反馈**：开机时 LED 白色闪烁 + 蜂鸣器“噔”一声
- ❓ **内置帮助**：设置中提供完整键位与功能说明，随时查阅

### ⌨️ 键位说明

> **Cardputer 键盘提示**：  
> `;` 和 `.` 分别对应 **上** 和 **下** 方向。  
> `Fn + `` ` `` 表示按住 `Fn` 键，再按键盘左上角的 `` ` `` 键（即 `~` 键）。

| 界面 | 操作 | 功能 |
|------|------|------|
| **主列表** | `;` / `.` | 上下选择 WiFi |
| | `Enter` | 查看 WiFi 详情 |
| | `空格` | 重新扫描 |
| | `H` | 进入设置菜单 |
| **WiFi 详情** | `;` / `.` | 切换按钮（连接 / 保存 / 返回） |
| | `Enter` | 确认当前按钮 |
| | `Fn + `` ` `` | 返回主列表 |
| **密码输入** | 直接输入 | 输入 WiFi 密码 |
| | `Enter` | 尝试连接 |
| | `退格` | 删除最后一个字符 |
| | `Fn + `` ` `` | 取消并返回详情 |
| **设置菜单** | `;` / `.` | 选择「语言」或「帮助」 |
| | `Enter` | 进入子菜单 |
| | `Fn + `` ` `` | 返回主列表 |
| **语言子菜单** | `;` / `.` | 选择语言（中文 / English / 退出） |
| | `Enter` | 确认选择 |
| | `Fn + `` ` `` | 返回设置菜单 |
| **帮助子菜单** | `Enter` 或 `Fn + `` ` `` | 返回设置菜单 |

### 🚀 快速上手

1. **烧录固件**：使用 M5Burner 选择本固件，起始地址填 `0x0`，点击烧录。
2. **开机**：设备启动后会显示开屏动画，随后自动扫描 WiFi。
3. **浏览网络**：使用 `;` 和 `.` 上下选择，按 `Enter` 查看详情。
4. **连接网络**：在详情页选择「连接」，输入密码后按 `Enter` 连接。连接成功后自动同步时间并保存密码。
5. **切换语言**：按 `H` 进入设置 → 选择「语言」→ 选择「中文」或「English」→ 按 `Enter` 确认。
6. **查看帮助**：按 `H` 进入设置 → 选择「帮助」→ 查看所有按键说明。

### 📝 注意事项

- **SSID 长度**：保存密码时，SSID 长度不能超过 15 个字符（NVS 键名限制），超长会提示无法保存。
- **中文显示**：依赖 M5GFX 内置的 `efontCN_12` 字体，若显示乱码请更新 M5Unified / M5GFX 库。
- **时间同步**：需要连接可访问外网的 WiFi 才能同步北京时间。

---

## 🇬🇧 English Guide

### ✨ Features

- 📡 **Real-time Scanning**: One-tap scan of all nearby WiFi networks, sorted by signal strength (strongest first)
- 📶 **Signal Visualization**: 5-bar signal meter + RSSI value + signal level description (Excellent/Good/Fair/Weak/Very Weak)
- 🔐 **Connect & Save**: Select a WiFi network, enter password, and connect. Passwords are auto-saved to NVS (survives power loss)
- 🌐 **Bilingual UI**: Built-in Chinese/English interface. Default is English; switch anytime in Settings. Language preference is persisted
- ⏰ **Time Sync**: Automatically syncs Beijing time via NTP after connecting to WiFi; displayed in top status bar
- 🔋 **Battery Display**: Shows battery percentage and charging icon in the top status bar
- 🎨 **Boot Animation**: WiFi icon with elastic scale + text slide-in/fade-in using non-linear easing
- 🔔 **Boot Feedback**: White LED flash + buzzer beep on startup
- ❓ **Built-in Help**: Full key bindings and feature guide available in Settings

### ⌨️ Key Bindings

> **Cardputer Keyboard Tip**:  
> `;` and `.` act as **Up** and **Down** respectively.  
> `Fn + `` ` `` means hold `Fn` and press the top-left `` ` `` key (i.e., `~` key).

| Screen | Key | Action |
|--------|-----|--------|
| **Main List** | `;` / `.` | Select WiFi up/down |
| | `Enter` | View WiFi details |
| | `Space` | Rescan |
| | `H` | Open Settings |
| **WiFi Detail** | `;` / `.` | Switch buttons (Connect / Save / Back) |
| | `Enter` | Confirm current button |
| | `Fn + `` ` `` | Back to main list |
| **Password Input** | Type directly | Enter WiFi password |
| | `Enter` | Attempt connection |
| | `Backspace` | Delete last character |
| | `Fn + `` ` `` | Cancel and return to detail |
| **Settings Menu** | `;` / `.` | Select "Language" or "Help" |
| | `Enter` | Enter submenu |
| | `Fn + `` ` `` | Back to main list |
| **Language Submenu** | `;` / `.` | Choose language (Chinese / English / Exit) |
| | `Enter` | Confirm |
| | `Fn + `` ` `` | Back to Settings |
| **Help Submenu** | `Enter` or `Fn + `` ` `` | Back to Settings |

### 🚀 Quick Start

1. **Flash Firmware**: Use M5Burner, select this firmware, set start address to `0x0`, and click Burn.
2. **Power On**: Boot animation plays, then WiFi scan starts automatically.
3. **Browse Networks**: Use `;` and `.` to navigate, `Enter` to view details.
4. **Connect**: In detail page, select "Connect", enter password, press `Enter`. On success, time syncs and password is saved.
5. **Switch Language**: Press `H` → Settings → Language → select "中文" or "English" → `Enter`.
6. **View Help**: Press `H` → Settings → Help → read all key bindings.

### 📝 Notes

- **SSID Length**: Passwords can only be saved for SSIDs up to 15 characters (NVS key limit). Longer SSIDs will show a save error.
- **Chinese Display**: Uses M5GFX built-in `efontCN_12` font. If garbled, update M5Unified / M5GFX libraries.
- **Time Sync**: Requires an internet-accessible WiFi network to sync Beijing time.

---

## 📄 更新日志 / Changelog

### v1.0.0
- 初始版本发布 / Initial release
- 支持 WiFi 扫描、信号强度可视化、连接与密码保存 / WiFi scanning, signal visualization, connect & password saving
- 支持中英文切换、NTP 时间同步、电池电量显示 / Bilingual UI, NTP time sync, battery display
- 加入开屏动画/ Boot animation
- 内置帮助页面 / Built-in help page

---

## 🙏 鸣谢 / Credits

- 固件由 **DeepSeek** 辅助开发 / Firmware developed with assistance from **DeepSeek**
- 基于 **M5Stack Cardputer-ADV** 硬件平台 / Based on **M5Stack Cardputer-ADV** hardware
- 使用 **M5Unified**、**M5Cardputer** 库 / Uses **M5Unified** and **M5Cardputer** libraries

---

**Enjoy your Cardputer WiFi Scanner!** 🎉"}

firmwares.firmwareDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"# 识字 · 拼音 — M5Paper 儿童墨水屏学习卡

> **Made by Tim** · v0.1.5
> 电子墨水屏护眼学习伴侣：无背光、深睡省电、进度记忆

![cover](screenshots/cover.png)

## 功能

| 模块 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| **识字** | 一年级上册 **100 汉字**（部编版写字表全册）· 认 → 写 → 用 认知闭环 |
| | 认：完整字 + 拼音 + 组词（2 二字词 + 1 四字词）+ 造句（目标字反白） |
| | 写：**米字格逐笔演示**（当前笔实心 / 已写衬灰 / 未写轮廓）+ 笔画名 + 笔顺序列 |
| **拼音** | **63 项**：声母 23 · 韵母 24 · 整体认读 16 |
| | 四线三格（字母基线锚定）· 发音口诀 · 例字 · 韵母/整体认读**四声逐调演示** |
| **首页** | 大时钟 + 日期 + 双入口卡片 |
| **对时** | 轻点时钟区 → Wi-Fi 连接 + SNTP 网络对时（未配置时直达配网） |
| **设置** | 右上角齿轮 → Wi-Fi 扫描配网（触摸密码键盘）/ 立即对时 / 关于 |
| **省电** | 空闲 5 分钟自动深睡（墨水屏保画，侧键唤醒续学） |

![home](screenshots/home.png)
![cards](screenshots/card_hanzi.png)
![pinyin](screenshots/card_pinyin.png)

## 安装

### 方式一：M5Burner（推荐）

1. 打开 M5Burner → 设备选择 **M5Paper**
2. 进入用户固件 / Publish Firmware，指向本仓库（含 `m5burner.json`）
3. 一键烧录（含全部数据分区，约 11MB）

### 方式二：esptool 手动烧录

```bash
# 替换 PORT 为你的串口 (macOS: /dev/cu.usbserial-*, Windows: COMx)
PORT=/dev/cu.usbserial-XXXXX
esptool.py --chip esp32 -p $PORT -b 460800 write_flash \
  0x1000    firmware/bootloader_0x1000.bin \
  0x8000    firmware/partitions_0x8000.bin \
  0x10000   firmware/shizi_card_0x10000.bin \
  0x310000  firmware/shizi_0x310000.bin \
  0xb80000  firmware/pinyin_0xb80000.bin
```

> 文件名即烧录地址（`名字_地址.bin`），五个文件缺一不可。

## 使用

| 操作 | 动作 |
|---|---|
| 首页轻点左卡 / 右卡 | 进入识字 / 拼音 |
| 首页轻点时钟区 | 网络对时 |
| 首页右上角齿轮 | 设置（配网 / 对时 / 关于） |
| 识字中轻点屏幕 | 逐笔演示（左 1/3 = 上一笔回看） |
| 左 / 右侧键短按 | 上一项 / 下一项 |
| 中键短按 | 重播 |
| 长按左键 1.5s | 转屏方向（记忆） |
| 长按中键 2s | 深睡 |
| 识字中长按右键 1.5s | 返回首页 |

## 硬件 / 技术

- **M5Paper**（ESP32-D0WD · 960×540 电子墨水屏 IT8951 · GT911 触摸 · 16MB Flash）
- ESP-IDF v5.5.1 + M5GFX
- 内容管线：makemeahanzi 笔画数据 + 规范笔顺表 + 楷体字形 → 全量预烘焙位图
- 首发认知设计：认字音形 → 写笔顺动觉 → 用组词造句

## 版本

| 版本 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 0.1.5 | 首个公开发布：识字 100 字 + 拼音 63 项 + Wi-Fi 对时 + 设置 |

---

**识字 · 拼音** · Made by Tim · 0.1.5"}

{"format":"markdown","content":"Tired of checking multiple usage screens and calculating the best time to use each provider?! This is for you.Open source, 100% local, and easy to set up — NO CAPTIVE PORTAL. Your Wi-Fi is configured via Bluetooth.

On the StickS3, the order of providers automatically changes according to which one is BEST to use over the next 4-hour window.

It requires a local daemon currently working on macOS and still needs to be ported to other platforms — but, as I said, it’s open source.

Download the daemon:
https://github.com/fcavalcantirj/sticks3-ai-usage/releases/latest

Source:
https://github.com/fcavalcantirj/sticks3-ai-usage

BtnA cycles through pages.
Hold BtnB (side button) for 1.5s to flip the screen 180°.

MIT licensed.

P.S. It also comes with a gorgeous web dashboard for a much better overview of your usage."}

firmwares.firmwareDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"Pense Bem — clean-room recreation of the 1988 TecToy "Pense-Bem" educational toy for the M5Stack Cardputer ADV. Built for my 6-year-old nephew.

All ten original games — Adição, Subtração, Multiplicação, Divisão, Aritmética, Operação, Siga-me, Memória de Tons, Número do Meio, Adivinhe o Número — plus Livro (activity-book mode with the reverse-engineered answer tables). 7-segment display look, original cue tunes, 3-minute auto-off.

Keys: number row = answers · ENTER = ok · BKSP = Liga · Q = Desl · L = Livro.

v0.0.1 is in Portuguese (the original toy's language). If likes, bug reports or discussions grow, I will build an English / multi-language version.

Methodology experiment: this firmware was produced by automated development — the plan and task ledger were written by a strong model (Claude Fable), then executed task by task by a free model (Laguna S 2.1 via OpenRouter), with hardware verification on the real Cardputer ADV. Prompts, ledger and full methodology: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1LfCu-MQ7BH4U_5DvRQHm_eYEzywBNIdk?usp=sharing

Source, demo video and releases: https://github.com/fcavalcantirj/pense-bem-cardputer-adv
Single merged image, flash at 0x0. MIT."}

firmwares.firmwareDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"# non magical csi - v2.2 > no magical radar Firmware for the M5Stack Cardputer that reads raw WiFi Channel State Information (CSI) from the ESP32-S3 radio, visualises it in real time, collects labelled training data for on-device ML models, and manages those files on-device. Built for studying what CSI actually is. For demo and educational purposes.

Knowledge should be free

## what it is When your ESP32 receives a WiFi frame, the hardware records how each OFDM subcarrier was attenuated and phase-shifted by the environment - that is the channel state. When something moves through the room, multipath reflections change, and those measurements change too. This firmware captures those measurements, draws them live on screen, runs a motion detector on top, guides you through structured data-collection sessions to build ML training datasets, and lets you browse and manage the collected files directly on the device. ## what it is not - Not radar. There is no angle, no distance, no localisation. - Not reliable for fine-grained gestures with a single AP. - Not a finished product. Calibration drifts. Environment changes break it. - Not magic. Every effect you see has a boring RF explanation. **Passive mode** frame rate depends on ambient WiFi traffic: beacons give ~10 fps per AP on the channel, data traffic adds more. Up to ~50 fps near an active device. **Active injection mode** sends 802.11 Probe Request frames at 10 Hz with per-frame SA MAC rotation, causing the target AP to reply with Probe Responses. Rate is intentionally kept at 10 Hz to avoid exhausting the AP's per-source-address rate-limit bucket. Frame injection uses a libnet80211 symbol-weakening patch (wsl_bypasser technique) applied at build time via `scripts/patch_libnet80211.py`. ## hardware **Primary**: M5Stack Cardputer ADV - ESP32-S3, ST7789 240x135, TCA8418 keyboard, ES8311 codec **Secondary**: M5Stack Cardputer v1/v1.1 - NS4168 amp, 74HC138 keyboard matrix ## views | key | view | |-----|------| | 1 | LOS - calibrated disturbance detector with audio alert | | 2 | Spectrum - amplitude waterfall per subcarrier | | 3 | Variance - which subcarriers fluctuate most | | 4 | Motion - scalar score + sparkline history | | 5 | Correlation - cross-subcarrier coherence | | 6 | ChanOcc - passive per-channel frame-rate survey | | 7 | Console - serial terminal mirrored on screen | | 8 | Training - guided ML data-collection session | | 9 | Files - SD card file browser | Navigation: arrow keys or WASD. ESC / backspace = back to menu. WiFi is stopped automatically when in the menu or Files view to save power. It restarts the moment you enter any sensing mode. **Global keys** (work in all modes): - **C** = cycle channel 1->2->...->13->1 - **+/-** = channel up/down - **P** = toggle active / passive injection (not available in Console or ChanOcc) - **ESC / M** = back to menu ## LOS detector Press **F** to scan for APs, select one, stand still during calibration, three ascending beeps = armed. Measures how much frame-to-frame channel differences exceed the calibrated baseline (z-score on differential amplitude). Score 0-100. **Calibration** collects a baseline in passive mode (80 frames, ~40-80 s) or active injection mode (100 frames, ~10 s at 10 fps). **Active injection** is on by default. Press **P** in any sensing mode (LOS, Spectrum, Variance, Motion, Corr, Training) to toggle between active and passive. ChanOcc is always passive. In LOS mode: **F** = scan APs, **P** = toggle active/passive, **R** = recalibrate, **C** = cycle channel, **Q** = quit. In Spectrum / Variance mode: **R** = reset waterfall history, **C** = cycle channel, **P** = toggle active/passive. **Audio alerts** - Geiger-counter style: beep rate scales continuously with score. Below 20 = silence. | Score | Beep rate | Tone | |-------|-----------|------| | 20-35 | 2 Hz | 800 Hz | | 35-50 | 5 Hz | 950 Hz | | 50-65 | 11 Hz | 1200 Hz | | 65-80 | 22 Hz | 1500 Hz | | >80 | 22 Hz | 2000 Hz | ## channel occupation (ChanOcc) Passive ambient survey. Hops through channels 1-13, dwelling 500 ms per channel (100 ms hardware settle + 400 ms count window). Displays passive frame-rate as horizontal bars for all 13 channels simultaneously. - Bars are auto-scaled to the **historical peak** seen this session - scale never shrinks. - A white tick marks the per-channel peak on each bar. - Stale fps values (zero on current sweep) are shown dimmed in grey. - **P** toggles active/passive injection. In passive mode, beacon frames are the main signal source (~10 fps per AP). In active mode, broadcast probe requests are sent on each channel during the dwell window, prompting probe responses from nearby APs and increasing the count. - OFDM beacons/responses (802.11g/n, >=6 Mbps) produce valid CSI; legacy DSSS frames (802.11b, 1 Mbps) do not. ## training mode Guided structured data-collection sessions that produce labelled CSV files for ML training. ### workflow 1. Enter Training (key 8) 2. Choose a procedure with W/S, press Enter 3. Type a session name (alphanumeric, `_`, `-`; Enter to confirm; ESC to cancel) 4. Follow the on-screen instructions - audio cues tell you when to move and when to hold still 5. CSV is written to SD card at `/non-magical-csi//_.csv` ### audio cues - **3 descending beeps** (1400->900->600 Hz) = transition phase - move to next position - **3 ascending beeps** (600->900->1400 Hz) = capture phase - hold still, recording starts - **3 rising beeps at end** = session complete ### procedures **indoor** (~100 s) - walk the door-to-device axis in a room. Labels: `absent`, `approach`, `still_mid`, `still_near`, `recede`. Requires line-of-sight between door and device. **outdoor** (~50 s) - linear distance sweep, walk ~10 m away and return. Labels: `still_near`, `recede`, `still_far`, `approach`. **zone** (~80 s) - distance sweep along the device axis, near to far and back. Labels: `still_near`, `still_mid`, `still_far`, `approach`, `recede`, `absent`. Covers the full shared label set so zone + free sessions combine cleanly. **free** - record any label at any time. Labels are drawn from whichever guided procedure was highlighted last. R=repeat, N=new label, ESC=finish. All captures append to one file. ### CSV format ``` ts_ms,label,rssi,ch,a00,a01,...,a55 ``` 56 LLTF HT20 subcarrier amplitudes per row. Transition rows (null label steps) are never written. ### data collection strategy - **Active injection on** (press P before starting) - gives stable 10 fps regardless of ambient traffic. Passive mode fps is unpredictable and makes temporal features unreliable. - **Multiple sessions** - collect at least 5-10 runs of each procedure in each environment. CSI fingerprints are highly environment-specific: furniture, people walking past, even temperature changes can shift them. - **Vary conditions** - different times of day, different people, door open vs closed. A model trained in one rigid condition will not generalise. - **Session naming** - name sessions meaningfully. There is no RTC on the ESP32; timestamps are milliseconds since boot and are useless across sessions. - **Check ChanOcc first** - use the channel occupation view to confirm your AP is active and delivering consistent fps on the chosen channel before starting a training session. ## file manager Browse and delete files on the SD card without removing it from the device. Access via key 9 from the menu. - W/S or arrow keys: scroll through files and directories - Enter or D: open a directory / confirm delete for a file - A or Back: go up one directory level - ESC or M: back to the menu Selecting a file shows a delete-confirm screen. Only deletion is supported - CSV data files are not meant to be edited on-device. WiFi is stopped while the file manager is open. ## ML pipeline *(work in progress)* The firmware collects labelled CSV data. What you do with it on a PC and how you eventually run inference on the device is covered in **[ML_PIPELINE.md](ML_PIPELINE.md)**. Short version: each frame is 56 subcarrier amplitudes. With enough labelled sessions you can train a small 1D CNN, quantize it to int8, and deploy it on the ESP32-S3 via ESP-DL (Espressif's native inference library, exploits S3 SIMD) or TFLite Micro as a fallback. The fingerprint is environment-specific - expect to retrain per deployment. On-device inference is the planned next step, not yet implemented. ## why the DC null gap in the spectrum OFDM WiFi reserves subcarrier 32 as a DC null. Subcarriers 0-3 and 61-63 are guard bands. The gap in the middle of the spectrum view is expected and correct. ## build Dependencies are vendored in `lib/`. No internet required at build time. ```sh pio run -e m5-cardputer-adv # build pio run -e m5-cardputer-adv -t upload # build + flash ``` The pre-build script `scripts/patch_libnet80211.py` weakens the `ieee80211_raw_frame_sanity_check` symbol in the ESP32 WiFi library so that `esp_wifi_80211_tx()` accepts all management frame subtypes. The patch is idempotent and survives incremental builds. Output binary: `bin/non-magical-csi--.bin` (factory merged, flash at 0x0). ## serial commands ``` csi start [ch] start CSI on channel (default 1) csi stop stop csi scan scan for nearby APs csi ap lock onto scanned AP (sets BSSID filter) csi ch change channel csi active start start active probe injection csi active stop stop injection csi info frame count, fps, per-subcarrier stats los start begin LOS sequence (countdown -> calibrate -> scan) los stop stop los recal recalibrate baseline mode [los|spec|var|motion|corr|console] switch view from terminal log [0-3] get/set log verbosity (0=off 1=err 2=info 3=dbg) beep [hz] [ms] test speaker ``` ## references - ESP32 CSI Toolkit - Hernandez & Kubisch (2021) - espressif/esp-csi - Espressif Systems (2023) - espressif/esp-dl - Espressif Systems (2024) - WiSee: Whole-Home Gesture Recognition - Patel et al., MobiCom 2013 - LLTF subcarrier mapping - ESP-IDF wifi_csi_info_t documentation"}

firmwares.firmwareDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"# Tab5-Launchpad

![Tab5-Launchpad](docs/previews/hero.png)

A dedicated firmware for the [M5Stack Tab5](https://docs.m5stack.com/en/core/Tab5)
(ESP32-P4) that turns its touchscreen into a class-compliant USB-MIDI grid
controller — six playing modes, live value readouts, and a flat,
professional UI, with zero DAW-specific lock-in: it's generic MIDI, so it
works with whatever you already use (map it in your DAW's own MIDI-learn,
the same way you'd map any controller).

All images on this page are real renders of the actual firmware code — the
project ships a native Linux preview tool (`tools/build-launchpad-preview.sh`)
that links the real rendering source against a software framebuffer, so
these aren't mockups.

## Features

- **Six modes**, one grid: **Notes** (chromatic, 3 layout sizes), **Drums**
  (GM percussion map, auto-selects MIDI channel 10), **Faders** (CC20-27,
  relative touch drag, live value readout), **XY** (CC1 + CC74, a soft
  glowing touch point, absolute position), **Macros** (CC102-117, 16 relative
  rotary knobs), **Looper** (4-track, records/replays whatever you play in
  any mode, per-track overdub, visual BPM metronome, can also capture MIDI
  from a connected host — see below).
- **Every control shows its real value and CC/note assignment on screen** —
  no memorizing a mapping, no guessing what a fader is currently at.
- **Large, dedicated channel picker** (not a cramped always-on strip) — 16
  full-size buttons, one tap to switch.
- **Panic button** — Sustain Off, All Notes Off, All Sound Off, across every
  channel actually used this session, with send-failure feedback.
- **Honest connection state** — the firmware only ever claims what it
  actually knows (USB enumerated vs. not), never implies a DAW is listening
  just because the OS sees the device.
- **Real double-buffered, vsync-synced rendering** — no tearing, every
  frame fully repainted.
- **Class-compliant USB-MIDI device**, always on from boot. Plug in, your
  DAW/synth/whatever sees a standard MIDI input — no driver, no DAW-specific
  plugin.

## How to use

### Home

Boots to a small home screen: open the controller, or check Settings /
Diagnostics.

![Home screen](docs/previews/12_home_landscape.png)

### Notes

Tap pads to play. The footer's dimension button cycles grid size (8x4 /
8x2 / 4x4); the channel button opens the full-screen picker; Panic clears
stuck notes instantly.

![Notes mode](docs/previews/02_note_pressed.png)

### Drums

Fixed 4x4 GM percussion layout. Switching into this mode auto-selects MIDI
channel 10 — the convention essentially every GM/GS/XG-aware synth and DAW
expects for drums — still overridable from the channel picker afterward.

![Drums mode, pads held](docs/previews/04_drum_pressed.png)

### Faders

Four real touch faders (CC20-27 depending on variant). Press anywhere in a
column to grab it, drag to change the value — the fader won't jump just
because you touched it.

![Faders mode](docs/previews/05_mixer_cc.png)

### XY

The whole pad is one continuous surface: X → CC1 (mod wheel), Y → CC74
(filter cutoff/brightness) — both conventional, DAW/synth-recognized CC
assignments. A soft glow tracks your touch instead of a hard crosshair.

![XY mode](docs/previews/06_xy_center.png)

### Macros

Up to 16 rotary knobs (CC102-117). Press and drag **vertically** to turn —
relative drag, not absolute angle, since a flat touchscreen has no
detents to make angle-based turning reliable.

![Macros mode](docs/previews/10_knob_variant0.png)

### Looper

**4 independent tracks.** Tap a track button (T1-T4) to select which one
Record/Play/Clear target — the other three keep doing whatever they were
already doing (playing, recording, paused) regardless of which one is
selected, so you can layer tracks: record a part on track 1, let it loop,
select track 2, record over the top of it, and so on.

Tap **Record** to start capturing on the selected track, tap it again to
close the loop at whatever length you just played (it starts looping
immediately). Switch to another mode and keep playing — the loop keeps
going underneath. Tap Record again while it's playing to **overdub**
(layers new material into that track without erasing it); tap again to
stop adding. **Play/Stop** pauses and resumes from exactly where it left
off, not from the start. **Clear** wipes the selected track only.

Each track records whatever you play locally in *any* mode, **and** MIDI
received from a connected host/DAW while that track is armed — so you can
loop something your DAW sends back to the device, not just what you play
on the pads.

A BPM readout with +/- buttons and a pulsing beat indicator give a visual
tempo reference — purely a feel aid, it does not quantize or snap
recording/playback to a grid.

![Looper mode, 4 tracks, mixed states](docs/previews/17_looper_multitrack.png)

### Channel picker

A dedicated full-screen picker (not a cramped strip) — large, legible
touch targets for all 16 MIDI channels.

![Channel picker](docs/previews/11_channel_selector.png)

### Settings

![Settings screen](docs/previews/13_settings_landscape.png)

### Diagnostics

Live hardware/USB health — chip, memory, battery, SD, panel, and detected
peripherals.

![Diagnostics screen](docs/previews/14_diagnostics_landscape.png)

## MIDI mapping reference

Exact note/CC numbers, value formulas, and per-mode variant tables:
[`docs/midi-mapping.md`](docs/midi-mapping.md).

| Mode | Message | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Notes | Note On/Off | Fixed velocity 100 (no pressure sensing on this touch panel) |
| Drums | Note On/Off | GM percussion map, fixed velocity 110, channel 10 by default |
| Faders | CC 20-27 | Continuous, relative drag |
| XY | CC 1 + CC 74 | Absolute touch position, holds last value on release |
| Macros | CC 102-117 | Relative vertical drag |
| Looper | (replays recorded messages) | Not its own message type — re-sends whatever was captured, locally or from the host, into the selected track |

MIDI channel is set entirely by the device (via the channel picker) — the
host never negotiates or assigns it; it just listens on whichever channel
its MIDI input is pointed at. 16 channels is a hard MIDI 1.0 protocol
limit, not a firmware restriction.

## Building

Stock ESP-IDF project (tested against 5.5.4):

```sh
idf.py build
idf.py -p /dev/ttyACM0 flash monitor
```

Requires a real ESP-IDF 5.5.4 install (`. $IDF_PATH/export.sh` before the
commands above) — this is a stock IDF project, nothing project-specific
needed beyond that. Known gap worth knowing about: some sandboxed/offline
setups fetch an `esptool` that predates ESP32-P4 support; if
`elf2image`/flashing fails with `invalid choice: 'esp32p4'`, you need an
esptool ≥ 5.x ahead of it on `PATH`.

Iterate on the screen's visuals without hardware at all:

```sh
./tools/build-launchpad-preview.sh   # writes real rendered frames to launchpad-preview/
```

A `perf` command is also available over the serial console (any terminal
at 115200 baud) — calls the real draw+present path directly per mode,
unthrottled, and reports timing. Useful if you're chasing a performance
question on your own hardware.

## Architecture notes

- `main/launchpad_modes.c/.h` — pure pad/CC-index → MIDI-message mapping,
  no platform dependency at all.
- `main/launchpad_controller.c/.h` — portable touch-ownership, note
  lifecycle, per-mode channel/layout recall, panic, transport-error state,
  and the Looper's 4-track recording/playback engine. Also platform-free,
  unit-testable natively.
- `main/launchpad_grid.c/.h` + `main/studio_ui.c/.h` — rendering and
  hit-testing, built on antialiased proportional type instead of a bitmap
  font. Every screen does a full repaint every frame it presents — required
  by the real double-buffered display pipeline (`main/display.c`); a
  partial/dirty-region redraw would desync the two alternating hardware
  framebuffers. Text renders via a composed-glyph blit (`su_text()` →
  `sgfx_blit()` → `display.c`'s `set_window`/`write_pixels`), not one fill
  call per antialiasing run.
- `main/launchpad_app.c` — the one ESP-IDF-specific file: touch polling,
  frame pacing, host MIDI receive polling (feeds the Looper's host-capture
  path), wiring the portable controller to real hardware.
- `main/usb_midi_device.c/.h` — always-on class-compliant USB-MIDI device
  (TinyUSB), no host mode of any kind.
- `lib/SIC`, `lib/SGFX`, `lib/konsole` — vendored hardware-abstraction,
  graphics, and console libraries (board bring-up, MIPI-DSI panel driving,
  serial CLI)."}

firmwares.firmwareDescription: {"format":"markdown","content":"PocketLab is an offline, privacy-focused Wi-Fi and Bluetooth learning toolkit for the M5StickS3. It includes a local WebUI, Cyber Academy checklist, Wi-Fi signal and channel analyzer, BLE inventory, Bluetooth keyboard tester, file vault, battery monitoring, and expandable networking glossary. PocketLab does not crack passwords, disconnect devices, attack networks, upload telemetry, or require internet access. Cyber Academy measurements and checklist progress remain temporary unless the user explicitly saves a survey from the main tools page. Public beta: additional improvements and compatibility updates are planned. Use only with equipment and networks you own or have permission to examine. Important: installing this factory firmware erases existing applications, files, baselines, and settings on the device."}

currentVersion.versionDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"## v0.17.0 Public Beta

Hardware-tested quality-of-life update for PocketLab on the M5StickS3.

### What’s new

- Cyber Academy checklist steps now complete automatically as activities are performed
- Added session-only room comparison for checking Wi-Fi coverage
- Shows median, strongest, weakest, and sample-count readings for each room
- Automatically highlights the room with the weakest median signal
- Shows the selected network’s security mode in the signal explorer
- Prevents browsers from displaying an outdated cached WebUI after upgrading

### Privacy and safety

Room names, signal measurements, and Cyber Academy progress remain only in browser memory. They are not transmitted to PocketLab or saved to the device, and they clear when the page is refreshed or closed.

PocketLab does not crack passwords, disconnect devices, attack networks, or upload telemetry. Use it only with equipment and networks you own or have permission to examine.

### Installation note

This factory image is for the M5Stack StickS3 only. Installing it at offset `0x0000` erases existing firmware, PocketLab files, saved baselines, and settings."}

{"format":"markdown","content":"**CardCast 将 M5Cardputer 变成便携式 Wi-Fi 麦克风，通过局域网将内置麦克风采集的声音实时传输到手机或电脑浏览器，无需安装额外应用。**

- 16 kHz、16 位单声道音频，通过 WebSocket 实时传输。
- 内置网页播放器，支持中英文切换、动态音频可视化及播放状态统计。
- 自动扫描 Wi-Fi，使用设备键盘完成配置，支持 DHCP 和静态 IP，并保存最近一次成功连接的网络设置。
- 支持断线自动重连与播放缓冲调节，减少音频延迟累积。
- 串流页面闲置 60 秒后自动关闭背光，按任意键唤醒，音频传输持续运行。

使用方法：开机后选择并连接 Wi-Fi，在同一局域网的手机或电脑上打开设备屏幕显示的网址即可收听。若浏览器未自动播放，点击页面播放提示。目前仅支持一个浏览器同时收听。

**CardCast turns your M5Cardputer into a portable Wi-Fi microphone, streaming live audio from its built-in microphone to a phone or computer browser over your local network. No additional app is required.**

- Streams 16 kHz, 16-bit mono audio over WebSocket.
- Includes a built-in web player with Chinese and English interfaces, live audio visualization, and playback statistics.
- Automatically scans for Wi-Fi and provides keyboard-based setup, with DHCP, static IP, and saved settings for the most recently connected network.
- Features automatic reconnection and adaptive playback buffering to reduce delay buildup.
- Turns off the streaming screen’s backlight after 60 seconds of keyboard inactivity. Press any key to wake it while audio streaming continues.

Getting started: Select and connect to Wi-Fi, then open the address shown on the device in a browser on the same local network. If playback does not start automatically, tap the play prompt. Currently supports one listener at a time."}

{"format":"markdown","content":"![](assets/beamstalker-bg.png)

Knowledge should be free 🏴‍☠️

# BeamStalker BeamStalker is a modular embedded RF experimentation firmware built around a shared UI, service, and backend abstraction layer. It targets multiple boards with very different displays and input methods while keeping the user experience, command surface, and internal app model consistent across targets. BeamStalker was initially bootstrapped from the [Neutrino](https://github.com/st4lk3r-unit/neutrino) firmware skeleton, then heavily extended into its own multi-target RF platform. ## 🖥️ Supported targets | Target | Status | Display | Input | Notes | |---|---:|---|---|---| | `native` | ✅ | SDL2 desktop window | keyboard | Linux debug target | | `native-headless` | ✅ | none | konsole / stdin | headless Linux target | | `esp32s3-tpager` | ✅ | 480×222 ST7796 | keyboard + encoder | main handheld target | | `esp32s3-tdongle-s3` | ✅ | 160×80 ST7735 | single button | compact dongle target | | `esp32s3-cardputer` | ✅ | 240×135 ST7789 | keyboard | compact keyboard target | | `esp32s3-cardputer-adv` | ✅ | 240×135 ST7789 | TCA8418 keyboard | Cardputer-ADV target via updated SIC | | `esp32s3-heltec-v3` | ✅ | 128×64 SSD1306 | single button | minimal OLED target | > BeamStalker is multi-target by design, but not “universal” yet. > The goal is a shared firmware architecture across supported boards, not fake portability. ## 📡 Current wireless backends | Backend | Status | Notes | |---|---:|---| | Wi-Fi (ESP32) | ✅ | scan, capture, AP-style tooling, raw 802.11 features depending on target/backend | | BLE (ESP32) | ✅ | scan + advertisement tooling | | Native Linux | ✅ | debug / UI / service development target | | Other radio backends | 🚧 | planned through the abstraction layer | ## ✨ Features Current firmware features include: - multi-target UI with a shared navigation model - native Linux target for development and debugging - Wi-Fi scanning (passive AP discovery, RSSI-sorted) - Wi-Fi packet capture to `.pcap` (DLT_IEEE802_11) - Wi-Fi beacon spam - Wi-Fi deauth (broadcast + directed, configurable reason code) - WPA2 EAPOL handshake capture — passive sniff or deauth-triggered, writes hashcat-compatible `.pcap` (`-m 22000`) - captive portal (manual rogue AP) - evil twin (clone AP + CSA/deauth lure + portal) - honeypot (broadcast or targeted client lure + portal) - karma (probe-response injection + portal) - BLE scanning - BLE advertisement spam - on-device logs and status views - konsole command interface for full control without relying on the UI - structured SD card layout: all files under `BeamStalker/` with per-tool subfolders ## 🛠️ Build BeamStalker uses PlatformIO. ### Requirements Before building, make sure you clone the repository **with its submodules**: ```bash git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/st4lk3r-unit/BeamStalker.git cd BeamStalker/firmware ```` If you already cloned the repository without submodules: ```bash git submodule update --init --recursive ``` BeamStalker now expects the updated SIC revision that contains `sic_board_default()`, `sic_key_poll()`, `SIC_TARGET_CARDPUTER_ADV`, the fixed Cardputer-ADV TCA8418 map, and the newer ES8311/SD/IR board profiles. After pushing/pinning that SIC commit, update the submodule pointer: ```bash git submodule update --init --recursive cd firmware/lib/SIC git fetch origin git checkout cd ../../.. git add firmware/lib/SIC git commit -m "Bump SIC for Cardputer-ADV support" ``` You will also need: * Python * [PlatformIO](https://platformio.org/) * a supported toolchain for the selected target ### Build examples ```bash # native desktop pio run -e native # native headless pio run -e native-headless # LilyGO T-Pager pio run -e esp32s3-tpager # LilyGO T-Dongle-S3 pio run -e esp32s3-tdongle-s3 # M5Stack Cardputer pio run -e esp32s3-cardputer # M5Stack Cardputer-ADV pio run -e esp32s3-cardputer-adv # Heltec WiFi LoRa 32 V3 pio run -e esp32s3-heltec-v3 ``` ## ⚡ Flash After building, you can flash directly with PlatformIO: ```bash pio run -e esp32s3-tpager -t upload ``` You can also use [release binaries](https://github.com/st4lk3r-unit/BeamStalker/releases/latest) with external flashers, depending on the board and boot flow: * `esptool.py` * browser flashers such as [`esptool-js`](https://espressif.github.io/esptool-js/) * launchers such as [`M5Launcher`](https://github.com/bmorcelli/Launcher) where applicable ## 🎮 Controls BeamStalker exposes a common interaction model across targets even when the physical inputs differ. The abstract navigation model is built around: * **Up / Down / Left / Right** * **Enter / Confirm** * **Back** * optional extra shortcuts depending on the target This means a full keyboard target, a rotary target, and a single-button target can all drive the same UI logic. ### 🧭 UI mapping On keyboard-oriented targets, the default mental model is: * `W A S D` → navigate * `Enter` → confirm * `Backspace` → back Some targets also expose: * arrow keys * rotary encoder navigation * single-button navigation patterns * board-specific shortcuts where available ### ⌨️ Konsole BeamStalker can also be controlled through **Konsole**, a command-driven interface exposed over serial / console. This matters especially on targets where physical input is minimal or awkward, such as dongles and one-button boards. Konsole is meant to provide: * full target control without depending on the on-device UI * a better workflow for automation and testing * a path toward scripting and boot-time command execution later on ## 🙏 Acknowledgements / inspirations A few projects and people helped shape BeamStalker, directly or indirectly: * [st4lk3r-unit/neutrino](https://github.com/st4lk3r-unit/neutrino) for the original firmware template and early architectural groundwork * [@sdardouchi](https://github.com/sdardouchi) for the GitHub Pages work and the broader old-school phone / embedded scene around [OperationSE](https://github.com/OperationSE) * [@Eun0us](https://github.com/Eun0us) for research and ideas around ESP console workflows via [Shell-ESP32](https://github.com/Eun0us/Shell-ESP32) * [@bmorcelli](https://github.com/bmorcelli) for [M5Launcher](https://github.com/bmorcelli/Launcher) and related handheld firmware ecosystem work * [@pr3y](https://github.com/pr3y) for [Bruce Firmware](https://github.com/pr3y/Bruce) * [@7h30th3r0n3](https://github.com/7h30th3r0n3) for [Evil-M5Project](https://github.com/7h30th3r0n3/Evil-M5Project) * [@Spacehuhn](https://github.com/SpacehuhnTech) for prior art and research around ESP raw Wi-Fi tooling And to all the projects that pushed the scene forward: knowledge should be free 🏴‍☠️ *Made with fun by akpalanaza.*"}

firmwares.firmwareName: Silicon Bubbles - iMessage Client (needs BlueBubbles server)
firmwares.firmwareDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"## ⚠️ You need a Mac first

**This is a client, not a server.** It talks to
[BlueBubbles](https://bluebubbles.app/install/), the free open-source
iMessage bridge, which must be running on a **Mac (or Hackintosh / macOS
VM) signed into iMessage** and reachable from the Cardputer over LAN or
HTTPS.

No Mac, no messages — there is no way around Apple on this one. Setup
takes about ten minutes and their documentation is good. Validated
against **BlueBubbles server v1.9.9**.

## What it does

| | |
|---|---|
| **Conversations** | One entry per person, not per thread — duplicate SMS/iMessage threads are merged |
| **Bubbles** | Left/right alignment, tails, author grouping, time labels |
| **Emoji** | 42 hand-drawn 12×12 glyphs covering 68 codepoints — unknown ones get a clean placeholder, never tofu |
| **Tapbacks** | Reactions shown as a pill on the bubble corner |
| **Sending** | From the 56-key keyboard, with an honest *sent-but-unconfirmed* state |
| **Sounds** | Five synthesized struck-bar timbres, not beeps — each one switchable |
| **Bilingual** | English and French, switchable on the device or in the web portal |

Text only by design: attachments show as `[attachment]`. Polling only —
no Socket.IO, no webhooks.

## Setup, from your phone

First boot raises a WiFi access point and shows a **QR code**: scan it
with your phone camera, join, and the configuration portal opens by
itself. Afterwards the same portal lives at `http://cardputer.local`.

Everything is also editable **on the device**: WiFi network scan, server
address and password, language, sounds, refresh rate. Plus local contact
names (BlueBubbles does not expose the Mac's contacts), and
**backup/restore of all settings to microSD** — so the next firmware
flash doesn't cost you your configuration.

## Keys

| Key | List | Conversation | Compose | Settings |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `;` `.` | move | scroll, bubble by bubble | — | change field |
| `,` `/` | — | — | — | change value |
| `Enter` | open | write | send | open WiFi scan / server / QR / SD backup |
| `` ` `` | info | back | cancel | save and exit |
| `r` | resync | — | — | — |
| `n` | name the contact | — | — | — |
| `p` / `s` | *(info screen)* test server / settings | | | |

## Device support

Built and tested on the **Cardputer ADV** only — hence the `-ADV` suffix
in the version. The original Cardputer uses a different keyboard
controller and audio path; it may work, it is untested, and a report
either way would genuinely help.

## 🚧 Status: work in progress

This runs daily against exactly **one** setup: an ADV, a BlueBubbles
v1.9.9 server behind Cloudflare, French phone numbers. That is one data
point. If you try it on anything else — other country codes,
group-heavy accounts, self-signed TLS, ngrok — please open an issue and
say what worked and what didn't. Right now, reports from setups unlike
mine are worth more than any feature.

Source, documentation and error-code table (E11–E50) on GitHub, MIT:
<https://github.com/chatelp/silicon-bubbles-cardputeradv>

> **Flashing this erases existing device settings.** Silicon Bubbles can
> back its own settings up to microSD (Settings → Backup to SD) and offers
> to restore them on first boot."}

currentVersion.versionDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"### 0.19.0-ADV — first public release

Everything below is new; this is the first build published anywhere.

**Reading and writing**
- Conversation list that merges duplicate threads per person, with a
  calibration pass that learns who you actually talk to
- Chat bubbles, bubble-by-bubble scrolling, group sender labels,
  unsend and edit handling
- 42 pixel-art emoji glyphs (68 codepoints), tapbacks on bubble corners
- Sending with a tri-state result — a timeout never risks a double send

**Setup and mobility**
- QR code on first boot: the phone joins the access point and the
  configuration portal opens by itself
- WiFi network scan, server address and password editable on the device
- Local contact names, settings backup/restore to microSD
- Bilingual interface (EN/FR), five synthesized sounds, each switchable

**Reliability**
- Responses parsed as a stream straight off the TLS socket — no body is
  ever buffered (the device has ~31 KB of contiguous heap at runtime)
- Documented error codes E11–E50 instead of raw parser messages
- 34 native tests covering the HTTP decoders, UTF-8/emoji segmentation,
  scroll stops, tapback parsing and phone-number merge keys

Validated against BlueBubbles server v1.9.9, on a Cardputer ADV."}

firmwares.firmwareDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"A Yi Jing casting device, not another tool.

Six lines, cast one by one the traditional three-coin way. Then the figure,
the figure it is tending toward, and a text to sit with — portrait,
Judgment, Image, and the meaning of each of the six lines. English and
French, entirely offline.

> **Built and tested on the Cardputer ADV only.** The place reading relies
> on the ADV's Wi-Fi and the device list here does not distinguish models —
> hence the `-ADV` suffix on the version.

## Reading the place

Before each casting the device listens to the room. A passive Wi-Fi scan —
never connected, radio off the moment it ends, no SSID or BSSID kept,
nothing stored or transmitted — becomes a living particle field on screen,
one dot per network, and it gently weights the draw.

| Reading | Derived from | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| **density** | network count + mean signal energy | leans yin or yang, **± 5 % at most** |
| **agitation** | channel spread + signal variance | makes changing lines likelier, **+ 4 % at most** |

Bounded, documented, on by default, and switchable off in the settings.

Press `w` at any moment for the raw numbers — networks, channels, dBm, both
readings, both weights, and the resulting probabilities of the four line
values. If something influences a draw, you should be able to audit exactly
how much.

```
P(yang)     = 0.5  + B     B = (density - 0.5) x 0.1   in [-0.05, +0.05]
P(changing) = 0.25 + G     G = agitation x 0.04        in [0, 0.04]
```

At B = G = 0 this is exactly the traditional 1/8, 3/8, 3/8, 1/8. Randomness
comes from `esp_random()`, the ESP32 hardware TRNG — no network, no account,
no AI, no cloud.

## Keys

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `space` | begin, cast a line, continue |
| `←` `→` | first figure / complementary figure |
| `↓` | full text, then pages, then trigram structure |
| `↑` | back through the pages |
| `l` | English / French |
| `h` | built-in help |
| `s` | settings — place reading, sounds, volume |
| `w` | technical view of the field |
| `esc` | back |

Soft PCM interface sounds, all switchable, with three volume levels.

## Source and method

MIT licensed, with the full casting specification and a desktop SDL
simulator that runs the exact same rendering code:
<https://github.com/chatelp/daoa-mini-cardputeradv>

Daoa Mini is a companion object for **Daoa**, my Yi Jing app for iPhone and
Android: <https://daoa.app>

I designed and directed this project; Claude Code wrote most of the
implementation. The scope, the product decisions, the visual direction and
all validation on real hardware are mine. The casting logic and the
probability maths are covered by tests anyone can run."}

firmwares.firmwareName: Silicon Casino - Slots Blackjack Poker Roulette
firmwares.firmwareDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"Slots, blackjack, video poker and roulette on a Cardputer. **Virtual
chips only** — no real money, no purchases, no account, no network of any
kind. You cannot be ruined: the house refills an empty balance. The
randomness is the ESP32 hardware TRNG.

### The five games

| Game | Rules | Return |
|---|---|---|
| Slots 3×1 | 8 symbols, one payline, pair-left pays ×2 | **95.24 %** |
| Video slot 5×3 | five paylines, its own reel strip | **94.95 %** per line |
| Blackjack | 3:2, dealer stands on all 17, double, no split | **95.81 %** |
| Video poker | Jacks or Better **9/6**, max-bet royal 800:1 | 9/6 full pay |
| Roulette | European, single zero, ten bet kinds | **97.3 %** on every bet |

The odds are computed, not tuned. Video poker is checked against all
**2,598,960** possible five-card hands, every roulette bet settles at
exactly **972,973 ppm** across the 37 pockets, and the slots return comes
analytically from the reel strips. 136 native tests in the repository
lock all of it — if a strip or a paytable drifts, the build fails.

### Keys

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `space` / `enter` | spin, deal, draw, launch the ball |
| **shake the device** | pulls the lever — launches the roulette ball too |
| `,` `/` | change bet, or move the cursor in a hand |
| `;` `.` | navigate the lobby, pick a roulette number |
| `1`…`9` `0` | house credit, +10 to +100, anywhere |
| `h` | help — general in the lobby, game rules in a game |
| `s` | settings · `l` leaderboard · `a` about |
| `` ` `` | back — works any time, even mid-hand |

### What makes it this device's casino

Everything is electronics. The slot cabinet is a printed circuit board
with mounting holes and vias, the blackjack felt is routed like one with
silkscreen, and the roulette wheel rides a rotary encoder marked
**RE1 — 37 detents**, one per pocket. While the reels spin, the bottom of
the screen is an oscilloscope trace that loses sync and tears whenever a
reel locks. Reel symbols are floppy, CRT, chip, invader — with a `GLYPHS`
setting that restores cherries and bells. Same paytable either way.

One balance shared by all five games, bets remembered per player and per
game, up to 8 players on a persistent leaderboard. Left idle for twelve
seconds, any game slips into a grey, free attract demo until you touch a
key. An arcade boot sequence opens the firmware, and its fake self-test
shows **real** hardware numbers — checked against the board definition
and the drivers actually instantiated.

### Tested on

Built and tested on the **Cardputer ADV**, which is what this listing
targets. It also runs on the original Cardputer — a player uses it
there — but the shake-to-spin lever needs the ADV's IMU; without it,
use `space`. Owners of the original model can flash the very same build
from the GitHub release linked below.

Source, desktop SDL simulator and full documentation, MIT licensed with
the pixel art included:
<https://github.com/chatelp/geek-casino-cardputeradv>

Built with Claude Code, directed and tested by a human. Nothing AI runs
on the device — press `a` in the lobby and it says so itself."}

currentVersion.versionDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"### 1.1 — the slot pays when the reels land

Fixes the first bug reported by a player (r/CardPuter, with a video and
exact numbers: 965 chips, 5 bet, 10 won).

The 3-reel slot credited the win **the moment you pressed spin**, in the
same instant as taking the bet. The balance already contained the payout
by the time the reels landed, so the celebration announced a win that had
nothing left to add — the spin looked like it paid nothing.

A spin is now two declared moments: the stake leaves on the press, the
win lands when the last reel stops and climbs with the celebration. Only
the 3-reel slot was affected — the video slot, blackjack, poker and
roulette already settled at the end.

No test was watching the balance *during* a spin, which is exactly why
this shipped. One now does, and it fails on the old behaviour.

The boot ROM line reads **V1.1** — that is how you check what you have.

Flashing this package erases the saved players, balances and leaderboard
(it rewrites the whole flash, NVS included)."}

{"format":"markdown","content":"PocketBoy S3 turns the M5Stack StickS3 into a private, offline GB/GBC homebrew gaming system.

The StickS3 creates its own Wi-Fi network and hosts the complete WebUI, game library, and save backup. Games run locally in Google Chrome on a connected phone or tablet—no native app, internet connection, cloud account, or telemetry required.

### Features

- Plays legally obtained homebrew `.gb` and `.gbc` games
- On-device game library with 2 MiB of dedicated storage
- DualSense, Xbox One, and touchscreen controls
- Controller-only landscape fullscreen with L2 toggle
- Browser audio with volume and mute controls
- Save states and battery-backed game saves
- Dedicated 1 MiB save-backup partition
- Save synchronization between Chrome and the StickS3
- Portable save export/import for moving between devices
- Battery level, charging status, Wi-Fi credentials, and join QR display
- Offline and private operation

PocketBoy S3 uses the open-source binjgb WebAssembly emulator. No commercial ROMs, copyrighted game data, or console firmware are included. Please use only games you created or have permission to use."}

{"format":"markdown","content":"## OrcDial 0.1.0-beta.1 — Initial public testing beta

Turn your M5Stack Dial into an optional wireless controller for OrcSDR on the M5Stack Tab5.

- Dashboard-aware encoder, button and touch controls.
- Home VFO with tuning keypad and supported frequency, mode, step, span, filter and volume adjustments.
- FT8 receive controls when supported by the connected OrcSDR firmware.
- Secure pairing with persistent trust and automatic reconnection.
- Dial Settings for pairing, connection status, display and knob preferences.
- Firmware version and source identity shown in About and serial startup.

### Compatibility and pairing

Requires OrcSDR firmware with pairing protocol 4. The protocol-compatible receiver snapshot is OrcSDR nightly commit `0b8be74`; exact-build hardware pairing remains unverified.

Open **Settings → Accessories & Companion** on the Tab5 and **Dial Settings → Pairing** on the Dial. Compare the six-digit codes and confirm on **both devices**.

Do not mix this release with the earlier protocol-3 OrcDial prototype.

### Installation and beta limitations

M5Burner installation resets the Dial’s saved settings and pairing. Pair again after installation.

Firmware builds, automated tests and package checks passed. Exact-image installation, pairing, recovery, prolonged operation and independent security acceptance remain open. Please report issues with the VERSION and SOURCE shown in About."}

currentVersion.versionDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"## 0.1.0-beta.1 — Initial Public Beta

The first public testing release of OrcDial for the **M5Stack Dial**, an optional wireless controller for **OrcSDR on M5Stack Tab5**.

### Included in this release

- Dashboard-aware controls using the encoder, button and touch display.
- Home VFO with a tuning keypad and frequency, mode, step, span, filter and volume adjustments where supported by OrcSDR.
- FT8 receive controls when supported by the connected receiver.
- Secure pairing, saved device trust and automatic reconnection.
- Dial Settings for pairing, connection status, display brightness, sleep and knob preferences.
- Firmware version and source commit displayed in **About** and reported at serial startup.

### Compatibility and pairing

Requires **OrcSDR pairing protocol 4**. OrcSDR nightly commit `0b8be74` has matching protocol and secure-session sources; exact-build pairing has not yet been verified on hardware.

To pair:

1. Open **Settings → Accessories & Companion** on the Tab5.
2. Open **Dial Settings → Pairing** on the Dial.
3. Start pairing, compare the six-digit codes and confirm on **both devices**.

This release is incompatible with the earlier protocol-3 OrcDial prototype.

### Installation

**M5Burner installation resets the Dial’s saved settings and pairing.** Configure the Dial and pair it with the Tab5 again after installation.

### Beta status

Firmware builds, automated tests and package checks passed. Exact-image installation, pairing, recovery, prolonged operation and independent security acceptance remain open.

Please include the **VERSION** and **SOURCE** shown in About when reporting an issue.

[Release assets and source](https://github.com/hardcoreerik/OrcDial/releases/tag/orcdial-v0.1.0-beta.1)"}

firmwares.firmwareDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"# MORPHASE — 4-Operator FM Polyphonic Synthesizer

**Standard build** (Unit MIDI / DIN, 12 voices)

Firmware that turns the Cardputer ADV into a 12-note polyphonic FM synth that you play from a MIDI keyboard. The Cardputer is not the keyboard: it is the editor and controller for the sound.

> Want to play over Bluetooth MIDI from an iPhone / iPad, or don't have a Unit MIDI? Use **MORPHASE BLE** instead.

## Key features

- 4-operator FM with 14 algorithms
- Waveform morphing: each operator slides smoothly through 8 waveforms
- Patch morph: move between patches lined up in 8 slots, blending everything
- GLITCH: repeat, reverse, chop, or knock the tone off for a moment
- Theremin (Unit ToF4M): wave your hand to move the sound, or play notes by hand height
- Tilt the unit (IMU) to change the tone; MIDI Learn
- Arpeggiator with STEP patterns; FX (Crush / Chorus / Delay / Reverb / Drive)
- 32 factory patches, ready to play

## What you need

- M5Stack Cardputer ADV (the original Cardputer is not supported)
- A MIDI keyboard + **Unit MIDI** on the Grove port (DIP switch = **BYPASS**, Grove 5V switch = **5VOUT**)
- A microSD card (for patches and settings)
- Earphones (the built-in speaker barely reproduces low notes)

## Manuals (English / Japanese, with PDFs)

https://github.com/oldtokage-collab/MORPHASE

Made by @Tokagetchi / Code by Claude (Anthropic) / License: CC BY-NC-SA 4."}

{"format":"markdown","content":"# MORPHASE BLE — 4-Operator FM Polyphonic Synthesizer

**BLE build** (Bluetooth MIDI + Unit MIDI / DIN, 10 voices)

Firmware that turns the Cardputer ADV into a 10-note polyphonic FM synth that you play over **Bluetooth MIDI** from an iPhone / iPad, Mac or PC — or from a MIDI keyboard through a Unit MIDI, both at once. The Cardputer is not the keyboard: it is the editor and controller for the sound.

> Bluetooth uses memory and CPU time, so this build plays 10 notes instead of 12. If you only play through a Unit MIDI, **MORPHASE** (Standard) gives you 12.

## Key features

- 4-operator FM with 14 algorithms
- Waveform morphing: each operator slides smoothly through 8 waveforms
- Patch morph: move between patches lined up in 8 slots, blending everything
- GLITCH: repeat, reverse, chop, or knock the tone off for a moment
- Theremin (Unit ToF4M): wave your hand to move the sound, or play notes by hand height
- Tilt the unit (IMU) to change the tone; MIDI Learn
- Arpeggiator with STEP patterns; FX (Crush / Chorus / Delay / Reverb / Drive)
- 32 factory patches, ready to play

## Connecting over Bluetooth

The unit appears as a Bluetooth MIDI device named **MORPHASE**. Connect **from inside an app** (tested: KeyPad on iPhone / iPad), not from the phone's Bluetooth settings. On a Mac, use Audio MIDI Setup → MIDI Studio → Bluetooth.

## What you need

- M5Stack Cardputer ADV (the original Cardputer is not supported)
- An app or device that sends Bluetooth MIDI, and/or a MIDI keyboard + Unit MIDI (DIP = **BYPASS**, Grove 5V = **5VOUT**)
- A microSD card (for patches and settings)
- Earphones (the built-in speaker barely reproduces low notes)

## Manuals (English / Japanese, with PDFs)

https://github.com/oldtokage-collab/MORPHASE

Made by @Tokagetchi / Code by Claude (Anthropic) / License: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0"}

{"format":"markdown","content":"```
MeshWatch turns an M5Stack StickS3 into a passive counter-surveillance scanner
and an off-grid MeshCore messenger — no phone required.

It listens on WiFi and BLE (it never transmits at the devices it detects) and
flags, with a confidence score, sound and an on-screen banner:

• Flock Safety ALPR cameras, Penguin battery packs and Raven gunshot sensors
• Axon body cameras / Tasers and other law-enforcement gear
• Item trackers — AirTag / Find My, Tile, Samsung SmartTag, Chipolo, Google FMD
  (warns when one has been following you)
• Consumer & CCTV WiFi cameras — Ring, Wyze, Reolink, Hikvision, Dahua, Arlo…
• Drones broadcasting Remote ID (WiFi and BLE)
• Rogue access points (karma / Pineapple-style SSID floods)
• Attack tools — Flipper Zero (incl. BadKB), BLE advertisement spam, Pwnagotchi
• Card-skimmer Bluetooth modules, WiFi deauth floods, iBeacon / Eddystone
• MeshCore and Meshtastic radios

Messaging & field tools
• Pair a MeshCore companion radio over Bluetooth and read/send mesh messages
  right from the stick — channels and contacts, with preset quick-replies.
• Signal finder with a CLOSER/FARTHER direction cue to walk a device down.
• Baseline watch: learn a safe area, then alert on anything new.
• Evidence log saved to flash (survives reboot), optionally geotagged.
• Stealth mode, auto-report to the mesh, team alerts, and a device lock with a
  duress wipe code.

Controls: two buttons. A = select, B = next, hold B = next screen / back.

Detection is for passive, defensive use only. An empty screen is not proof that
an area is free of surveillance. Signatures adapted from the flock-you and
nyanBOX projects; camera OUIs from the public IEEE registry.

Source & docs: https://github.com/Korrie71/meshwatch
```"}

给住校学生用的桌面天气预报机（M5Stack StickS3 / ESP32-S3）。

## 功能
- 🕐 **横屏时钟**：时间 + 农历 + 干支（丙午马年 戊戌月 丁巳日 九月初一）
- 📅 **7 个天气页**：今日 · 未来5天 · 防晒指数 · 生活提示 · 24小时趋势 · 空气质量 · 洗晒指数
- 🎨 **动态天气图标**：太阳旋转、雨点下落、雪花飘、雷电闪烁

- 🎙 **离线语音播报**：气温/天气/体感/湿度/风速/紫外线/带伞提醒（普通话/English，男声/女声）
- ⚠️ **天气预警**：高温/严寒/降雨/雷电/大雾/大风/重污染/极强紫外线
