firmwares.firmwareDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"# non magical csi - v2.2 > no magical radar Firmware for the M5Stack Cardputer that reads raw WiFi Channel State Information (CSI) from the ESP32-S3 radio, visualises it in real time, collects labelled training data for on-device ML models, and manages those files on-device. Built for studying what CSI actually is. For demo and educational purposes.

Knowledge should be free

## what it is When your ESP32 receives a WiFi frame, the hardware records how each OFDM subcarrier was attenuated and phase-shifted by the environment - that is the channel state. When something moves through the room, multipath reflections change, and those measurements change too. This firmware captures those measurements, draws them live on screen, runs a motion detector on top, guides you through structured data-collection sessions to build ML training datasets, and lets you browse and manage the collected files directly on the device. ## what it is not - Not radar. There is no angle, no distance, no localisation. - Not reliable for fine-grained gestures with a single AP. - Not a finished product. Calibration drifts. Environment changes break it. - Not magic. Every effect you see has a boring RF explanation. **Passive mode** frame rate depends on ambient WiFi traffic: beacons give ~10 fps per AP on the channel, data traffic adds more. Up to ~50 fps near an active device. **Active injection mode** sends 802.11 Probe Request frames at 10 Hz with per-frame SA MAC rotation, causing the target AP to reply with Probe Responses. Rate is intentionally kept at 10 Hz to avoid exhausting the AP's per-source-address rate-limit bucket. Frame injection uses a libnet80211 symbol-weakening patch (wsl_bypasser technique) applied at build time via `scripts/patch_libnet80211.py`. ## hardware **Primary**: M5Stack Cardputer ADV - ESP32-S3, ST7789 240x135, TCA8418 keyboard, ES8311 codec **Secondary**: M5Stack Cardputer v1/v1.1 - NS4168 amp, 74HC138 keyboard matrix ## views | key | view | |-----|------| | 1 | LOS - calibrated disturbance detector with audio alert | | 2 | Spectrum - amplitude waterfall per subcarrier | | 3 | Variance - which subcarriers fluctuate most | | 4 | Motion - scalar score + sparkline history | | 5 | Correlation - cross-subcarrier coherence | | 6 | ChanOcc - passive per-channel frame-rate survey | | 7 | Console - serial terminal mirrored on screen | | 8 | Training - guided ML data-collection session | | 9 | Files - SD card file browser | Navigation: arrow keys or WASD. ESC / backspace = back to menu. WiFi is stopped automatically when in the menu or Files view to save power. It restarts the moment you enter any sensing mode. **Global keys** (work in all modes): - **C** = cycle channel 1->2->...->13->1 - **+/-** = channel up/down - **P** = toggle active / passive injection (not available in Console or ChanOcc) - **ESC / M** = back to menu ## LOS detector Press **F** to scan for APs, select one, stand still during calibration, three ascending beeps = armed. Measures how much frame-to-frame channel differences exceed the calibrated baseline (z-score on differential amplitude). Score 0-100. **Calibration** collects a baseline in passive mode (80 frames, ~40-80 s) or active injection mode (100 frames, ~10 s at 10 fps). **Active injection** is on by default. Press **P** in any sensing mode (LOS, Spectrum, Variance, Motion, Corr, Training) to toggle between active and passive. ChanOcc is always passive. In LOS mode: **F** = scan APs, **P** = toggle active/passive, **R** = recalibrate, **C** = cycle channel, **Q** = quit. In Spectrum / Variance mode: **R** = reset waterfall history, **C** = cycle channel, **P** = toggle active/passive. **Audio alerts** - Geiger-counter style: beep rate scales continuously with score. Below 20 = silence. | Score | Beep rate | Tone | |-------|-----------|------| | 20-35 | 2 Hz | 800 Hz | | 35-50 | 5 Hz | 950 Hz | | 50-65 | 11 Hz | 1200 Hz | | 65-80 | 22 Hz | 1500 Hz | | >80 | 22 Hz | 2000 Hz | ## channel occupation (ChanOcc) Passive ambient survey. Hops through channels 1-13, dwelling 500 ms per channel (100 ms hardware settle + 400 ms count window). Displays passive frame-rate as horizontal bars for all 13 channels simultaneously. - Bars are auto-scaled to the **historical peak** seen this session - scale never shrinks. - A white tick marks the per-channel peak on each bar. - Stale fps values (zero on current sweep) are shown dimmed in grey. - **P** toggles active/passive injection. In passive mode, beacon frames are the main signal source (~10 fps per AP). In active mode, broadcast probe requests are sent on each channel during the dwell window, prompting probe responses from nearby APs and increasing the count. - OFDM beacons/responses (802.11g/n, >=6 Mbps) produce valid CSI; legacy DSSS frames (802.11b, 1 Mbps) do not. ## training mode Guided structured data-collection sessions that produce labelled CSV files for ML training. ### workflow 1. Enter Training (key 8) 2. Choose a procedure with W/S, press Enter 3. Type a session name (alphanumeric, `_`, `-`; Enter to confirm; ESC to cancel) 4. Follow the on-screen instructions - audio cues tell you when to move and when to hold still 5. CSV is written to SD card at `/non-magical-csi//_.csv` ### audio cues - **3 descending beeps** (1400->900->600 Hz) = transition phase - move to next position - **3 ascending beeps** (600->900->1400 Hz) = capture phase - hold still, recording starts - **3 rising beeps at end** = session complete ### procedures **indoor** (~100 s) - walk the door-to-device axis in a room. Labels: `absent`, `approach`, `still_mid`, `still_near`, `recede`. Requires line-of-sight between door and device. **outdoor** (~50 s) - linear distance sweep, walk ~10 m away and return. Labels: `still_near`, `recede`, `still_far`, `approach`. **zone** (~80 s) - distance sweep along the device axis, near to far and back. Labels: `still_near`, `still_mid`, `still_far`, `approach`, `recede`, `absent`. Covers the full shared label set so zone + free sessions combine cleanly. **free** - record any label at any time. Labels are drawn from whichever guided procedure was highlighted last. R=repeat, N=new label, ESC=finish. All captures append to one file. ### CSV format ``` ts_ms,label,rssi,ch,a00,a01,...,a55 ``` 56 LLTF HT20 subcarrier amplitudes per row. Transition rows (null label steps) are never written. ### data collection strategy - **Active injection on** (press P before starting) - gives stable 10 fps regardless of ambient traffic. Passive mode fps is unpredictable and makes temporal features unreliable. - **Multiple sessions** - collect at least 5-10 runs of each procedure in each environment. CSI fingerprints are highly environment-specific: furniture, people walking past, even temperature changes can shift them. - **Vary conditions** - different times of day, different people, door open vs closed. A model trained in one rigid condition will not generalise. - **Session naming** - name sessions meaningfully. There is no RTC on the ESP32; timestamps are milliseconds since boot and are useless across sessions. - **Check ChanOcc first** - use the channel occupation view to confirm your AP is active and delivering consistent fps on the chosen channel before starting a training session. ## file manager Browse and delete files on the SD card without removing it from the device. Access via key 9 from the menu. - W/S or arrow keys: scroll through files and directories - Enter or D: open a directory / confirm delete for a file - A or Back: go up one directory level - ESC or M: back to the menu Selecting a file shows a delete-confirm screen. Only deletion is supported - CSV data files are not meant to be edited on-device. WiFi is stopped while the file manager is open. ## ML pipeline *(work in progress)* The firmware collects labelled CSV data. What you do with it on a PC and how you eventually run inference on the device is covered in **[ML_PIPELINE.md](ML_PIPELINE.md)**. Short version: each frame is 56 subcarrier amplitudes. With enough labelled sessions you can train a small 1D CNN, quantize it to int8, and deploy it on the ESP32-S3 via ESP-DL (Espressif's native inference library, exploits S3 SIMD) or TFLite Micro as a fallback. The fingerprint is environment-specific - expect to retrain per deployment. On-device inference is the planned next step, not yet implemented. ## why the DC null gap in the spectrum OFDM WiFi reserves subcarrier 32 as a DC null. Subcarriers 0-3 and 61-63 are guard bands. The gap in the middle of the spectrum view is expected and correct. ## build Dependencies are vendored in `lib/`. No internet required at build time. ```sh pio run -e m5-cardputer-adv # build pio run -e m5-cardputer-adv -t upload # build + flash ``` The pre-build script `scripts/patch_libnet80211.py` weakens the `ieee80211_raw_frame_sanity_check` symbol in the ESP32 WiFi library so that `esp_wifi_80211_tx()` accepts all management frame subtypes. The patch is idempotent and survives incremental builds. Output binary: `bin/non-magical-csi--.bin` (factory merged, flash at 0x0). ## serial commands ``` csi start [ch] start CSI on channel (default 1) csi stop stop csi scan scan for nearby APs csi ap lock onto scanned AP (sets BSSID filter) csi ch change channel csi active start start active probe injection csi active stop stop injection csi info frame count, fps, per-subcarrier stats los start begin LOS sequence (countdown -> calibrate -> scan) los stop stop los recal recalibrate baseline mode [los|spec|var|motion|corr|console] switch view from terminal log [0-3] get/set log verbosity (0=off 1=err 2=info 3=dbg) beep [hz] [ms] test speaker ``` ## references - ESP32 CSI Toolkit - Hernandez & Kubisch (2021) - espressif/esp-csi - Espressif Systems (2023) - espressif/esp-dl - Espressif Systems (2024) - WiSee: Whole-Home Gesture Recognition - Patel et al., MobiCom 2013 - LLTF subcarrier mapping - ESP-IDF wifi_csi_info_t documentation"}

{"format":"markdown","content":"Features

Music & Library

MP3, WAV, FLAC and AAC playback from microSD (FAT32/exFAT).

Album artwork, metadata, music search, folders, favorites and playback queue.

Shuffle, repeat, seeking and adjustable playback speed (75–125%).

Optimized library scanning and artwork caching.

Audio Processing

11-band equalizer (±12 dB) with presets and custom profiles.

Bass+ mode, adjustable Reverb and stereo peak limiter.

Real-time processing for local and Bluetooth audio.

Interface & Customization

Custom LVGL touchscreen interface with animated dragon graphics and audio-reactive visualizations.

Album artwork, rotary volume control and playback animations.

PIN screen lock, custom wallpapers and startup image.

Battery monitoring, system clock and automatic screen-off with background playback.

Physical Keyboard Support

firmwares.firmwareDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"把一块桌面屏变成 1998 年的像素战场。

20 关小挑战 · 5 种塔（各 3 级）· 9 种敌人 · 8 种 BOSS 技能 · 本机大模型写就
· 魔性音效（一个音频文件都没有，全部是算出来的）

敌人从右边沿路走向你的基地，你只有 20 条命和有限的塔位。后面的关卡是岩地：
大片地面不能建塔，「好位置」本身就是要精打细算的预算 —— 难在要想，不难在抠门。

· 纯触摸：点底部选塔 → 点草地建塔 → 点已建的塔升级或卖出 → 右上角提前开下一波
· 8 种 BOSS 技能：自愈、现场产兵、死亡分裂、全场加速、沉默你的塔、偷你的金币、
  半血蜕甲变凶、周期性隐身
· 有一关是整屏一体的迷宫，也有一关是两条独立前线（守得住一边，守不住两边）
· 难度由一位真正的小学生测试员打出来的反馈定稿：不能轻易过关，但绝不需要唯一解

A pixel tower defence for M5Stack Tab5, written by a local AI model.

20 bite-sized levels · 5 upgradable towers · 9 enemy types · 8 boss abilities
· every pixel drawn by code, every sound synthesised — the app ships with no
image or audio files at all.

Build a maze with your towers and hold 20 lives. Later maps are rock fields:
most ground is unbuildable, so the good spots are a budget you have to spend well.

· Touch only: pick a tower → tap green ground → tap a built tower to upgrade or sell
· 8 boss abilities: self-heal, spawn, death-split, global haste, EMP, gold steal,
  armour molt, periodic ghosting
· Difficulty tuned from a real primary-school playtester's notes: never a
  single-solution puzzle, always retry-until-you-win

⚠️ 整包刷机会清空关卡进度与解锁记录；只想保住进度就用不擦除的升级方式 ⚠️

github.com/andjiang0083/pixel-tower-defense"}

currentVersion.versionDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"v0.5.4 · 第 10 关不再堵死，中英文切换回来了

第 10 关有个老问题：它的第二波敌人少，下一波会在上一波还没走完时就开——一波叠一波，最后满屏敌人、画面像卡死。现在一波要等自己的敌人快清完才允许下一波叠上来，第 10 关稳稳跑顺。

最重的那几关也顺了：地面以前每帧要重画两千多个小方块，现在每格只画一次、擦掉时一次就成，48 个敌人加 20 座塔的最坏情况也不卡了。之前那个「同时最多几只敌人」的限制已经撤掉——它只是把问题盖住，不是修好。

标题界面的 英文 / 中文 按钮回来了，选好会记住；两种语言下的每个界面都逐屏校对过，还加了一道「一个汉字都不许缺」的自检。

v0.5.4 · level 10 no longer chokes, and EN / 中文 is back

Level 10 had an old problem: its second wave is small, so the next wave used to start before the previous one had finished — wave after wave piled onto the field until the screen filled up and the game looked frozen. A wave now waits until its own enemies are nearly gone before the next may overlap it, and level 10 stays smooth.

The heaviest maps are smoother too: the ground used to be redrawn as 2000+ small tiles every frame; each cell is now drawn once and cleared in a single pass, so 48 enemies plus 20 towers no longer stutter. The temporary cap on how many enemies could be alive at once is gone — it was hiding the problem, not fixing it.

The ENGLISH / 中文 buttons are back on the title screen and the choice is remembered, and every screen has been checked in both languages."}

firmwares.firmwareDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"# Wifi_RIG_CTRL for M5Stack CoreS3 SE Ver 3.19 M5Stack CoreS3 SE を無線機（リグ）のリモートコントローラーにするファームウェアです。 Raspberry Pi（Wifi_Rig_CTRL FastAPI バックエンド）または ICOM WLAN Remote（CI-V over WiFi）経由でリグを操作し、 APRSビーコン送出や、Wifi_Rig_PTT（別売のリレー基板）/ Hamlib 経由でのPTT制御に対応します。 by JI1ORE --- ## 1. 同梱ファイル | ファイル | 内容 | |---|---| | `src/` `include/` `platformio.ini` `merge_bin.py` | ソース一式（PlatformIO プロジェクト） | | `M5CoreHamCAT_CoreS3SE_v3.19.bin` | ビルド済みファームウェア（マージ済み、0x0番地に書き込み可） | 書き込み済み `.bin` を直接使う場合は、esptool等で 0x0 番地に書き込んでください。 ```bash esptool.py --chip esp32s3 write_flash 0x0 M5CoreHamCAT_CoreS3SE_v3.19.bin ``` 自分でビルドする場合は、PlatformIO（VSCode拡張 または CLI）でこのフォルダをプロジェクトとして開き、 `Build` / `Upload` を実行してください。 ```bash pio run # ビルド pio run -t upload # ビルド＋書き込み ``` M5Stack Core2 / M5Stack Core2 Tough 向けはそれぞれ別フォルダ（`M5CoreHamCAT_Core2` / `M5CoreHamCAT_Core2Tough`）で公開しています。 --- ## 2. ハードウェア接続（Port の役割） | Port | ピン | 用途 | |---|---|---| | **Port A** | SDA=G2 / SCL=G1 (+GND/5V) | **ロータリーエンコーダ**（M5純正 I2C エンコーダユニット Unit Encoder / SKU:U135 を接続） | | **Port B** | G8 / G9 (+GND/5V) | **PTTキー入力（G8）＋ステータスLED（G9）**。詳細は下記 | ### Port B の配線（重要） - **G8 ⟷ GND**：外部トグルスイッチ／フットスイッチ／メカニカルキー（M5純正 SK6812 等）のPTT接点をここに接続します。 G8は内部プルアップ（`INPUT_PULLUP`）されているため、スイッチはG8とPort BのGND間に接続するだけでOKです（プルアップ抵抗など追加部品は不要）。 - **G9**：WS2812互換のNeoPixel（1灯）のデータ入力。送受信状態をLEDの色で表示します（後述）。 > **重要な仕様**：実際に送信（PTT ON）されるのは、**画面上の「PTT」ボタンがON（`txEnabled`）** かつ **Port BのG8が閉（LOW）** の**両方が揃ったとき**だけです。 > 画面の「PTT」ボタンだけをタップしても、Port Bに何も接続していなければ送信されません。 > 想定運用：画面の「PTT」ボタンで送信を許可（アーム）しておき、実際の送信タイミングは外部スイッチ（フットスイッチ等）で操作する、という2段構えの安全設計です。 ### ステータスLED（Port B, G9）の色 | 色 | 状態 | |---|---| | 赤 | **実際に送信中**（Hamlib / Wifi_Rig_PTT / CI-V いずれの方式でも） | | 青 | 送信スタンバイ中（画面のPTTボタンON＝アーム済み、PTT方式=Wifi_Rig_PTT、実送信はしていない） | | 緑 | 送信スタンバイ中（画面のPTTボタンON＝アーム済み、PTT方式=Hamlib または CI-V） | | 消灯 | 画面のPTTボタンOFF（送信アーム解除中） | ### 画面の向き CoreS3 SE は画面回転（上下反転）は行わず、通常の向きのまま表示します（画面反転は Core2 Tough 版のみ）。 ### オーディオ CoreS3 SE は内蔵マイク/スピーカーに加え、外部 Module Audio（ES8388、Port A/B とは別のI2C: SDA=G12, SCL=G11）を選べます。 設定画面（PTT Method 画面）でSPK出力先・Mic入力先をそれぞれ内蔵／Module Audio（外部）から独立して選択できます。 --- ## 3. 初回起動〜接続までの流れ ### 3-1. 起動画面（スプラッシュ） 電源を入れると "Wifi_Rig_CTRL" のロゴ表示後、**Normal** / **Skip** の2つのボタンが表示されます。 - **Normal**：通常起動。Wi-Fi選択 → Raspberry Pi/CI-V接続 → リグ選択 → PTT方式選択、の順に毎回設定を確認しながら進みます。 - **Skip**：前回保存済みの設定（Wi-Fi・Pi接続先・リグ・PTT方式）を使って、確認画面を飛ばして一気にメイン画面まで自動接続します。 画面左上には **「既定:Normal」/「既定:Skip」** の小さいトグルがあります。これをタップして「既定:Skip」にしておくと、 **8秒間何もタップしなかった場合の自動遷移先がSkipになります**（Normal/Skipボタンをその場でタップした場合はそちらが優先されます）。 毎回Skipで起動したい場合は、一度この既定値をSkipにしておけば、以後はボタン操作なしで自動的にSkip起動されます。 ### 3-2. Wi-Fi接続画面 周囲のWi-Fi（Androidテザリング等）をスキャンして一覧表示します。SSIDをタップしてパスワードを入力し接続します。 ### 3-3. Raspberry Pi / CI-V 接続画面 画面右上の **「Pi Mode」/「CI-V」** で接続方式を切り替えます。 - **Pi Mode**（Raspberry Pi + rigctld/FastAPI バックエンド経由） - Hostname（またはIPアドレス。mDNS使用/不使用を切替可） - API Port / Audio Port - API Key（任意。バックエンド側で認証を要求する場合のみ） - **CI-V**（ICOM WLAN Remote互換、無線機のWiFiに直結。Pi不要） - Host（無線機のIPアドレス） - Ctrl Port / CIV Port / Addr(hex)（CI-Vアドレス） - Username / Password（無線機側で設定した認証情報） - Timeout（無操作時の画面消灯までの時間） 入力後「Connect」をタップします。 ### 3-4. リグ選択画面 接続先（Pi/CI-V）から取得したリグ一覧から操作対象を選択します。 ### 3-5. PTT方式選択画面 - **Wifi_PTT**：別売の Wifi_Rig_PTT リレー（Remotekeyer）へWiFi/UDP経由でPTT信号を送る方式。ICOM機でHamlib経由PTTだと変調が乗らない問題を回避するために用意された方式です。 - PTT Host（mDNS名 or IPアドレス）、PTT Port を設定 - **Hamlib**：rigctld 経由で通常のCAT PTT制御を行う方式。 - PTT Device（シリアルデバイス）、PTT Type（RTS/DTR）を設定 設定後「OK」でメイン画面へ遷移します。 --- ## 4. メイン画面の操作方法 ### 上段（ステータス表示） - 左：接続中の機種名 - 右上のチップ（左から）： 1. **テーマチップ**（例:"OCN"）：タップでデザインテーマを **OCN → AMB → MONO** の順に切替 2. **昼夜チップ**（"NGT"/"DAY"）：タップで夜間⇄日中表示に切替。日中モードでは画面輝度を最大にし、明るい場所でも見やすい高コントラスト配色になります 3. **TXピル**：送信中は赤（Hamlib）またはオレンジ（APRS送信中）に点灯 ※ テーマ・昼夜チップは**送信中（PTT ON）でも操作可能**です。 - 周波数表示（大きく表示）：タップで周波数の直接入力画面へ（送信中はタップ無効） - Sメーター：受信信号強度をグラデーションで表示 - ステータスチップ：ST(ステップ幅) / PW(パワー) / MD(モード) / WD(フィルタ幅) ### ボタン（4×3グリッド） | ボタン | 機能 | |---|---| | Freq | 周波数を選択（ロータリーエンコーダで増減） | | Step | 周波数ステップ幅を選択・変更 | | Mode | 運用モード（SSB/CW/FM等）を選択・変更 | | Wid | フィルタ幅を選択・変更 | | Pow | 送信パワーを選択・変更 | | SQL | スケルチレベルを選択・変更 | | APRS | **短押し**：APRS送信のON/OFF切替（要:APRS Enabled設定＋GPS位置情報取得済み）。
**長押し（0.7秒以上）**：APRS設定画面を開く | | PTT | 画面上のPTTアーム状態をON/OFF切替（実際の送信にはPort Bの外部スイッチも必要。上記「Port Bの配線」参照） | | Back | 接続を切ってリグ選択画面へ戻る | | SPK | スピーカー（受信音声）のON/OFF | | DOWN / UP | 選択中の項目（Freq/Step/Mode/Wid/Pow/SQL）の値をボタンでも増減可能 | ### ロータリーエンコーダ（Port A / Unit Encoder） Freq/Step/Mode/Wid/Pow/SQL のいずれかのボタンで項目を選択した状態で回すと、その項目の値を増減できます。 --- ## 5. APRS設定（APRSボタン長押しで表示） | 項目 | 内容 | |---|---| | APRS Enabled | APRS機能自体のON/OFF | | Use GPS | ONの場合、Android(Tasker)から取得した位置情報を自動使用（手動入力欄はロックされる） | | Latitude / Longitude | Use GPS=OFF時の手動位置情報 | | APRS TXFreq | APRSビーコン送信周波数 | | Baudrate | 1200 / 9600 | | TX Interval | ビーコン送信間隔（30/60/120/180/300/600秒） | | Callsign / SSID | 自局コールサイン・SSID | | Path | WIDE1-1 / WIDE1-1,WIDE2-1 / WIDE2-1 / DIRECT / NONE | | Symbol | APRSシンボル（アイコン表示） | | Destination | APRS宛先コード（TNC種別） | | Sound Device | Pi側で使用するサウンドデバイス | **GPS位置情報について**：Use GPS=ON時は、Android側でTasker HTTPサーバー（設定画面下部に表示されるポート・パスを参照）を起動しておく必要があります。 M5はWiFi接続後、定期的にAndroidへ位置情報を取りに行き、取得できていない状態でAPRS送信を開始しようとすると「GPS位置情報未取得」の警告が出て開始できません（その場合はその場で自動的に一度再取得を試みます）。 --- ## 6. 配色テーマ | テーマ | 特徴 | |---|---| | OCN (Ocean) | 標準配色（ティール/ブルー系） | | AMB (Amber) | 真空管・VFD風の琥珀色。夜間運用向けの落ち着いた配色 | | MONO | 無彩色・最大コントラスト。視認性重視 | 各テーマとも昼間モード（明るい背景・高コントラスト）／夜間モード（暗い背景）を持ち、画面右上のチップで独立して切替できます。設定は本体に保存され、再起動後も保持されます。 --- ## 10. v3.19 での変更点（v2.51 との比較） - バージョン表記を 3.19 に更新（アプリ／Pi API と版を統一） - **リグ／ラズパイとの通信断を検知して警告表示**: 一定時間（約3秒）リグまたは Raspberry Pi と通信できない状態が続くと、周波数の「MHz」の上に黄色の⚠マークを表示します。Pi 経由では API の `rig_ok`（Pi は応答するがリグに届いていない状態）とも連動します。 - **MONO／AMBER テーマで S メーターが見えにくい問題を修正**: これらのテーマは昼間モードのアクセント色が暗く、メーターがほぼ見えなかったため、メーター専用に明るい配色を使うようにしました。 --- ## 9. v2.50 での変更点（v2.30 との比較） - バージョン表記を 2.33 に更新 - APRSで無線機内蔵APRSモデム（FTX-1等、TX Method=Rig）を使用している場合、 M5側（Android中継）のGPS位置情報が未取得・古くてもAPRSを開始・継続できるように 修正。この方式ではリグ自身のGPSで位置情報が付加されるため、M5側のGPS取得状況を 条件にするのは誤りだった（従来はGPS未取得時に開始を拒否、または位置情報が 途絶えると自動停止してしまっていた） ## 8. v2.30 での変更点（v2.20 との比較） - バージョン表記を 2.30 に更新 - Pi 経由モードは **Raspberry Pi 側 API**（`api.py`）の更新で、接続中の機種が 実際にサポートするモード一覧を動的に検出するようになった（例: FT-991 の C4FM、 IC-705 の D-STAR など、従来は選べなかった機種固有のデジタルモードが Mode 選択に 表示されるようになる）。M5本体にはPi更新機能がないため、反映するには **Android/iOSアプリの「Update Pi」ボタンを一度使うか、Raspberry Piのセットアップ をやり直す**必要がある（詳細は `RaspberryPiSetup/readme.txt` を参照） - CI-V直結モードのMode選択に D-STAR（IC-705/IC-9700）と WFM を追加 （従来はAndroid/iOS版にはあったがM5版のみ選択肢になかった） - RasPi接続画面で「Scan」から検出した機器のIPをコピーした際、自動的に 「Use IP」モードへ切り替わるようにした（API Port / Audio Portはコピーせず、 既存の設定を維持する） - RasPi接続画面のSCAN／Connectボタンの横幅を調整し、「Connect」ラベルが 省略されず表示されるようにした - CI-Vモードのフィルタ選択を修正。D-STAR時はIC-705の仕様上フィルタ0x01のみ 受け付けるため、幅指定に関わらずフィルタ0x01を送信するようにした - APRS設定画面で Enabled / TX Method（リグモデム使用有無）を変更してOKを 押した際、画面遷移や再接続なしにその場でAPRS送受信を停止・再起動するように改善 ## 7. v2.20 での変更点（v2.18 との比較） - バージョン表記を 2.20 に更新 - CI-Vモード時のポーリング間隔を緩和（200ms→500ms）し、無線機側の負荷によるWiFi切断を回避 - CI-Vモード時のPTT OFFにリトライ処理を追加（送信固着防止） - VFO A/B・MAIN/SUBの自動判別・表示に対応 - APRS受信ビーコン一覧画面（距離・方位表示）を追加 - streamTask強制終了処理・ENOMEM対策など安定性改善 - PTT Method画面からリグ選択画面へ戻った際、CATデバイス／機種の未保存の選択が保存済みの値に戻ってしまう不具合を修正"}

firmwares.firmwareDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"# SP2ALERT for M5StopWatch

POTA / SOTA スポット通知ファームウェア(M5Stack「M5StopWatch」向け)。
`SP2ALERT_Android_1.3` の機能を、ESP32-S3ベースの円形AMOLEDウェアラブル
「M5StopWatch」(1.75インチ 466x466 タッチ, ボタン2+電源ボタン, WiFi)に
移植したものです。

起動フロー: スプラッシュ → Wi-Fi接続画面 → スポット監視(カード表示)。
Wi-Fi接続画面は `M5CoreHamCAT_ForCore3SE_2.33` の実装パターンを移植しています。

## ビルド・書き込み

```bash
# ビルド
pio run

# ファームウェア書き込み(実機をUSB接続した状態で)
pio run -t upload

# 音声クリップ(data/voice/*.pcm)をLittleFSへ書き込み(初回・クリップ変更時に実行)
pio run -t uploadfs

# シリアルモニタ
pio device monitor
```

初回ビルド時に `M5.getBoard()` がシリアルログで `board_M5StopWatch` を
返すことを確認してください(異なる場合はPSRAM未検出などのハード起因の
可能性があります)。

## 音声読み上げクリップについて

`data/voice/*.pcm` は16bit / 16kHz / モノラルの録音済み音声クリップで、
`alert_engine.cpp` がコールサイン等をアルファベット/数字ごとに1クリップずつ
連結再生する方式です(自由文の公園名・山名は読み上げ対象外)。

現在同梱しているクリップは、macOS標準の `say` コマンド(英語音声
Samantha)で機械合成したものです。実用上問題ない品質ですが、より自然な
音声にしたい場合は同じファイル名(NATOフォネティック26種 + 数字0-9 +
pota/sota/qrt)で16bit/16kHz/モノラルPCM(ヘッダなし)の音声に差し替えて
`pio run -t uploadfs` を再実行してください。

## 現在のスコープ(初期リリース)

- アラート: CWトーン / 音声読み上げ(録音クリップ)。CWバイブ(振動)は未対応。
- フィルターは単一のグローバル設定のみ(Android版の名前付き複数プリセットは非対応)。
  バンド/モードなどの一覧編集UIは本体には無く、ON/OFFと数値パラメータの
  みを本体設定画面で調整できます。
- Hunt済み/Chase済み(CSVインポート)による除外は非対応。
- 通知済み/確認済み状態はRAM保持のみで、再起動すると失われます
  (再起動直後は現在マッチしているスポットに対して再度アラートが鳴り得ます)。
- Bluetooth関連機能は非対応(本体はWiFiのみ)。"}

{"format":"markdown","content":"## 2026-10-30 (v0.7.0-alpha) - SIGNAL HUNTER
- **Hunt a BLE device by signal strength.** A "Track device" action on the BLE scanner opens a proximity view that locks onto the chosen device and turns its advertisement RSSI into a smoothed signal meter with a getting-closer / getting-farther arrow and a red/amber/green band, so you can walk down a beacon or tag. It is labelled signal, not distance (RSSI is not a tape measure). 
- **Locate a WiFi AP by beacon signal.** A "Locate AP" action on the WiFi scanner does the same for an access point: it locks the AP's channel, reads its beacon RSSI frame by frame and drives the same meter, arrow and band, and works on a hidden or idle AP.
- **Act on connected clients from Evil Twin.** The CLIENTS list is now interactive: ENTER on a client opens a menu to deauthenticate it once (bounce it back through the captive portal) or block it, which keeps it kicked off for the rest of the session.
- **BLE Identity Spoof is no longer a dead action.** Selecting "Spoof Identity" on a scanned device previously did nothing; it now opens the spoofer locked to that device to clone its name and MAC, and a cold launch from the BLE menu shows a `(select from scanner)` prompt that routes to the scanner to pick a target instead of advertising an empty persona. (Remains in the experimental tier pending on-device confirmation of the clone.)
- **Read-only logs scroll with a position thumb.** The probe, credential, client-traffic, saved-network, About and What's New views now use the shared list component: a proportional scrollbar thumb replaces the old carets and "N/M" readout, and scrolling clamps cleanly at both ends.
- **Crashes now record the heap state that preceded them.** A small flight recorder in always-on RTC memory logs the free heap, largest free block (fragmentation) and minimum free heap with a real timestamp, so an out-of-memory reboot leaves evidence of how starved the heap was instead of a bare reset.
- **Footer counters no longer truncate.** Large index/total counters (such as a four-digit file count) render in full instead of being cut to "1000/10"; the counter formatter is now shared and bounds-checked. First external community contribution.
- **Build integrity: third-party firmware-library ZIPs are pinned by SHA256.** The two external release ZIPs the build downloads are verified against recorded checksums in CI, so a re-uploaded asset at a fixed URL can't silently change the shipped bytes.



## 2026-10-30 (v0.7.1-alpha)

Stability point release.

- **BadBLE no longer loops after a reflash.** HID mode now advertises a fresh random identity each session by default, so a host's stale bond from a previous install can no longer collide and spin the device in an endless reconnect loop. "Fixed MAC" becomes opt-in persistence for operators who deliberately want a reconnectable identity, and a reconnect-storm guard stops advertising (with a "forget on host" hint) if that opt-in path ever spins. Verified on-device.
- **BadUSB SD scripts are discoverable.** The "No scripts found" screen now names the path and format (DuckyScript `.txt` in `/adversary/badusb/`), and the README documents the convention. The SD-loading feature already existed; operators just could not find it.
- **BadBLE "Type" row relabelled "Appearance".** It only ever set the BLE GAP appearance icon hint (hosts classify an HID device by its report map, which is always a keyboard), so the honest label avoids implying it changes the device class. A dead `setAppearance` no-op was removed. Real mouse/joystick device types are tracked for a later release."}

{"format":"markdown","content":"## 2026-10-25 (v0.6.0-alpha) FIELD USABILITY
- **The screen now sleeps on idle to save battery.** After a period of inactivity the display dims to a still-readable level, then turns off; any key wakes it. Both delays are configurable in Settings > Display (Dim After / Screen Off), and the dim stage is a readable intermediate so a glance does not require a keypress.
- **Clocks show your local time.** Set a UTC offset in Settings > Time Zone and the wardriving clock and on-screen times render local, while saved logs and exports stay in UTC so captures remain comparable across devices.
- **Actions that need an SD card grey out when none is in.** Rebuild Index no longer runs a scan that reports a false success with no card present; it reads as disabled until a card is inserted, matching the rest of the SD-gated menu.
- **Wardriving radio mode is chosen per run from the idle screen.** The WiFi / BLE / both selector sits on the pre-run screen, so each session picks its radios without a trip into Settings.
- **A what's-new screen shows once after an update.** The first boot on a new version opens a short summary of what changed; reopen it any time from Settings > What's New. The version is shown live from the build, so the notes never carry a stale number.
- **Handshake Auto Hunt describes itself accurately.** The config screen no longer claims Auto Hunt "uses values from the Settings menu": its timing is built in and the whitelist is its only Settings input, which the copy now states."}

{"format":"markdown","content":"## 2026-10-23 (v0.5.0-alpha) - The UX Update
- **One model behind every attack-config screen.** Deauth, Evil Twin, Karma, Probe Flood, Beacon Spam and Handshake now share the same config form: identical row chrome (label left, value right), the same selection and scrolling behaviour as the lists, one green start-button style, and one keyboard model for navigating, editing values and activating a row.
- **Handshake is now two screens: Auto Hunt and Manual.** The mode is chosen from the Wireless -> Handshake menu instead of toggled inside the screen, so each presents only the controls it needs.
- **Deauth and Handshake Manual take their target from the scanner.** The Target row shows `(select from scanner)` until set; selecting it opens the WiFi scanner and returns with the chosen AP. Manual capture shows the target SSID, channel and BSSID on the capturing screen.
- **Destructive confirms are consistent everywhere.** Every delete / clear / discard / forget prompt now routes through one shared confirm dialog.
- **Menus grouped by purpose, with a unified footer style.** The Wireless and BLE menus are banded into Recon / Attacks / Data sections, and footer hints and key glyphs follow one house style across the UI. 
- **New Tron electric-cyan theme preset.**
- **Wardriving is steadier in BOTH (WiFi+BLE) mode.** A fixed-size Bloom filter bounds deduplication memory and a passive BLE scan flattens the heap-usage slope, so long BOTH-mode sessions no longer trend toward out-of-memory; the live log reserves per-type slots and the network count survives Stop for the save screen.
- **Optional heap-fragmentation readout.** The heap badge can show the largest free block alongside free heap, the tell that classified the BOTH-mode OOM.
- **Sniffer capture controls moved into a config block** for a consistent setup flow before capture."}

{"format":"markdown","content":"## 2026-10-19 (v0.4.0-alpha)
- **Wardriving now observes BLE as well as WiFi.** A BLE observation source feeds both the live network log and the WiGLE CSV export, selectable with a radio-mode setting (WiFi / BLE / both); deduplication is type-aware so a WiFi AP and a BLE peripheral never collapse into one row. WiFi and BLE run at the same time via radio coexistence. 
- **Sniffer capture no longer corrupts the heap.** The WiFi-driver-task callback mutated containers the main loop also touched with no synchronization, so under load the dual-core chip smashed allocator metadata and rebooted (`CORRUPT HEAP`), usually caught on exit-to-menu. Each frame is now copied into a POD and handed to the main loop over a FreeRTOS queue, which does all stats/log/pcap work on one task. 
- **Packet log reads cleanly under heavy traffic.** Scrolling up off the newest row freezes the log so it stays readable at any packet rate (stats, flood detection and capture keep running), and the log renders in capture order after its ring buffer wraps.
- **Release firmware runs quiet.** A level-gated logging layer and a dedicated release build ship the image at WARN, so the serial console is no longer flooded at runtime.
- **One shared component behind every list and popup menu.** The scanner, sniffer, wardriving, captures, RFID, radio, BLE, settings and handshake-history lists, and all eight quick-action popups, now route through a single list/menu component, so navigation, scrolling and the selected-row highlight are consistent across the whole UI.
- **Evil Twin lists every connected client.** The clients view no longer drops entries."}

{"format":"markdown","content":"## 2026-10-11 (v0.3.0-alpha)
- **RFID Write / clone.** Restore a saved `.nfc` dump onto a MIFARE Classic 1K card — all 47 data blocks written back with the recovered keys (Key A → Key B → factory-FF fallback), with a per-block write-retry so a transient RF warm-up can't drop a block on the first pass. Every outcome is reported (blocks written, auth failures, write failures); nothing is silently skipped. 
- **UID cloning on magic cards.** The opt-in UID write now lands block 0 on both card families: a Gen2/CUID direct write, and — falling through when that is refused — the Gen1a backdoor. The firmware reports which card type it detected; an ordinary card's locked UID is reported plainly, not masked. Verified end-to-end on a Gen1a card (UID written, read back, then restored).
- **Reliable Gen1a magic detection and sector reads.** Detection retries the timing-sensitive backdoor probe so a magic card is not missed on the first try; the audit read path authenticates once per sector (the fix for sectors reading back as `??`) and names every read/auth failure instead of failing silently.
- **Dashboard web AP is WPA2-protected.** The on-device dashboard access point now uses an auto-generated per-device key instead of being open. (#45)
- **Sniffer capture survives an attack handoff.** WiFi is re-initialised on sniffer start, so launching a capture after an attack no longer comes up dead. (#52)
- **Root-menu list items live-gate on Re-scan.** Menu entries for a module seated after boot (RFID, Wardriving, Captures, BadBLE) un-grey as soon as a Re-scan finds the hardware, no reboot."}

firmwares.firmwareDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"# 🪇 Детская погремушка — M5StickC Plus2

Трясёшь — играет и светится. Три режима, безопасная громкость и яркость, умеет засыпать само, если про него забыли.

## Что это

Обычный M5StickC Plus2 превращён в музыкальную игрушку для малыша: движение рукой даёт ноту и цвет на экране. Никаких проводов и приложений — включил, и можно играть. Громкость и яркость программно ограничены специально для детских ушей и глаз, а если устройство оставили лежать без дела, оно само притухнет и уснёт, экономя батарею.

## Включение и выключение

На торце устройства — кнопка питания. Нажатие включает экран, долгое удержание полностью выключает устройство.

Пока устройство включено, оно умеет засыпать само (см. [«Сон»](#сон) ниже) — для этого отдельно ничего нажимать не нужно.

## Режимы

Режимов три, переключаются кнопкой **A** по кругу: Погремушка → Шкатулка → Пианино → Погремушка.

### 🪇 Погремушка

Самый простой режим. Трясёшь — звучит нота и экран вспыхивает цветом. Чем сильнее трясти, тем ярче «дышит» экран.

### 🎵 Шкатулка

Нужно несколько раз потрясти, чтобы «завести» — дальше мелодия играет сама, а цвет на экране медленно переливается. По мере того как завод кончается, музыка замедляется — потряси ещё, чтобы продолжить.

### 🎹 Пианино

Наклоняешь устройство — высота ноты меняется по ступеням, как клавиши. Звук идёт только пока двигаешь: остановился — тишина, хотя полоска на экране останется показывать последнюю ноту.

## Управление

| Кнопка | Действие |
|---|---|
| **A** (под экраном) | Переключить режим. Если устройство спало — первое нажатие будит его и не меняет режим, нужно нажать ещё раз. |
| **B** (сбоку) | Переключить громкость по кругу: Тихо → Обычно → Без звука → Тихо. |

## Экран

В верхней полоске — название текущего режима, значок громкости и индикатор заряда батареи. При зарядке от USB-C рядом с батарейкой появляется молния. Чем меньше заряда — тем тревожнее цвет индикатора (жёлтый, затем красный).

## Сон

Если устройство полежало без движения около 20 секунд — экран притухает. Ещё примерно через минуту он гаснет и устройство засыпает полностью, почти не тратя батарею. Разбудить можно тряской или нажатием **A** — режим и громкость при этом не теряются. Пока устройство подключено к USB, оно не засыпает само — удобно, если оно просто лежит на столе заряжается.

## Если что-то пошло не так

- **На полоске красным светится «IMU»** — не определяется датчик движения. Это не поломка в привычном смысле: нажатие **A** всё равно проиграет ноту и даст вспышку на экране, кнопка **B** по-прежнему меняет громкость, но переключение между тремя режимами недоступно, пока датчик не заработает.
- **Экран мигнул сообщением «Заряд» и устройство выключилось** — батарея разрядилась почти полностью, это штатное поведение для защиты аккумулятора. Просто зарядите через USB-C.


## Для тех, кто хочет заглянуть под капот

Прошивка собирается через [PlatformIO](https://platformio.org/) (`pio run -e m5stack-stickc-plus2`), построена на [M5Unified](https://github.com/m5stack/M5Unified)."}

firmwares.firmwareDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"k85OS 7.8 (security update)

A hardening release. No new features; every user of the Web Terminal, the hotspot web file manager or FTP should update.

Security
Web Terminal and hotspot web file manager: the login cookie now carries a random per-login session token instead of the access key itself, with HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict (this also blocks cross-site requests to /api/exec, /delete, /mkdir, /firmware/pull). The hotspot no longer accepts the access key in the URL, and a valid session is no longer locked out by other people's failed attempts. A new key ends all old sessions.
Web Terminal: it can no longer be started on an open (password-less) access point.
FTP: the password is stored as a salted PBKDF2-SHA256 hash (old logins are upgraded automatically on the first successful login); new passwords must have at least 8 characters; after 6 failed logins in total, logins are locked for 5 minutes.
Hotspot web file manager: uploads, deletes and new folders can no longer touch protected files (configuration, services, keys). Uploads go through a temporary file, so a failed or interrupted upload no longer deletes an existing file, and a full filesystem is reported as a failure.
Firmware flashing: a slot that failed signature verification (or an aborted write) is invalidated immediately, so it can never be activated later through "Alt Firmware".
Lock screen password: constant-time hash comparison; a failed key derivation can never match.
The stale SSH host key left over from earlier versions is deleted from internal storage at boot.
Fixed
Update check and firmware list: the GitHub API reply buffers are now 32 KB (releases with several assets could overflow the old 4 KB buffer), and an overflowing reply fails cleanly instead of producing broken JSON.
About 24 KB of internal RAM freed by moving large static buffers to PSRAM.
Notes
Log in to the hotspot web file manager again after updating (sessions are new).
Existing short FTP passwords keep working; set a new one with ftppass if you want 8+ characters. Set it from the on-device Terminal rather than the Web Terminal, because the Web Terminal sends commands in the URL over plain HTTP."}

{"format":"markdown","content":"**Needs the free PC server from GitHub: https://github.com/yejun/tab5-web-display**

Show web pages on your Tab5 and use them by touch, like on a tablet: tap buttons and links, drag sliders, pinch to
zoom. A small Python program on your PC opens the page in Chrome or Chromium and streams it to the Tab5 over WiFi.

**What it can do**
- Show any website (`--url`), your own HTML file (`--file`), or a video (`--file clip.mp4`, with sound)
- Multi-touch: pinch zoom and scrolling; swipe between tabs, three fingers for back and forward
- M5Stack's Tab5 Keyboard: type into pages, control videos, type the WiFi password; its lights show the status
- Sound: what the page plays comes out of the Tab5's speaker (Linux PC)
- Built-in apps: dashboard (weather, forecast, air quality, headlines), clock with calendar, sticky notes,
  老黄历 (Chinese almanac), touch and motion demo. No API keys needed.
- Smooth and light: only changed areas are sent and drawn by the Tab5's hardware JPEG engine; animations
  run at up to ~58 fps, videos at up to 30
- Battery level in the settings

**How to run**
1. Flash this firmware. On first start, pick your WiFi network on the Tab5's screen.
2. On a PC on the same network (Python 3.9+), download the project from GitHub and run:
   pip install -r requirements.txt
   python server/server.py
3. With the Tab5 plugged in by USB, the server finds it by itself. Otherwise add `--device <IP>`; the Tab5
   shows its IP address.

Use a server version that matches this firmware (v1.3.x); the server warns if they differ.

Swipe down from the top edge for the settings (WiFi, brightness, volume, keyboard lights, flip)."}

{"format":"markdown","content":"#### **M5StickC Plus 2 Aviation Avionics & Acoustic Variometer (M5-Watch)**

**M5StickC Plus 2 Aviation Avionics & Variometer** is a compact, wrist-wearable flight instrument designed for general aviation enthusiasts and free-flight pilots (paragliding, hang gliding, sailplanes, and ultralights). 

Powered by the **ESP32-PICO-V3-02** inside the **M5StickC Plus 2** and an external **GY-63 (MS5611-01BA03)** barometric altimeter connected via Grove Port A, this project delivers a double-buffered, 100% flicker-free civil aviation **Primary Flight Display (PFD)** alongside a sensitive, thermal-hunting audio variometer and real-time **Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE)** flight computer telemetry.

---

### 🌟 Key Features

* **Civil Aviation Glass Cockpit (PFD)**:
  * Dynamic artificial horizon rendered at 35–40 FPS with a $5^\circ$ pitch ladder, roll bank indicator, and 3D perspective runway.
  * Rolling tape altimeter with high-contrast digits and take-off relative reference (**AGL**).
  * Analog-style Vertical Speed Indicator (**VSI**) bar with graduated climb/sink rates.
* **4 Operational Display Modes**:
  * **Mode 0 (PFD Cockpit)**: Horizon, Altimeter tape, VSI, and system telemetry banner.
  * **Mode 1 (Tactical HUD)**: Fullscreen artificial horizon with large digital altitude and climb-rate readout.
  * **Mode 2 (Classic Dial)**: Traditional 3-pointer analog altimeter dial (hundreds, thousands, and tens of thousands).
  * **Mode 3 (In-Flight Calibration Menu)**: Step-by-step **1-meter** manual altitude calibration stored permanently in non-volatile flash (NVS).
* **Smart Acoustic Variometer**:
  * Progressive pitch and audio beep cadence for thermal lift, with an urgent continuous alarm tone for strong sink.
  * **Zero-Drift Silent Deadband** ($|VSI| < 0.20\text{ m/s}$): completely silent when resting on a table (no phantom beeps).
  * Instant single-click hardware toggle for Audio / Mute.
* **10Hz BLE Telemetry for Flight Computers**:
  * Broadcasts standard `$LK8EX1` NMEA sentences (barometric pressure in Pascals, calibrated altitude, climb rate in cm/s, ambient temperature, and battery voltage).
  * Chunked into standard 20-byte ATT packets for 100% seamless compatibility with **XCTrack**, **XCSoar**, **Flyme**, **LK8000**, and **SeeYou Navigator** without MTU truncation issues.
* **Automatic & On-Demand Attitude Leveling**:
  * Automatically tares flight posture (0° pitch, 0° roll) at startup to match the pilot’s natural arm/cockpit angle.
  * Long-press quick re-tare feature allows instant re-leveling mid-flight.

---

### 🛠️ Hardware Specifications

* **Controller**: M5Stack M5StickC Plus 2 (ESP32 @ 240 MHz, 240×135 color IPS LCD, internal MPU6886 6-axis IMU, buzzer, 200 mAh LiPo).
* **Barometric Sensor**: GY-63 module (TE Connectivity MS5611-01BA03, 24-bit $\Delta\Sigma$ ADC, 10–20 cm resolution).
* **Bus Architecture**: Independent I2C bus isolation (`I2C_NUM_0` for Grove Port A sensor and `I2C_NUM_1` for internal IMU/PMIC) with automated bus recovery.
* **Wireless Protocol**: BLE 4.2 Nordic UART Service (NUS), 10Hz transmission rate.

---

### 🕹️ Button Control Layout

* **Button A (Front M5)**:
  * *Single Click*: Zero AGL Take-off Altitude (`AGL = 0m`).
  * *Long Press (>1s)*: Level Artificial Horizon to current arm attitude.
  * *Double Click*: Toggle Simulated DEMO Flight Mode.
* **Button B (Bottom Side)**:
  * *Single Click*: Toggle Variometer Sound ON/OFF (Mute / Unmute).
  * *Long Press (>1s)*: Cycle screens (`PFD` ➔ `HUD` ➔ `Dial` ➔ `Calibration Menu`).
* **Inside Calibration Menu (Mode 3)**:
  * `Button A`: $+1\text{ meter}$.
  * `Button B`: $-1\text{ meter}$.
  * `Hold Button A (>1s)`: Save to NVS Flash memory and apply QNH sea-level pressure.
  * `PWR Button`: Cancel and return to flight display."}

firmwares.firmwareDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"Dedicated firmware for M5Stack StopWatch based on the Meta [Muse Gadget SDK](https://github.com/facebookincubator/muse-gadget-sdk/tree/main/esp32). The firmware runs on the ESP32-S3R8 and provides board-level support for the M5Stack StopWatch's round touchscreen AMOLED display, audio codec, power management IC, and physical buttons.

Key features include:

- **Full On-Screen UI**: Displays Muse status, an animated avatar, connection status, battery information, response text, and settings on the 1.75-inch, 466 x 466 round AMOLED display.
- **Voice Interaction**: Captures voice through the built-in microphone and plays Muse's voice responses through the speaker. The blue upper-right button provides Push-to-Talk control.
- **Touch and Button Controls**: Supports touchscreen interaction and integrates the StopWatch's blue voice button, yellow speaker control button, and red power button.
- **Image Display**: Displays images sent by Muse and renders them for the round screen resolution.
- **Muse Pairing and Connectivity**: Pairs with the Muse App, connects to a home Wi-Fi network, and establishes an encrypted communication session. Device settings, Bluetooth configuration, and OTA updates are supported.
- **Power Management and Low-Power Operation**: Monitors battery and USB power status. When running on battery with the display off, the firmware powers down the display and audio circuits and enters Light Sleep until awakened by a physical button.

The hardware adaptation targets the M5Stack StopWatch with an ESP32-S3R8, 16 MB Flash, 8 MB Octal PSRAM, CO5300 AMOLED display controller, CST820 touch controller, ES8311 audio codec, single microphone, and AW8737A speaker amplifier."}

{"format":"markdown","content":"Muse-Gadget For CoreS3 is open-source firmware based on the Meta [Muse Gadget SDK](https://github.com/facebookincubator/muse-gadget-sdk/tree/main/esp32) that turns the M5Stack CoreS3 into a touchscreen Muse AI assistant terminal. It provides voice Q&A, content display, and local service connectivity, making it suitable as a desktop assistant, smart home control interface, or AI application development platform.

Key features include:

- **Voice Q&A**: Hold the side `PWR` button to record a question, then release it to send the message to Muse. Muse transcribes and processes the message and displays its text response on the device.
- **Dedicated AI Terminal**: Start conversations and view responses and images directly on the CoreS3 without using a phone for every interaction.
- **Local Device and Service Connectivity**: The home-network tunnel allows Muse to reach devices on the same network and developer-built local HTTP APIs. Integrations can be extended to read sensors, retrieve status information, control relays, and perform similar tasks.
- **Touch Control and Device Management**: Use the touchscreen to open settings, check connection and battery status, and manage brightness, volume, power, and other device options.
- **AI Hardware Prototyping**: Developers can register custom device commands, integrate local services, and add new interaction logic through the SDK, using CoreS3 to build smart home panels and dedicated AI terminals.

This firmware requires the Muse App, a Muse account, an SDK Token, and Wi-Fi connectivity to access Muse services. It is not a standalone offline AI model. The firmware supports the CoreS3 dual microphones, speaker, touchscreen, `PWR` button, battery management, and software power-off features."}

firmwares.firmwareDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"*DECK//OS* turns the **M5Stack Tab5** and its keyboard into a pocket cyberdeck. It has a neon cyberpunk-inspired terminal-style interface and is built to be used from the keyboard, with touch as a backup.

## Modules - **TERMINAL**: SSH client with saved hosts and a full terminal emulator, plus chat with an Ollama server on your local network - **NOTES**: plain-text and Markdown notes saved on the SD card - **CALC**: calculator with a scrolling history - **WEATHER**: current conditions and forecast for your location - **PLAYER**: MP3 player for music on the SD card, through the speaker or headphones - **FILES**: browse, preview and delete files on the SD card, or upload and download them from a browser over Wi-Fi, protected by a PIN - **SYSTEM**: Wi-Fi, brightness, keyboard light, screen timeout with a clock screensaver, and over-the-air updates

## Requirements An M5Stack Tab5 and the Tab5 Keyboard. A microSD card is recommended for notes, music and files.

## Updates After this first install, updates arrive over the air from GitHub *(SYSTEM > UPDATE)*. Every update is signed, and a bad update rolls back on its own.

Source code, guide and web installer: https://github.com/hey-its-brian/tab5-cyberdeck"}

currentVersion.versionDescription:
{"format":"html","content":"

v1.3.0: new home screen, Obsidian vault sync

New home screen

Five tiles instead of one per module. TOOLS (TERMINAL, CALC, SYSTEM) and FILES & MEDIA (FILES, PLAYER) are groups: the tile lists what is inside and opens a screen of the same tiles. NOTES stays a tile of its own, WEATHER is a widget with the current conditions, and NET TOOLS is a placeholder for v1.4. Alt+1..5 opens a tile, Alt+T N C W M F S jumps to a module from anywhere, Esc or Del goes back one level, and the status bar shows where you are.

Obsidian vault sync

NOTES has two sources: LOCAL (the deck's own notes) and VAULT, an Obsidian vault kept in sync with the Self-hosted LiveSync plugin through its CouchDB. The deck speaks the plugin's database format directly (chunked notes, end-to-end encryption, matching chunk ids), so notes written on the deck show up in Obsidian as its own. NOTES > VAULT > SYNC holds the server, database, login and passphrase, an AUTO SYNC interval, SYNC NOW, RESCAN and a log. Markdown notes sync both ways with folders; attachments stay in Obsidian; a note changed on both sides keeps the Obsidian version and the deck's text as \"name (deck conflict).md\". Supported plugin settings are the defaults (E2EE v2 or off, xxhash64 ids, no path obfuscation, no compression).

Also

  • NOTES browses folders: Enter opens one, Backspace goes up.
  • Memory: the interface, parsed JSON and the sync's connection no longer compete for internal RAM, which had caused failed settings reads and SD card errors in the betas.
  • Del works as a back key wherever a module isn't using it.

Install

  • Over the air from v1.2.0: SYSTEM > UPDATE, or accept the popup.
  • From v1.1.0 or older: once over USB with the web installer (https://hey-its-brian.github.io/tab5-cyberdeck), because those builds cannot reach GitHub any more.
"}

{"format":"html","content":"

Important: Re-flash once over USB

GitHub changed its TLS certificate, and every earlier DECK//OS build (v1.1.0 and older, plus the 1.2 betas) rejects it, so SYSTEM > UPDATE and the update popup say they cannot reach GitHub. Install v1.2.0 once with the web installer over USB (your settings and files are kept if you choose not to erase). From v1.2.0 on, over-the-air updates work again.

New

Screen timeout and clock screensaver (SYSTEM > SAVER): after OFF / 1 / 2 / 5 / 10 / 30 minutes idle, a drifting, dimmed clock takes over (with the current track if music plays), then the screen sleeps. Any key or touch wakes it.
Ollama chat in TERMINAL (+ OLLAMA, Ctrl+O), contributed by @hardparking and hardened before merge: chat with an Ollama server on your LAN, with streaming replies and /models, /model, /clear.

Fixed

  • Update checks fail with \"could not read releases from GitHub\": certificates are now verified in software, because the ESP32-P4's ECC accelerator rejects GitHub's new P-256 certificate.
  • Boot loop with no SD card inserted (contributed by @hardparking).
  • More internal RAM for early boot: large buffers moved to PSRAM, removing a boot-time crash that new features could trigger.
  • ESP-IDF 5.5: fixes the 5.4.0 task-deletion bug behind the portal crash, among others.
"}

firmwares.firmwareDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"Weather dashboard for the M5Stack PaperColor (ESP32-S3, 4" Spectra 6 color e-ink, 600x400) with a browser-based config page on your local network. No API keys or accounts: weather from Open-Meteo, US zip-code geocoding from Zippopotam.us.

# FEATURES - Current conditions: temperature, feels-like, humidity, wind, condition icon - Indoor temperature and humidity from the onboard SHT40 - 5-day forecast with highs (red), lows (blue), and precipitation chance - Six built-in themes: Classic, Night, Forest, Comic, Time Circuit (Back to the Future), DECK//OS (cyberdeck HUD in four accents) - Alternate view: pick a second theme and flip between them with any top-edge button - Web config page at http://m5weather.local (zip, units F/C, refresh 15 min to 3 h, theme, Wi-Fi) - First-boot captive portal over a WPA2 hotspot - Settings persist in flash; hardware RTC corrected from NTP - Hardened LAN web server: Host/Origin checks, validated input, size-capped API responses

# FLASHING Flash at address 0x0. If the port does not respond, hold the side power button for about 6 seconds with USB-C connected to enter download mode, flash, then press it once to reboot.

# FIRST BOOT 1. On your phone or laptop join the Wi-Fi network "M5Weather-Setup" (password: m5weather). 2. A setup page opens (or browse to http://192.168.4.1). Enter your home 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi credentials. The device reboots and joins. 3. Browse to http://m5weather.local, enter your US zip code, and click "Save & Update Display".

# NOTES - The device stays awake so the config page is always reachable; plan on USB power. - A full e-ink refresh takes several seconds with visible flashing, which is normal for Spectra 6 panels. - Trusted-LAN model, no login: anyone on your network can change settings. - US zip codes only for now.

Source, build instructions, and version notes: https://github.com/hey-its-brian/m5weather"}

currentVersion.versionDescription:
{"format":"html","content":"

Weather dashboard for the M5Stack PaperColor (ESP32-S3, 4\" Spectra 6 e-ink, 600x400) with a browser-based config page on your LAN. No API keys: weather from Open-Meteo, zip geocoding from Zippopotam.us.

New in 1.4.0

  • DECK//OS theme: the Tab5 cyberdeck's HUD ported to the PaperColor as a fourth rendering style, in four accent variants (NETRUNNER / ARASAKA / NOMAD / MILITECH). Dotted background grid, chamfered panels with accent tabs, hero temperature in Orbitron, a // NOW readout, a 5-day hi/lo/rain trace, and forecast tiles with the current day lit.
  • The deck's gray tones have no ink equivalent and dithering stays off, so \"dim\" is rendered as a second ink and the faint grid is drawn as dotted lines. Nomad (yellow) and Netrunner (blue) read brightest on the panel.
  • Theme gains accent2 and grid fields for future styles.

Since v1.0.0 (the last tagged release)

  • 1.3.0: Alternate view. Pick a second theme in the config page and flip between the two with any of the three top-edge buttons (redraw only, no network fetch).
  • 1.2.0: Comic and Time Circuit themes; the theme system grew from palette-only to palette + rendering style.
  • 1.1.0: Indoor temperature and humidity from the onboard SHT40, shown under current conditions and exposed in GET /api/status. Saving a new zip now fetches weather immediately.

Install

  • M5Burner: flash m5weather-v1.4.0-full.bin (bootloader + partition table + app, merged) at address 0x0. Connect over USB-C, hold the side power button for about 6 seconds to enter download mode if the port does not respond, flash, then press it once to reboot.
  • esptool: esptool.py --chip esp32s3 write_flash 0x0 m5weather-v1.4.0-full.bin
  • PlatformIO: pio run -t upload from a clone of this repo.
  • m5weather-v1.4.0-app.bin is the application image alone (flash at 0x10000) for anyone who already has a bootloader and partition table on the device.
"}

{"format":"markdown","content":"# PocketQuestMini — A little world. A big quest.

A cozy fantasy adventure for the M5Stack StickS3, designed for short sessions you can put down anytime.

## Two ways to play

- **On the StickS3:** Battle Slimes, Wolves and Goblins using the Face button or gentle motion controls. Earn XP, level up and save your progress.
- **In your browser:** Explore an illustrated woodland road, fight turn-based battles, discover loot chests, challenge bosses and return to Oakwood for a peaceful rest.

Both experiences share your hero’s XP and level, saved on the StickS3.

## Browser features

- Female and male Nova appearances.
- Touch, keyboard and compatible PS5 controller support.
- Increasing road difficulty and randomized encounters.
- Animated Oakwood resting scene.
- Original background theme: “The Gentle Glade.”

## Getting started

Join the device-specific Wi-Fi shown on the StickS3, then open:

http://PocketQuest

Address fallback: http://192.168.4.1

No Internet connection or account is required to play. Pair controllers with your phone, tablet or computer—not the StickS3.

M5 cycles the connection and mini-game screens. The Face button and gentle motion control handheld combat.

Browser controller, fullscreen and audio support vary by device. Touch controls remain available.

**Supported hardware: M5Stack StickS3 with 8 MiB flash and 8 MiB PSRAM.**"}

firmwares.firmwareDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"# Cardputer ADV  ·  IMU Air-Mouse

把 M5Stack **Cardputer-Adv**（ESP32-S3 / 8 MB flash）变成一只「空中鼠标」：  
内置 BMI270 6 轴 IMU 的倾角驱动 USB HID 鼠标，摇一摇机身 = 单击。

---

## 文件清单

| 文件                                        | 大小     | 说明                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| **`cardputer-adv-imu-mouse.factory.bin`** | 584 KB | **完整工厂镜像**（bootloader + partition + app，**推荐直接烧这一个**） |
| `firmware.bin`                            | 518 KB | 仅 app 分区（需要先用对应的 bootloader + partition 表）            |
| `firmware.elf`                            | 15 MB  | ELF 调试信息（带符号表，可用于反汇编 / 调试）                            |
| `sketch/sketch.ino`                       | —      | 源程序                                                   |
| `src/main.cpp`                            | —      | 源程序（与 sketch.ino 等价）                                  |

---

## 一、烧录（推荐 esptool.py）

### 1. 准备工作

- **Python 3.7+**
- 安装 esptool：
  ```bash
  pip install esptool
  ```
- Cardputer-Adv 通过 **USB-C** 连上电脑。
- 进入下载模式：侧开关拨到 **OFF** → 按住 **G0 键不松** → 拨到 **ON** 开机 → 1 秒后松开 G0。

### 2. 烧录（一条命令搞定，0x0 地址写入完整工厂镜像）

```bash
esptool.py --chip esp32s3 --port /dev/ttyACM0 \
    --baud 921600 \
    --before default_reset --after hard_reset \
    write_flash --flash_mode dio --flash_freq 80m --flash_size 8MB \
    0x0 cardputer-adv-imu-mouse.factory.bin
```

> Windows 改成 `--port COM3`（或 `COM5` 等，看设备管理器）。

### 3. 也可以用 M5Burner / 乐鑫 Flash 下载工具

M5Burner（<https://m5burner.m5stack.com>）→ 选择 bin → 偏移 0x0 即可。

---

## 二、使用方法

1. 烧录后重启（拨 OFF→ON）。
2. 第一次插上 USB 时，**电脑的「设备管理器」会识别到一个新的「HID-compliant Mouse」**——这就是 Cardputer-Adv 在模拟的鼠标。
3. 倾斜 Cardputer，光标移动；摇一摇 = 单击。
4. 屏幕状态条会显示当前速度档位 / 倾斜角度 / 姿态原始值。

### 按键操作

> 固件现已是 **复合 USB HID 设备：键盘 + 鼠标**。默认打字 = 键盘输入；按住 `Fn` 才进入鼠标快捷键模式。

**普通模式（直接打字）：**

| 操作                  | 效果                        |
| ------------------- | ------------------------- |
| **键盘任意按键**          | 直接作为 USB 键盘输入到电脑（56 键全支持） |
| **倾斜机身**            | 光标跟随倾斜方向移动（越大越快）          |
| **摇一摇 / 轻拍**        | 单击（默认左键）                  |
| **BtnA（G0 键，机身侧边）** | 按住 = 左键拖动                 |

**鼠标快捷键（需按住 Fn）：**

| 操作                          | 效果                               |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| **`Fn` + `-` / `Fn` + `=`** | 调低 / 调高光标速度（1 ~ 10 档，屏幕 SPD 状态条） |
| **`Fn` + `0`**              | 重新校准「水平姿态」（把机身放在你想要的中心角度）        |
| **`Fn` + `1`**              | 切换「摇一摇」是「左键」还是「右键」               |
| **`Fn` + `↑` / `Fn` + `↓`** | 向上 / 向下滚轮                        |
| **`Fn` + `Esc`**            | 重新校准陀螺仪偏置（保持静止约 1 秒）             |
| **`Fn` + `空格`**             | 熄屏 / 点亮屏幕（熄屏时鼠标和打字仍然正常工作，再按一次点亮） |

---

## 三、工作原理

- **ESP32-S3 native USB** 直接接出 **HID Mouse** 设备（无需任何驱动，Win10/11/macOS/Linux 自动识别）。
- `M5Cardputer` 库读取 TCA8418 键盘控制器（I²C 0x34）。
- `M5.Unified` 的 `IMU_Class` 通过内部 I²C 总线驱动 BMI270（0x68），提供加速度 + 陀螺仪。
- 倾斜姿态：用加速度向量与「中性参考」之间的旋转角 `atan2(sin, cos)`，对死区、灵敏度（`RESPONSE_EXP`）做响应曲线整形。
- 「摇一摇」= 监测到加速度幅值瞬间偏离 1g 超过阈值 0.55g，触发一次鼠标左键脉冲。
- 8ms 周期（≈125 Hz）发送鼠标位移包，速度档位（1~10）按比例缩放像素。

---

## 四、构建参数（如果想自己重新编译）

| 项               | 值                                                |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| Board           | ESP32S3 Dev Module                               |
| Flash           | 8 MB（DIO / 80 MHz）                               |
| PSRAM           | **Disabled**（FN8 没有 PSRAM）                       |
| USB CDC on boot | **Enabled**（不勾的话原生 USB HID 不可用）                  |
| USB Mode        | Hardware CDC + HID                               |
| Partition       | Default（1.3 MB app + 1.4 MB spiffs）              |
| Arduino core    | esp32 2.0.17                                     |
| Toolchain       | xtensa-esp32s3-elf-gcc 8.4.0 (esp-2021r2-patch5) |

### 用 arduino-cli 命令行编译

```bash
arduino-cli core install esp32:esp32@2.0.17
arduino-cli lib install "M5Cardputer" "M5Unified" "M5GFX"
arduino-cli compile --fqbn esp32:esp32:esp32s3 \
    --build-property build.partitions=default \
    --build-property upload.maximum_size=8388608 \
    --build-property flash_size=8MB \
    --output-dir build sketch
esptool.py --chip esp32s3 -p /dev/ttyACM0 --baud 921600 \
    write_flash --flash_mode dio --flash_size 8MB \
    0x0 build/sketch.ino.bin
```

---

## 五、参数调优

打开 `sketch/sketch.ino`，顶部有完整的可调参数：

```cpp
static constexpr float    TILT_FULL_DEG  = 35.0f;   // 倾斜几度 = 满速度
static constexpr float    BASE_PX_FULL   = 22.0f;   // 满速度每帧最多移动多少像素
static constexpr int      SPEED_DEFAULT  = 4;       // 默认速度档
static constexpr float    DEADZONE_DEG   = 1.2f;    // 死区
static constexpr float    RESPONSE_EXP   = 1.7f;    // 响应曲线（>1 越靠近中心越细）
static constexpr float    SHAKE_TRIG_G   = 0.55f;   // 摇一摇触发阈值（g 偏离）
static constexpr uint32_t SHAKE_DEBOUNCE = 380;     // 摇一摇间隔
```

---

## 六、常见问题

**Q: 烧录后插电脑没反应？**  
A: 确认 USB 数据线支持数据传输（纯充电线不行）；检查 Device Manager 是否看到 "HID-compliant Mouse"。

**Q: 倾斜方向反了？**  
A: 在源码中调换 `tiltComponent(0)` 或 `tiltComponent(1)` 的符号；或者把 `nx`/`ny` 互换。

**Q: 摇一摇太灵敏 / 不灵敏？**  
A: 改 `SHAKE_TRIG_G`（默认 0.55g，越大越不灵敏）和 `SHAKE_DEBOUNCE`（默认 380 ms）。

**Q: 是否需要电池？**  
A: 不需要。USB-C 供电即可，IMU + USB HID 全程在线。"}

{"format":"markdown","content":"# Dragon Detector for M5Stack StopWatch C152

Built specifically for the **M5Stack StopWatch C152**: a round Wi-Fi/Bluetooth detector, themed watch, stopwatch and locksport timer.

## StopWatch features

- Radar, signal tracking, watch lists and local detection history.
- Logo watch faces, custom themes and animated locksport timers.
- Touchscreen, yellow/blue buttons, vibration and the RX8130CE real-time clock.
- Capture sessions, notebook exports, radio tools and BLE Lab.
- Background scanning pauses while using the clock or timers.

## Installation and clock setup

**M5Stack StopWatch C152 only.** Use the complete ESP32-S3 factory BIN at **0x0** for its **16 MB flash**. A factory installation replaces saved settings and files. For a compatible existing installation, choose StopWatch C152 and **Update matching Dragon Detector** in the [web flasher](https://valleytech-dragon-detector.pages.dev/#install).

Connect a USB data cable. Hold the power/reset button for about two seconds until the green LED lights, then release to enter download mode. Leave the buttons untouched during flashing and verification. After flashing, briefly press the button to restart. If it stays blank, close the serial connection, unplug USB, double-press power to turn it off, wait five seconds, then press power once. Reconnect USB after the logo appears.

Close M5Burner's serial connection and connect **Detector tools** in the web flasher to set and verify the time, date and timezone. M5Burner does not set the clock. On the StopWatch, **Settings > Time** provides separate Time, Date and Sync tabs. [Clock setup guide](https://valleytech-dragon-detector.pages.dev/guides/CLOCK-SETUP.html).

## On the StopWatch

![Dragon Detector running on M5Stack StopWatch C152](https://valleytech-dragon-detector.pages.dev/assets/stopwatch-clock-01320.png)

Detection identifies radio signatures, not intent or ownership. Radar position represents signal strength, not direction. Use active radio tools only with devices and networks you are authorized to test.

[Source and releases](https://git.churchofmalware.org/Valleytech/Dragon-Detector) · [Attributions](https://valleytech-dragon-detector.pages.dev/guides/CREDITS.html)"}

⚠️ 重要：StickS3 的 Type-C 口不对外供电（VBUS 只进不出），USB Host 模式直插目标板是没有电的！请使用带 5V 注入的 OTG 转接线（或供电 USB Hub），或目标板独立供电；走 UART 兜底接线（Hat2 排针）则无此限制。


AirSerial 把 StickS3 变成 WiFi 无线串口桥，远程烧录/调试 ESP32/ESP8266：


● 双路线：USB Host 直插目标板 USB 串口（CH34x/CP210x/FTDI/CDC-ACM，克隆 CH340 除外），或 UART 杜邦线兜底

● esptool 标准握手：rfc2217://<设备IP>:3334，自动复位进下载模式免按键

● Web Portal：配网、USB Host 开关、状态监控、WebSocket 终端

● 透明 TCP（3333）+ RFC2217（3334）双端口，pyserial 直接当本地串口用

● LCD 状态屏 + 意外重启原因上报（WDT/panic 分类）


首次使用：烧录后开 http://192.168.4.1/ 配网，设备即切到 STA 模式上线。

文档与源码：https://github.com/zyntraio/AirSerial

已知边界见 README：无 OTA;UART 接线路线 esptool 需 --before no-reset-no-sync。

"}

{"format":"html","content":"

## 更新内容


esptool默认握手在RFC2217/UART路线上正式打通——不再需要 --before no-reset-no-sync 绕参。已端到端验证：chip-id、1MB read-flash（85.9kbit/s）、write-flash+哈希校验，全部零参数通过。


修复三个根因：

- DTR/RTS曾交叉映射——现按esptool标准约定：RTS=GPIO3→EN、DTR=GPIO6→IO0（接线见README的UART接线表）

- UART RX凑包bug——每个小包被延迟约100ms，恰好顶死esptool的0.1s SYNC窗口（35/35全败）；RX改为事件驱动，延迟<1ms

- 改波特率时崩溃+回包丢失——set_params不再中途拆UART驱动（修复spinlock panic和SYNC回包丢失）


其他：

- DTR/RTS改为开漏输出，探测时误夹GND不再持续短路

- StickS3走USB Host模式需自供电OTG方案（Type-C口不对外供电）

- panic遗言hook在IDF 6.0.3验证可用

"}

{"format":"html","content":"

- 网页串口终端全面修复：解决一直\"连接中\"、随机掉线、重复点击连不上的问题

- 支持电脑与手机同时使用网页界面

- 网页终端与 RFC2217 端口新增 !airsn 本地命令

  （status / stats / set baud / usbhost / restart）

{"format":"markdown","content":"**仅适用于 M5Stack Cardputer ADV，中文界面。**

观象是一部掌心里的「卦意字典」：离线三币六爻、古今卦意阅读与循序自学，在近黑与暖金的界面中，起一卦，也学一卦。

- **三币六爻**：每爻两次 Enter，六爻由下而上形成，从本卦读到动爻与之卦。
- **三档阅读**：短意抓住线索，古文保留完整句子，精意讲清卦势、义理、处事与辨误；本卦／之卦卦意页按 T 切换。
- **逐爻精意**：覆盖 384 爻及用九、用六。爻辞、小象、精意分节分页，按 Enter 顺读至之卦。
- **六十四卦自学**：首页按 L，先学 12 课基础与八卦助记，再动手选择上下卦、浏览 64 卦目录。40px 大字卦名、六爻图与上下卦同屏呈现。
- **离线使用**：无需 Wi-Fi 或 microSD；最近 12 条历史保存在本机，起卦节奏、音效与减少动态可设置。

**文本与出处**
经传原文、古注节选与观象今释分别标明。今释依据王弼注、孔颖达疏《周易正义》等古典材料，由项目借助 AI 编写并复核；所据出处可查。所收古文包括卦辞、大象、爻辞、小象及相关用辞，并非全本《易传》。
[文本出处](https://github.com/Lyzbn/GuanXiang-Firmware/blob/main/TEXT_SOURCES.md) · [安装、使用及许可](https://github.com/Lyzbn/GuanXiang-Firmware)

此处提供完整合并固件，烧录会重置原有历史和设置。已有观象用户如需保留数据，请按 [GitHub 安装与兼容升级说明](https://github.com/Lyzbn/GuanXiang-Firmware/blob/main/INSTALL.md) 操作。

firmwares.firmwareDescription:
{"format":"markdown","content":"## Dash-Chan — your tiny wardriving companion

**Official M5Stack StackChan K151 only. Public beta.** Eight original companions, Avatar Studio, offline personality, passive Wi-Fi/BLE awareness and GPS-tagged WiGLE CSV logging to microSD.

**These instructions describe 0.8.1-beta. Check the selected firmware version: earlier releases remain available, and new submissions may be awaiting M5Stack review.** Version 0.8.0 requires `upload.json`; 0.7.x and earlier do not support Wardrift. The web installer provides the current release.

### Installation — read before burning

**The M5Burner BIN is a factory-reset image at 0x0. It overwrites NVS, including saved preferences and factory servo calibration.** Back up your own robot and restore its NVS before enabling head motion. Speech and motion default OFF on a fresh installation. The SD card is not formatted.

For updates that preserve calibration, use the **[web flasher and Avatar Studio](https://valleytech-dash-chan.pages.dev/)**. Follow the [backup and recovery instructions](https://valleytech-dash-chan.pages.dev/guide/docs/M5BURNER.html) before using the merged image.

### Meet your copilot

- Eight original buddies, layered outfits, custom colors and eyes; all cosmetics available immediately.
- Full Face or Recon + Buddy view, contextual phrases, quiet petting, level/XP, an SD lifetime notebook, and food earned through saved wardrives.
- Receiver/port/baud settings for original Unit GPS, GPS SMA/AT6668 and DIY ATGM336H. [GPS wiring and settings](https://valleytech-dash-chan.pages.dev/guide/docs/GPS.html).
- Steady, Gentle, Lively or Motors off head modes, mute controls, and distinct camera/drone clue reactions.
- Manual uploads, Upload all and optional uploads after Stop + Save to WiGLE, WDGWars and Wardrift, using the SD-card configuration below.

## SD card setup: step by step

1. **Check the firmware version.** Use **0.8.1-beta or newer** for the filename `config.json`. Version 0.8.0 uses the same schema-2 contents but requires the old name `upload.json`. Earlier versions do not support Wardrift. If installing from M5Burner, check the selected version; a submitted update may still be awaiting review. Follow the [installation guide](https://valleytech-dash-chan.pages.dev/guide/docs/FLASHING.html) or [M5Burner calibration/backup guide](https://valleytech-dash-chan.pages.dev/guide/docs/M5BURNER.html) when updating.
2. **Gather your credentials.** Use your home **2.4 GHz Wi-Fi SSID and password**. For WiGLE, obtain the **API name and API token** from [your account](https://wigle.net/account), not your login password. For WDGWars, obtain the **64-character hexadecimal API key** from [your profile](https://wdgwars.pl/profile). For Wardrift, create a **device API key** in [your Wardrift account](https://wardrift.net). Only obtain credentials for services you plan to enable. Keep them out of chat, screenshots and public repositories.
3. **Stop and save any drive, wait for uploads to finish, then power off Dash-Chan.** Remove the microSD card and insert it into your computer. Do not format it. Existing logs and pet progress should stay on the card.
4. **Open the SD card's root folder and create `dashchan` if it does not already exist.** Inside it, create `config.json`. The complete device path must be `/dashchan/config.json`, not `/config.json` or `/dashchan/dashchan/config.json`.
5. **Copy the template below into a plain-text editor**, or download [config.example.json](https://valleytech-dash-chan.pages.dev/config.example.json) and rename it to `config.json`. Enter your Wi-Fi credentials. Change a destination from `false` to `true` and fill its credential fields to enable it. **Enable at least one destination**; the blank template is deliberately unconfigured. You may enable all three. Unused credential strings can stay empty.
6. **Save as UTF-8 JSON.** On Windows, choose **Save as type: All files** and the exact filename `config.json`. Enable **View → Show → File name extensions** in File Explorer to ensure it is not `config.json.txt`. Keep the double quotes, commas, braces and unquoted `true`/`false`; JSON does not allow comments or trailing commas. If a password contains a double quote or backslash, escape it as `\"` or `\\`, or use the optional web setup form to generate the file safely.
7. **Safely eject the card, reinsert it, and power on Dash-Chan.** Open **Menu → Upload drives → Refresh**. The enabled destinations should appear. A missing/invalid-configuration message means you should check the filename, folder, JSON syntax and enabled service credentials.
8. **Test one saved drive while within range of your home Wi-Fi.** In **Menu → Upload drives**, select a drive with the arrows, tap **Send selected**, review the destination list, then tap again to confirm. Wait for the result and check that service's account. No networks are uploaded merely by saving the configuration or pressing Refresh.
9. **Send the backlog when ready.** Tap **Upload all (N)**, review the destination list, then **Confirm all (N)**. Confirmed destinations are skipped on later attempts; original CSV files remain on SD. See the full upload guide linked below if an outcome is uncertain.
10. **Choose automatic behavior explicitly.** Set `automatic` to `true`, save the file and Refresh to attempt each new nonempty drive after **Stop + Save**. Keep it `false` for manual uploads only. Automatic mode tries at that moment: it does **not** wait for your arrival home, upload an old backlog at boot, or retry failed sends. If home Wi-Fi was unavailable when you stopped, use **Send selected** or **Upload all** when you get home.

```json
{
  "schema": 2,
  "ssid": "YOUR_2.4_GHZ_WIFI_NAME",
  "password": "YOUR_WIFI_PASSWORD",
  "wigle": false,
  "wigleName": "",
  "wigleToken": "",
  "wdg": false,
  "wdgKey": "",
  "wardrift": false,
  "wardriftToken": "",
  "automatic": false,
  "donate": false
}
```

| Setting | Enter or choose |
| --- | --- |
| `ssid`, `password` | Your 2.4 GHz home Wi-Fi name and password. An empty password is allowed for an open network. Enterprise login and captive portals are unsupported. |
| `wigle`, `wigleName`, `wigleToken` | Set `wigle` to `true` and enter the WiGLE API name and token. |
| `wdg`, `wdgKey` | Set `wdg` to `true` and enter the 64-character hexadecimal WDGWars API key. |
| `wardrift`, `wardriftToken` | Set `wardrift` to `true` and enter the Wardrift device API key. |
| `automatic` | `false` for manual control; `true` for a single attempt after each Stop + Save. |
| `donate` | Optional WiGLE commercial-use donation, off by default. This does not enable uploads by itself. |
| `schema` | Leave at `2`. Keep every field in the template, even for disabled destinations. |


### Old configs, recovery and privacy

Existing `/dashchan/upload.json` files still work in 0.8.1+. You may rename one to `config.json`. If both exist, `config.json` takes precedence; an invalid new file does not silently use the old one. The website's form is optional and produces this same SD-card file.

Keep configuration files private: they contain readable Wi-Fi passwords and API keys. To disable uploads and remove credentials, stop activity and power off; remove `config.json`, `config-new.json`, `config-backup.json`, `upload.json`, `upload-new.json` and `upload-backup.json` from `/dashchan/` if present. Reinsert/restart and Refresh. Keep `/wardrives/` and upload receipts intact. Removing only the main file can restore a recovery copy.

Uploads pause scanning and resume it afterward. Accepted receipts prevent blind duplicate submissions; uncertain outcomes require checking the service account first. **[Full upload guide, troubleshooting and receipts](https://valleytech-dash-chan.pages.dev/guide/docs/UPLOADS.html)** · **[GitHub setup guide](https://github.com/valleytechsolutions/Dash-Chan/blob/main/docs/UPLOADS.md)**.

### On the robot

![Recon and buddy](https://valleytech-dash-chan.pages.dev/assets/ui-recon.png)

![GPS settings](https://valleytech-dash-chan.pages.dev/assets/ui-gps-setup.png)

![Upload destinations — synthetic setup](https://valleytech-dash-chan.pages.dev/assets/ui-upload-all.png)

### Validation and limits

The 0.8.1 configuration change passes host tests for new/legacy names, precedence, backup recovery and write failures. The preceding 0.8.0 build was checked on K151: GPS SMA on black B had a valid fix with both radios active, and a short stationary drive saved 115 validated CSV rows. That does not prove moving-car coverage or endurance. Factory-reset installation through M5Burner and live uploads with real service accounts remain unverified beta checks. Transport acceptance does not guarantee service-side processing or credit.

Native radio coverage is passive 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi and BLE. Detection signatures/OUI matches are clues, not proof of device identity, recording or intent. No 5 GHz, Bluetooth Classic, jamming, deauthentication or payload recording.

The merged image is assembled from clean release parts; no device backup, user credentials or recorded observations are included. [Download bundle with source, checksums and notices](https://valleytech-dash-chan.pages.dev/firmware/Dash-Chan.zip) · [Corresponding source archive](https://valleytech-dash-chan.pages.dev/source.zip) · [Quickstart](https://valleytech-dash-chan.pages.dev/guide/docs/QUICKSTART.html) · [Credits and licenses](https://valleytech-dash-chan.pages.dev/guide/docs/SOURCES.html).

GPL-3.0-or-later with retained dependency notices. Thanks to Dragon Detector, SquachWatch/skizzophrenic, Colonel Panic, Midwest Gadgets/Piglet, JustCallMeKoko, M5Stack, Espressif, NimBLE, TinyGPSPlus, OpenDroneID and the credited researchers. Original Dash-Chan companions; BWM/VTS marks belong to their owners. No upstream endorsement is implied."}

{"format":"markdown","content":"## 0.7.2-beta — Field Friends and configurable GPS

**Official M5Stack StackChan K151 only. Beta firmware.** Eight original companions, Avatar Studio, offline personality, passive Wi-Fi/BLE awareness, and GPS-tagged WiGLE CSV logging to microSD.

### What's new since 0.6

- Kits the fox, Ripple the axolotl and Byte the beetle join Mochi, Sprout, Orbit, Wisp and Ember. Eight shapes, eight eye styles, headwear, eyewear, neckwear and custom colors; all outfits available immediately.
- GPS presets for Unit GPS v1.1, GPS SMA / AT6668, older Unit GPS, and ATGM336H-5N/6N. Choose the Grove port or supported custom RX pin, select baud, or find the receiver's current baud automatically.
- GPS diagnostics separate valid serial data, signals seen, satellites used and a usable position fix. Receiver antenna reports are shown when available. A connected antenna does not guarantee reception.
- SD-backed lifetime notebook for unique Wi-Fi networks successfully saved during drives. Full Face and Recon + Buddy views, contextual captions, eight affection phrases, desktop scanning modes, configurable lights, quiet petting and master mute remain included.

### Installation — read before burning

**This M5Burner BIN is a factory-reset image at 0x0. It overwrites NVS, including saved preferences and factory servo calibration.** Back up your own robot and restore its NVS before enabling head motion. Speech and motion default OFF on a fresh installation. The SD card is not formatted.

For updates that preserve calibration, use the **[web flasher and Avatar Studio](https://valleytech-dash-chan.pages.dev/)**. [Backup and recovery guide](https://valleytech-dash-chan.pages.dev/guide/docs/M5BURNER.html) · [GPS setup](https://valleytech-dash-chan.pages.dev/guide/docs/GPS.html).

### On the robot

![Recon and buddy](https://valleytech-dash-chan.pages.dev/assets/ui-recon.png)

![GPS module, port and baud settings](https://valleytech-dash-chan.pages.dev/assets/ui-gps-setup.png)

### Validation and limits

0.7.2 is installed on the development K151. Build, host/parser regressions, WiGLE CSV round trips, avatar/web tests, and image checks pass. GPS serial reception and settings were checked with Unit GPS v1.1 and GPS SMA. The current outdoor comparison has not obtained a position fix; this does not establish a successful wardrive. Factory-reset installation through M5Burner is not physically tested.

The merged BIN embeds the exact four published 0.7.2 release images, with every gap verified erased. No personal device backup, credentials, settings or observations are included. The SHA-256 is provided with the source release.

Detection signatures and OUI matches are clues, not proof of identity, police presence, recording or intent. Native radio coverage is passive 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi and BLE. No 5 GHz, Bluetooth Classic, jamming, deauthentication or payload recording. WiGLE uploads require valid GPS data and user configuration.
